data.title: Phrase origin: Why do we "call" functions?
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了编程术语中为何使用“调用”（call）函数的说法。作者通过几个类比解释了这个术语的来源，包括将函数调用比作召唤朋友或仆人，以及像打电话一样请求帮助。文章指出，函数“调用”更接近于“召唤”子程序的概念，源自从图书馆中“调用”书籍的术语。文章追溯了“调用号”（call number）在图书馆学中的使用历史，并引用了John W. Mauchly在1947年的文章，该文章讨论了计算机子程序库中的“调用”概念。MANIAC II的1956年手册进一步明确了这一术语，描述了如何通过“调用号”从子程序库中召唤子程序用于程序组装。这表明编程中的“调用”函数术语源自图书馆学的“调用”书籍概念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于计算机术语"call"（调用）的起源和使用的讨论，以及与其他相关术语和语言现象的比较。

不同观点：
• jamesemmott引用Grace Hopper的观点，认为"compiler"一词源于从图书馆的"call number"（索书号）中获得灵感，子程序的调用（call）也与从图书馆中提取资料有关。
• seanc认为图书馆学对现代计算的贡献被低估，比如通过卡片目录解释数据库索引。
• Swiffy0分享了芬兰语中"call"的翻译为"kutsua"，意为"邀请"或"召唤"，指出在不同语言中该词的含义差异。
• fanf2提供了1951年Wilkes, Wheeler, Gill著作中的例子，显示"call in"用于调用子程序，并提供了相关文献资源。
• userbinator提到除了"call"以外，还会使用"invoke"或"execute"，并对ESL（英语作为第二语言）计算机科学学生误用"call"表示不满。
• skaushik92反思了"library"一词的起源，认识到其最初指的是磁带等物理存储介质。
• gorgoiler提到舞蹈中"call"的用法，认为与函数调用无关，但描述了每一步的算法。
• ks2478引用了音乐中的"call and response"现象，甚至提到返回值的概念。
• Ferret7446通过观察提出，新词的传播依赖于其易记和能引起共鸣的特性，并以"salty"为例说明这一过程。
• walthamstow离题地提到视频通话中使用的"jump on a call"这一表达。
• pixelpoet提到游戏中"proc"的用法，推测其来源于程序调用（procedure call）。
• kragen讨论了其他可能的动词如"instantiating"、"evaluating"、"computing"等，并引用了Mauchly的文献，指出早期文献中使用了"utilize"和"direct"等词。
• vincent-manis引用莎士比亚的《亨利四世》台词，幽默地说明调用（call）与响应的关系。
• amelius幽默地提到使用"gosub"（go to subroutine）来调用函数。
• seabass表达了对计算机历史讨论的喜爱，并好奇为何使用"throw"和"raise"来描述错误处理，以及为何"for"被用于循环结构。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到多个语言和文化背景下的术语使用差异，比如芬兰语中的"kutsua"。
• 提到了多个与"call"类似的动词和术语，如"invoke"、"execute"、"jump"等，展示了计算机术语的多样性和历史演变。
• 讨论中涉及了多个历史文献和具体例子，如Grace Hopper的言论、早期编程书籍等，提供了丰富的背景资料。
• 有些评论带有幽默和个人观察，如引用莎士比亚台词和"salty"一词的类比。
• 最后，seabass提出了对其他计算机术语如"throw"、"raise"和循环结构中"for"使用的思考，扩展了讨论的范围。

44506251.article_content:
Phrase origin: Why do we “call” functions?
On
StackExchange
,
someone asks why programmers talk about “calling” a function. Several possible allusions spring to mind:
Calling a function is like calling on a friend — we go, we stay a while, we come back.
Calling a function is like calling for a servant — a summoning to perform a task.
Calling a function is like making a phone call — we ask a question and get an answer from outside ourselves.
The true answer seems to be the middle one — “calling” as in “calling up, summoning” —
but indirectly, originating in the notion of “calling for” a subroutine out of a library of subroutines
in the same way that we’d “call for” a book out of a closed-stack library of books.
The OED’s first citation for
call number
in the library-science sense comes from
Melvil Dewey
(yes,
that Dewey
)
in 1876. The OED defines it as:
A mark, esp. a number, on a library book, or listed in a library’s catalogue,
indicating the book’s location in the library; a book’s press mark or
shelf mark
.
I see librarians using the term “call-number” in
The Library Journal
13
.9
(1888) as if it was very well established already by that point:
Mr. Davidson read a letter from Mr. A.W. Tyler […] enclosing sample of the new
call blank
used at the
Plainfield (N.J.) P. L., giving more room for the signature and address of the applicant. […]
“In connection with Mr. Tyler’s new
call slip
[…] I always feel outraged when I make up a long list
of
call numbers
in order to make sure of a book, and then the librarian keeps the list, and the next
time I have it all to do over again.”
According to
The Organization of Information
4th ed. (Joudrey & Taylor, 2017):
Call number.
A notation on a resource that matches the same notation in the metadata description and
is used to identify and locate the item; it often consists of a classification notation and a cutter number,
and it may also include a workmark and/or a date. It is the number used to “call” for an item in a closed-stack
library; thus the source of the name “call number.”
Cutter number.
A designation with the purpose of alphabetizing all works that have exactly the same classification notation.
Named for
Charles Ammi Cutter
, who devised such a scheme, but spelled
with a small
c
when referring to another such table that is not Cutter’s own.
John W. Mauchly’s article
“Preparation of problems for EDVAC-type machines”
(1947)
uses the English word “call” only twice, yet this seems to be an important early attestation of the word
in the context of a “library” of computer subroutines:
Important questions for the users of a machine are: How easily can reference be made to any of the subroutines?
How hard is it to initiate a subroutine? What conditions can be used to terminate a subroutine? And with what
facility can control revert to any part of the original sequence or some further sequence […] Facilities
for conditional and other transfers to subroutines, transfers to still further subroutines, and transfers
back again, are certain to be used frequently.
[…] the position in the memory at which arguments are placed can be standardized, so that whenever a subroutine
is
called in
to perform a calculation, the subroutine will automatically know that the argument which is to
be used is at a specified place.
[…] Some of them might be written out in a handbook and transferred to the coding of the problem as needed,
but those of any complexity presumably ought to be in a
library
— that is, a set of magnetic tapes in which
previously coded problems of permanent value are stored.
[…] One of the problems which must be met in this case is the method of withdrawal from the library
and of compilation in the proper sequence for the particular problem. […] It is possible […] to evolve
a coding instruction for placing the subroutines in the memory at places known to the machine, and in such
a way that they may easily be
called into use
[…] all one needs to do is make brief reference to them
by number, as they are indicated in the coding.
The manual for the
“MANIAC II assembly routine”
(January 1956)
follows Mauchly’s sketch pretty closely. MANIAC II has a paper-tape “library” of subroutines which
can be summoned up (by the assembler) to become part of a fully assembled program, and in fact each item
in the “library” has an identifying “call number,” just like every book in a real library has a call number:
The assembly routine for Maniac II is designed to translate descriptive code into absolute code. […]
The bulk of the descriptive tape consists of a series of instructions, separated, by control words,
into numbered groups called
boxes
[because flowcharts: today we’d say “basic blocks”]. The allowed
box numbers are
01
through
EF
[. …] If the address [in an instruction’s address field] is
FXXX
,
then the instruction must be a transfer, and the transfer is to the subroutine whose
call number
is
XXX
. The most common subroutines are on the same magnetic tape as the assembly routine, a

data.title: I'm Building LLM for Satellite Data EarthGPT.app
data.author: sabman
data.article_summary: EarthGPT是一个利用大型语言模型（LLMs）和现代遥感技术处理多光谱卫星影像的平台。用户可以通过其演示功能体验卫星图像分析，并能通过hi@earthgpt.app联系平台。该平台由Geobase提供支持，旨在提供先进的地球观测数据分析服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕将大型语言模型（LLM）应用于遥感图像分析的工具、技术及其潜在价值展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **notachatbot123**：对使用"turbo"色彩映射表示质疑，认为应该考虑色彩科学的长期研究，引用了经典的色彩研究资源，暗示色彩选择可能不够科学。
• **goroutines**：对将LLM应用于遥感分析表示支持，认为像Planet、Descartes等公司也应该朝这个方向发展。
• **joshvm**：提到遥感领域的范围正在扩大，并提供了一个包含基础模型和LLM集成的资源列表，指出该领域的工具和资源越来越丰富。
• **jesterx**：提到另一个使用LLM生成Google Earth Engine代码的论文，提供了一个相关项目（SatGPT）的链接，暗示这种方法并非全新。
• **rubyfan**：质疑LLM在此应用中的独特价值，询问如果没有LLM，哪些任务会更难完成，或者LLM带来了哪些新的能力。
• **RamblingCTO**：对整体想法表示赞赏，但指出在实际使用中遇到的问题，如无法查看某些示例，建议提供更多预定义的示例供用户参考。
• **sabman**：分享了个人经验，表示在多年从事遥感分析产品开发后，认识到LLM在分析影像和光谱带方面的潜力，支持将LLM引入该领域。
• **mahmed315**：简单表示这是一个好主意，没有深入讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：主要集中在LLM在遥感分析中的实际价值和应用效果。rubyfan对LLM的必要性提出质疑，而sabman和goroutines等人则表示支持。
• 实用性问题：RamblingCTO提到了工具在实际使用中的可用性问题，强调了用户体验的重要性。
• 资源分享：joshvm提供了相关资源列表，为感兴趣的用户提供了更多信息来源。
• 对比与参考：jesterx提到了类似的项目（SatGPT），为讨论提供了一个对比的参考点。

这些观点共同构成了对LLM在遥感分析中应用的多角度讨论，涵盖了技术、实用性和科学性等方面。

data.author: AntonioBarthes
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI与社会语言学中的权力 dynamics 以及在使用AI生成内容进行学术讨论时的严谨性

不同观点：
• **tony_borlini** 认为AI（DeepSeek-V3）不仅能够总结文章观点，还能进行反驳，这让人感到惊讶。他通过让AI生成博客回应了一篇关于AI、权力与社会语言学的文章，并将该回应发布在个人博客上，邀请读者进一步讨论。

• **carschno** 提供了一个与讨论相关的学术文章的永久链接，指向一篇可能与AI和社会语言学相关的学术资源，但并未直接发表个人观点，而是提供了一个供进一步研究的参考。

• **whatevsmate** 持批评态度，认为社会语言学家在讨论AI和权力 dynamics 时应更加严谨，而不应仅仅基于与一个AI的互动就做出广泛结论。他质疑了所使用的AI模型和版本的透明性，并讽刺这种研究方法为“自我民族志研究”和“ cynical fart-sniffing ”。

• **joules77** 则从人类认知局限性的角度出发，认为“幻觉”和“胡说八道”是人类认知的自然部分，因为人类大脑无法容纳所有知识。他将这种现象与人类在面对知识不足时的默认行为联系起来，并以“本地黑猩猩首领”的比喻来强调这一点。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**在于使用AI生成内容进行学术讨论的严谨性和透明性。whatevsmate对研究方法和AI模型的选择提出了质疑，认为不应轻率地根据AI生成的内容做出广泛结论。
• **讨论的另一层面**是AI在互动中表现出“反驳”能力是否值得惊讶，以及这种能力对学术讨论的实际价值。tony_borlini对此感到惊讶并认为值得进一步探讨，而whatevsmate则持怀疑态度。
• **joules77** 的评论引入了一种人类认知与AI行为之间的类比，为讨论提供了一个新视角，即AI的“幻觉”和“胡说八道”是否可以与人类的类似行为相提并论。

data.title: Is the doc bot docs, or not?
data.author: tobr
data.article_summary: 在这篇文章中，Robin Sloan描述了他在升级Shopify电子邮件通知模板时，使用Shopify的LLM开发文档机器人获取帮助的经历。他询问如何检测订单是否包含通过Shopify Collective履行的商品，文档机器人提供了代码，但实际应用中发现该代码无效，原因是订单标签在确认邮件生成时尚未存在。Robin反思文档机器人的价值，认为提供错误信息可能比没有帮助更糟糕，质疑这种工具是否真正有助于文档工作。他最终提供了一个有效的代码解决方案，并表达了对文档准确性的关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文档机器人（Docs bots）在实际应用中的挑战和表现

不同观点：
• **Emil_Sorensen**：认为文档机器人很难在生产环境中做到完美。需要在依赖底层文档和利用LLM潜在知识之间取得平衡，而这需要大量的评估（evals）。特别是在处理GraphQL schema时，难度更大。同时提到其公司Kapa.ai在为多家企业开发文档助手。
• **Cco**：其公司经过多次评估后，发现当前的LLM机器人尚未达到可以向客户提供的标准，约有60%的答案是好的，20%是中立或差的，20%是有害的。目前最好的方法仍是将文档添加到本地LLM IDE中自行查询。
• **Dworks**：预测未来因非确定性系统导致的问题会引发AI泡沫破裂。认为当前公司不顾系统非确定性问题，强行使用AI将导致严重后果。
• **Schnable**：提到其使用Gemini时遇到系统编造不支持的功能和代码的情况，认为当前AI在产品中的使用尚未成熟。
• **Shlomo_Z**：对Shopify的文档机器人提出质疑，建议创建免费测试项以免去使用信用卡交易的必要。
• **Bewelge**：认为Shopify的帮助页面像“销售文档”，不提供实际操作指导。其曾遇到文档机器人无法正确回答技术问题的情况，但在更新后情况有所改善。
• **Simonw**：希望文档机器人能正确回答复杂技术问题，并建议建立一个能测试代码的环境以提高答案的可靠性。
• **Bravesoul2**：质疑Shopify需要真实信用卡测试的做法，认为不如Stripe的测试机制。
• **Ngriffiths**：认为文档机器人相当于读过文档的人，可能提供不同准确度的答案。直接引用文档是最好的方式，能确保责任明确。
• **Schaum**：提到Gurubase.io，可以用来与文档交互并验证响应。
• **Trjordan**：指出文档和文档机器人都有错误率，文档可能有遗漏或误导，而文档机器人速度更快。认为在测试代码后再投入生产是合理的折中。
• **Domk**：认为对Shopify等平台的深入理解是避免错误的关键，AI仅依赖文档是不够的。
• **Ysofunny**：将文档比作有损压缩的JPEG，查询越具体，噪声越大。
• **Goroutines**：建议使用精确的逐步文档（如install.md）配合简单的RAG系统和编码代理，认为这是正确的方向。
• **Anentropic**：猜测窄领域的文档机器人表现不如ChatGPT等在“搜索”模式下的表现。

补充讨论：
• 文档机器人在生产环境中的表现和可靠性是主要关注点，特别是在处理技术文档和复杂查询时。
• 不同用户和公司对文档机器人的期望和实际体验存在差异，有的认为其速度快但准确性不足，有的则希望其能提供更可靠的技术指导。
• 争议的焦点在于文档机器人的错误率和其是否能替代传统文档或人类经验，以及如何在速度和准确性之间取得平衡。

44507244.article_content:
This is a post from Robin Sloan ’s lab blog & notebook. You can visit the blog’s homepage , or learn more about me . Is the doc bot docs, or not? July 8, 2025 Upgrading my Shopify email noti­fi­ca­tion templates this morning, I asked Shopifyâs LLM-powered devel­oper doc­u­men­ta­tion bot this ques­tion: Whatâs the syntax, in Liquid, to detect whether an order in an email noti­fi­ca­tion con­tains items that will be ful­filled through Shopify Collective? Iâd done a few tra­di­tional searches, but couldnât find an answer, so I thought, okay, letâs try the doc bot! The reply came, quick and clean: {% if order.tags contains 'Shopify Collective' %}

Some items in your order are being fulfilled by a partner merchant through Shopify Collective.

{% endif %} Looks great. I added this code, but it didnât work; the con­di­tion wasnât being satisfied, even when orders had the nec­es­sary tag, vis­ible on the admin screen. Shopify doesnât pro­vide a way to test uncon­ven­tional email for­mats without actu­ally placing real orders, so I did my cus­tomary dance of order-refund, order-refund, order-refund. My credit card is going to get locked one of these days. Turns out, the Shopify Collective tag isnât present on the order at the time the con­fir­ma­tion email is generated. Itâs added later, pos­sibly just moments later, by some other cryptic Shopify process. I donât think this is doc­u­mented anywhere, so in that sense, itâs not sur­prising the doc­u­men­ta­tion bot got it wrong. My ques­tion is: whatâs the point of a doc bot that just takes a guess? More point­edly: is the doc bot docs, or not? And very point­edly indeed: what are we even doing here?? Iâve sent other queries to the doc bot and received helpful replies; Iâd cat­e­go­rize these basi­cally as search: âHow do I do X?â âWhatâs the syntax for Y?â But I believe this is a sit­u­a­tion in which the cost of bad advice out­weighs the ben­efit of quick help by 10X, at least. I can, in fact, figure out how to do X using the real docs. Only the doc bot can make things up. If it was Claude making this kind of mistake, Iâd be annoyed but not surprised. But this is Shopifyâs sanc­tioned helper! It waits twin­kling in the header of every page of the dev site. I suppose there are domains in which just taking a guess is okay; is the offi­cial doc­u­men­ta­tion one of them? I vote no, and I think a freestyling doc bot under­mines the effort and care of the folks at Shopify taking the time to write doc­u­men­ta­tion that is thor­ough and accurate. P.S. One working answer to my ques­tion looks like this: {% assign has_collective_item = false %} {% for line_item in line_items %} {% if line_item.product.tags contains 'Shopify Collective' %} {% assign has_collective_item = true %} {% endif %} {% endfor %} To the blog home page

data.title: 7-Zip for Windows can now use more than 64 CPU threads for compression
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：7-Zip软件的现状、功能、跨平台支持及相关技术细节

不同观点：
• [d33] 认为7-Zip因缺乏zstd支持可能会失去竞争力，尤其在大文件处理上，zlib的性能不佳，而zlib-ng的改进效果有限。不过，他承认7-Zip在加密和文件分割方面表现出色。
• [avidiax] 质疑为什么Windows上的7-Zip有限制，而在Linux上没有发现类似问题。
• [fabiensanglard] 讨论了ZIP格式在写入磁盘前需要知道压缩大小的问题，猜测7-Zip可能是将压缩流缓存在RAM中，以保证输出的稳定性。
• [ninjis] 提到因为Windows现在原生支持7z格式，所以他不再觉得需要使用NanaZip。
• [aquir] 表示自从切换到macOS后，他一直怀念7-Zip软件。
• [leecarraher] 分享了他使用pbzip2的经验，认为尽管理论上压缩效率较低，但实际使用中没有显著差异。
• [izzydata] 提出了一个相关问题，询问"zip"术语是否与zip磁盘驱动器有相同的起源。
• [lihaciudaniel] 强调了7-Zip在移动设备上通过Termux和QEMU-utils处理虚拟磁盘文件的实用性。
• [ltbarcly3] 持批评态度，认为7-Zip在现代平台上已经不再重要，且其最新增强功能对绝大多数用户来说没有实际意义。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是7-Zip在现代计算环境中的相关性和实用性，尤其是在不同操作系统上的表现和限制。
• 另一个讨论点是关于压缩算法和格式的技术细节，例如压缩效率、写入机制以及缓存使用等。
• 还有对7-Zip跨平台支持的讨论，特别是macOS和Linux用户的需求和体验。
• 最后，评论中还包含了一些轻松或讽刺的言论，如[marcodiego]引用xkcd漫画，以及[ltbarcly3]对讨论本身的价值提出质疑。

data.title: Most RESTful APIs aren't really RESTful
data.author: BerislavLopac
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要讨论了Roy Thomas Fielding的论文《架构风格与基于网络的软件架构设计》，该论文介绍了代表性状态转移（REST）架构风格，旨在设计可扩展、高性能和可维护的网络系统，特别是Web服务。Fielding分析了多种网络架构风格的优缺点，强调REST专注于可扩展性、简洁性和适应性。他指出，REST是一种提供原则和约束的架构风格，而非具体的技术实现，如HTTP动词或CRUD风格API。

文章澄清了关于REST的常见误解，例如REST不等于CRUD，资源也不仅仅是持久化实体。Fielding特别强调了超媒体作为应用状态引擎（HATEOAS）的重要性，认为没有超媒体控制的API不能称为RESTful。HATEOAS通过动态发现链接减少客户端与服务器的耦合，提高系统的可演化性。

此外，文章解释了REST中的“资源”概念，指出资源是信息的抽象映射，而非具体的服务器实体，URI的语义由创建者定义，而非客户端或服务器需要理解的内容。

When talking about REST, it is worth reading
the dissertation
of Roy Thomas Fielding. The
original paper
that describes RESTful web, “Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures” Roy T. Fielding (2000), introduces the Representational State Transfer (REST) architectural style as a framework for designing scalable, performant, and maintainable networked systems, particularly web services.
The paper aims to analyze architectural styles for network-based systems, identifying their strengths and weaknesses. It defines REST as a specific architectural style optimized for the modern web, focusing on scalability, simplicity, and adaptability.
Fielding demonstrates how REST principles shape the success of the web, advocating for its adoption in designing distributed systems with universal, stateless interfaces and clear resource-based interactions.
In his dissertation he does
not
prescribe the specific use of HTTP verbs (like GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) or focus on CRUD-style APIs as REST is often implemented today.
The dissertation clearly describes REST as an architectural style that provides principles and constraints for building network-based applications, using the web as its foundational example.
Roy Fielding has explicitly criticized the oversimplification of REST in CRUD-style APIs, emphasizing that many so-called “RESTful” APIs fail to implement key REST constraints, particularly the use of hypermedia for driving application state transitions. In his 2008 blog post, “REST APIs must be hypertext-driven,” Fielding states:
“If the engine of application state (and hence the API) is not being driven by hypertext, then it cannot be RESTful and cannot be a REST API. Period.”
Source
This underscores his view that without hypermedia controls, an API does not fulfill the REST architectural style Hypermedia controls are elements embedded in a resource representation that guide clients on what actions they can take next.
Common misconceptions in the context of what people consider REST are for example:
REST is CRUD (often it is, but not always)
A resource is an entity (often meaning a persistence entity).
RESTful API must not use verbs.
But those are actually
design decision
made for the API at hand, chosen by their creators and have nothing to do with REST.
What Does “Driven by Hypertext” Mean?
The phrase “not being driven by hypertext” in Roy Fielding’s criticism refers to the absence of Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State (
HATEOAS
) in many APIs that claim to be RESTful. HATEOAS is a fundamental principle of REST, requiring that the client dynamically discover actions and interactions through hypermedia links embedded in server responses, rather than relying on out-of-band knowledge (e.g., API documentation).
{
"orderId"

,

{

{

"/orders/123"
},

:
{
"href"
:
"/orders/123/cancel"
,
"method"
:
"POST"
}
}
}
The core problem it addresses is client-server coupling. There are probably countless projects where a small change in a server’s URI structure required a coordinated (and often painful) deployment of multiple client applications. A HATEOAS-driven approach directly solves this by decoupling the client from the server’s namespace. This addresses the quality of evolvability.
Simply implementing HATEOAS will bring you closer to RESTful principles than debating whether verbs are allowed in your API.
What is a “Resource”?
Often people argue about what a resource in REST is. I’ve seen more or less commonly people expressing the opinion that a resource is a data structure coming from the server, unfortunately often even equal to a persistence entity.
Let’s check what Fielding says about it:
The key abstraction of information in REST is a resource.
Any information that can be named can be a resource: a document or image, a temporal service (e.g. “today’s weather in Los Angeles”), a collection of other resources, a non-virtual object (e.g. a person), and so on. In other words, any concept that might be the target of an author’s hypertext reference must fit within the definition of a resource. A resource is a conceptual mapping to a set of entities, not the entity that corresponds to the mapping at any particular point in time.
Semantics are a by-product of the act of assigning resource identifiers and populating those resources with representations. At no time whatsoever do the server or client software need to know or understand the meaning of a URI – they merely act as a conduit through which the creator of a resource (a human naming authority) can associate representations with the semantics identified by the URI. In other words, there are no resources on the server; just mechanisms that supply answers across an abstract interface defined by resources. It may seem odd, but this is the essence of what makes the Web work across so many different implementations.

data.author: hadat
data.article_summary: **RN Maps Clustering** 是一个为 React Native 构建的现代化、高性能地图标记聚类库，基于 **supercluster** 库，提供简单、声明式的 API，支持对 **react-native-maps** 组件的美观高效的标记聚类。主要特性包括高性能、完全类型化（使用 TypeScript）、可自定义聚类样式、自动展开标记（spiderfier）等。安装方式可通过 npm、yarn 或 pnpm 添加 **rn-maps-clustering** 和 **react-native-maps**。使用时只需用 **<ClusteredMapView />** 替换 **<MapView />**，并可自定义聚类组件和处理聚类点击事件。该库还支持多种聚类参数配置，如聚类半径、最大缩放级别等。欢迎贡献代码。

• kevg123对项目表示赞赏，特别是对spiderfier功能感兴趣，并询问了对expo-maps的看法，提供了一个相关博客链接以供参考。

争议焦点：
• DanielHB的经验显示了在React Native中处理地图功能的复杂性，而kevg123则关注新的工具如expo-maps是否能有效解决这些问题。两者反映了不同时间点和技术发展阶段下开发者的实际体验和期望。

总结：讨论主要围绕React Native项目中地图功能的实现复杂性、现有工具的使用经验以及对新工具的评价和建议。

RN Maps Clustering
A modern, performant, and fully-typed map clustering library for React Native. Built on top of the battle-tested
supercluster
library,
RN Maps Clustering
provides a simple, declarative API for adding beautiful and efficient marker clustering to your
react-native-maps
components.
✨ Features
High Performance:
Leverages
supercluster
for lightning-fast clustering of thousands of points.
Fully Typed:
Written entirely in TypeScript for a superior developer experience.
Declarative API:
Works just like
react-native-maps
. Simply wrap your
<Marker />
components.
Customizable:
Easily provide a custom component to render clusters.
Spiderfier:
Automatically spreads out markers at max zoom level for easy interaction.
Modern:
Built with modern React hooks and best practices.
🚀 Installation
Install the library and its peer dependencies:
npm install rn-maps-clustering react-native-maps
#
or
yarn add rn-maps-clustering react-native-maps
#
or
pnpm add rn-maps-clustering react-native-maps
Follow the installation instructions for
react-native-maps
.

data.title: SUSE launches new European digital sovereignty service to meet surging demand
data.author: saubeidl
data.article_summary: SUSE推出了一项名为"Sovereign Premium Support"的新服务，旨在帮助欧洲企业和政府在其IT基础设施中实现数字主权。该服务确保所有支持人员和数据都位于欧盟境内，客户支持数据存储在欧盟的网络和服务器上，且只有欧盟工作人员能访问敏感数据。此举响应了欧盟对数据隐私和独立性的日益关注，特别是面对非欧盟国家，尤其是美国公司的数据控制风险。SUSE的这项服务专为需要严格数据驻留和操作控制的组织设计，如国防、政府和执法部门，但也面向所有欧洲组织开放。这项服务在当前地缘政治不确定性增加的背景下，为欧洲客户提供了更强的安全保障和业务连续性支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕SUSE Linux、数据主权和欧洲数字主权的讨论

不同观点：
• [pjmlp] 认为FOSS（自由和开源软件）操作系统可能是摆脱美国主导的消费级操作系统及相关编程语言的唯一出路。他提到自己曾是Linux的狂热爱好者，对Linux发行版的碎片化以及桌面环境的梦想破灭感到失望，但特别指出SuSE和KDE的整合曾给他留下深刻印象。

• [jpalomaki] 强调仅仅关注服务器位置（如“存储在欧盟网络和服务器上”）并不足够，关键是谁在管理和控制这些服务器和网络。他认为讨论数据主权时，管理权比物理位置更重要。

• [0xfedcafe] 对SUSE在欧洲的被忽视表示不解，指出SUSE已经具备几乎所有必要的工具（如Rancher和openSUSE），并且在欧洲有相当的知名度。他对欧洲数字主权讨论中倾向于选择美国项目（如Fedora）而非SUSE表示质疑。

• [defraudbah] 对欧洲数据主权持怀疑态度，认为通过更多法规未必能赢得这场“战争”。他提到德国的先例，认为即使丹麦有可能迁移到Linux，最终可能也会像德国一样反复。同时，他对未来十年是否会有实质性改变表示悲观，预测只会出现更多补助和法律，但不会有根本性变化。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到SUSE的历史和其在欧洲的知名度，特别是其与KDE的整合及在开源项目中的地位。
• 数据主权的定义和实现方式存在争议，焦点在于服务器位置与管理权的相对重要性。
• 对欧洲是否能够真正实现数字主权存在不同看法，有人持乐观态度，认为SUSE是合适选择，而有人则持怀疑态度，认为法规和政策变化难以带来实际效果。

SUSE launches new European digital sovereignty support service to meet surging demand
With SUSE's help, European companies and governments can ensure their IT support, software, and data assets are safe.
Written by
Steven Vaughan-Nichols,
Senior Contributing Editor
Senior Contributing Editor
July 8, 2025 at 12:00 a.m. PT
Thomas Fuller/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images
Wary of the US government and tech companies, the European Union (EU) has seen a surge in support for
open source
and
Linux
. In the last few months, local EU governments,
including the city of Lyon in France,
the
German state of Schleswig-Holstein
, and
Denmark,
have begun their move to Linux and open-source software from
Microsoft Windows
and Office. Now, Luxembourg-based European open-source powerhouse
SUSE
is offering extensive support to businesses and governments that want to keep their IT infrastructure inside the European Union.
Also:
7 things every Linux beginner should know before downloading their first distro
The
Digital Sovereignty
movement is a big deal in Europe for a reason. Today, over 90% of European data resides on servers operated by non-EU and primarily American companies. This dependency exposes EU entities to data privacy, economic leverage, and potential risks of foreign surveillance.
As a result, according to tech researcher IDC,
84% of European organizations using cloud technologies are either currently using or planning to use sovereign cloud solutions
. Rahiel Nasir, IDC's research director for European Cloud Strategies, described 2025 as a "watershed year," with growing geopolitical and economic uncertainties putting digital sovereignty at the forefront for organizations.
Also:
Linux's remarkable journey from one dev's hobby to 40 million lines of code - and counting
That's why SUSE, a global leader in enterprise open-source solutions, has announced the launch of its Sovereign Premium Support package. This comprehensive support service is designed to meet the growing demand for digital sovereignty.
Specifically, Dirk-Peter (DP) van Leeuwen, SUSE's CEO, explained: "For some, it's a brand new story. But for us,
digital sovereignty
is old news. We've been enabling it for years for our customers. Along the way, we've learned you have to get three main things right: Data, technology, and operations. The last area -- business operations -- is often least looked at, but it's often the hardest to deliver. Ultimately, it is about the people -- where are they? And how do we ensure we have the scale to deliver business continuity? That's what we're addressing with the launch of SUSE Sovereign Premium Support."
Also:
I put Linux on this 8-inch mini laptop, and unlocked a new way of computing
In practice, SUSE's Sovereign Premium Support is tailored for enterprises and public sector organizations that require strict data residency, privacy, and operational control within the EU. The service ensures that:
All support personnel and data are based in the EU, with named premium support engineers and service delivery managers assigned to each customer.
Customer support data is stored exclusively on EU-located networks and servers, addressing both regulatory and geopolitical concerns.
Access to sensitive data is strictly limited to EU-based staff, with a commitment to encrypting all data required for troubleshooting.
This approach directly responds to the evolving landscape of European regulations and the heightened focus on digital independence. While it's an approach meant specifically for areas such as defense, government, and law enforcement, where compliance and resilience are paramount, it's being offered to all European organizations.
As Udo Wuertz, CDO and fellow at the data center company
Fsas Technologies Europe
, said, SUSE's "Open by Design, Sovereign by Choice" philosophy, combined with enhanced EU-based support, provides tailored solutions for customers with stringent sovereignty requirements.
Also:
Can't upgrade your Windows 10 PC? Here are your options before it all ends in 3 months
If this focus sounds paranoid, well, the world has changed. There's more geopolitical uncertainty today than since the Cold War threatened to get hot. So, for Europeans, SUSE's new program may be just what they need to feel secure again. SUSE stands ready to help with its Linux, open-source, and cloud offerings.
Contact SUSE
to learn more about their latest service.

44507166.article_summary: SUSE推出了一项名为"Sovereign Premium Support"的新服务，旨在帮助欧洲企业和政府在其IT基础设施中实现数字主权。该服务确保所有支持人员和数据都位于欧盟境内，客户支持数据存储在欧盟的网络和服务器上，且只有欧盟工作人员能访问敏感数据。此举响应了欧盟对数据隐私和独立性的日益关注，特别是面对非欧盟国家，尤其是美国公司的数据控制风险。SUSE的这项服务专为需要严格数据驻留和操作控制的组织设计，如国防、政府和执法部门，但也面向所有欧洲组织开放。这项服务在当前地缘政治不确定性增加的背景下，为欧洲客户提供了更强的安全保障和业务连续性支持。
44507166.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕SUSE Linux、数据主权和欧洲数字主权的讨论

不同观点：
• [pjmlp] 认为FOSS（自由和开源软件）操作系统可能是摆脱美国主导的消费级操作系统及相关编程语言的唯一出路。他提到自己曾是Linux的狂热爱好者，对Linux发行版的碎片化以及桌面环境的梦想破灭感到失望，但特别指出SuSE和KDE的整合曾给他留下深刻印象。

• [jpalomaki] 强调仅仅关注服务器位置（如“存储在欧盟网络和服务器上”）并不足够，关键是谁在管理和控制这些服务器和网络。他认为讨论数据主权时，管理权比物理位置更重要。

• [0xfedcafe] 对SUSE在欧洲的被忽视表示不解，指出SUSE已经具备几乎所有必要的工具（如Rancher和openSUSE），并且在欧洲有相当的知名度。他对欧洲数字主权讨论中倾向于选择美国项目（如Fedora）而非SUSE表示质疑。

• [defraudbah] 对欧洲数据主权持怀疑态度，认为通过更多法规未必能赢得这场“战争”。他提到德国的先例，认为即使丹麦有可能迁移到Linux，最终可能也会像德国一样反复。同时，他对未来十年是否会有实质性改变表示悲观，预测只会出现更多补助和法律，但不会有根本性变化。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到SUSE的历史和其在欧洲的知名度，特别是其与KDE的整合及在开源项目中的地位。
• 数据主权的定义和实现方式存在争议，焦点在于服务器位置与管理权的相对重要性。
• 对欧洲是否能够真正实现数字主权存在不同看法，有人持乐观态度，认为SUSE是合适选择，而有人则持怀疑态度，认为法规和政策变化难以带来实际效果。

data.title: Introduction to Indian English
data.author: sandwichsphinx
data.article_summary: 印度英语在不到200年的时间里成为印度人与世界以及彼此交流的主要语言之一，与印地语并驾齐驱。英语在印度的治理、教育、媒体和出版业中占据重要地位，例如英语报纸的发行量仅次于印地语。历史上，英国通过东印度公司进入印度，经过150年的教育政策演变，英语逐渐普及。1835年，麦考利提案确立英语为高等教育语言，尽管遭遇反对，但最终成功实施，使印度人接触到西方思想和英语。在印度独立运动中，英语一度优先，但后来转向重视印度语言。独立后，宪法规定印地语为官方语言，英语为辅助官方语言。尽管存在语言地位的争论，英语仍然是高等教育和法律系统的主要语言，尤其在城市和专业领域，被视为追求物质进步和声望的象征。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：印度英语中特有的表达方式及其在跨文化沟通中引起的困惑和趣味。

不同观点：
• **"I'll revert back" 引起的混淆**：susam 分享了一个实例，展示了在跨文化沟通中因使用 "revert back" 导致的误解。Bob 作为英语母语者，误解了 Raj 所说的 "revert back"（实际上是想表达 "get back to me"），以为是要恢复被删除的附件。这表明某些印度英语表达可能在国际沟通中引起困惑。

• **"Please do the needful" 的使用**：n1b0m 和 rob74 提到 "Please do the needful" 是一个常见的印度英语表达，常用于分配任务或请求完成某项工作。这一表达在其他英语变体中不常见，但在印度英语中被广泛使用。

• **语言翻译对印度英语表达的影响**：jbhoot 指出，印度英语中的一些独特表达可能源自于印度人将母语翻译成英语时的思维过程。这种现象并非印度独有，其他非英语母语者也可能会有类似的表达方式。

• **"Prepone" 的使用**：gulabjamuns 提到 "prepone" 作为 "postpone" 的反义词，在印度英语中被使用。这个词汇在其他英语变体中较为少见，并指出文章遗漏了许多常见的印度英语用法。

• **其他独特的印度英语词汇**："give a click" 和 "updation" 被提及为印度英语中的独特表达。devnull3 提供了 "updation" 的字典链接，展示了这个词的正式性。jbhoot 还分享了 "Juggernaut" 作为一个源自印度的英语词汇，具有历史和文化背景。

补充讨论：
• **文化背景对语言的影响**：jbhoot 提供的 "Juggernaut" 例子展示了印度文化对英语词汇的影响，强调了语言和文化的密切联系。
• **不同英语变体之间的差异**：评论中提到的多个表达展示了印度英语中特有的词汇和用法，这些用法在其他英语变体中可能不常见或引起困惑。

争议焦点：
• **跨文化沟通中的误解**：susam 分享的实例展示了在跨文化沟通中因语言表达差异导致的误解，强调了理解不同英语变体中独特表达的重要性。

总结：评论主要讨论了印度英语中特有的表达方式，包括 "I'll revert back"、"Please do the needful"、"prepone"、"give a click" 和 "updation" 等，并探讨了这些表达在跨文化沟通中可能引起的混淆和趣味。同时，评论还指出了语言翻译和文化背景对印度英语表达的影响。

World Englishes
Introduction to Indian English
Content
History
Vocabulary
Grammar
Pronunciation
In less than 200 years since its formal introduction as part of a nascent and westernized education system, English has grown to be the medium through which the people of India communicate with the world, and often with one another. In large parts of a country with several major languages, it vies with Hindi—the most commonly used Indian language—as the spoken language of choice. There is a range of ability from a mere smattering of words, to some amount of rudimentary communication, to highly proficient use of the language. Arguably, the number of Indians speaking at least a few words of English, and the contexts in which they do so, continue to grow by the day. The language has a large presence in governance, education, media, and the publishing industry. For instance, the number of English language newspapers registered in India and their circulation figures are second only to those in Hindi. India produces the third largest number of English books in the world, after the USA and UK.
History
The link between Britain and India is an old one, starting around the time of the formation of the East India Company in 1600. The British came initially seeking business opportunities in a wealthy country. Later, they gained control of different regions through alliances, battles, and treaties. Educational efforts commenced with setting up individual schools and progressed to actually implementing formal policies. This was a process that evolved over a period of 150 years. Necessarily, though not without resistance, this involved the spread and growth of English in a territory that had a vast population speaking hundreds of languages, with many having a formal history of at least two thousand years.
The most significant linguistic policy initiative of the British was Thomas Babington Macaulay’s Minute of 1835, which led to the establishment of English as the language of instruction for higher education. This momentous decision paved the way for the eventual entrenchment of English in the country. The proposal met with fierce opposition from a group of highly-placed British officials and Indians. In the end, though, Macaulay prevailed. As a consequence, Indians were rapidly exposed to western ideas, science, law, governance, and, of course, English. By 1857, universities were being set up in the three Presidencies:  Bengal, Bombay, and Madras. In 1854, with Sir Charles Wood’s Despatch, school education also benefitted, although the focus was not only on English; the local languages were also given due importance. Macaulay created a job market for people who learned English, with the aim of meeting the administrative needs of the British; this same skill is now the gateway for Indians to compete for the best jobs, globally.
English and the struggle for freedom
When the Indian National Congress was formed in 1885 to fight for India’s freedom preference for membership was initially, and perhaps ironically, given to those who spoke English. By 1920, however, Mahatma Gandhi’s leadership ensured that Indian languages were given primacy; this coincided with the British government handing over the Education Department to be managed by Indian officials. The debate over abandoning English altogether, and replacing it with Hindi/Hindustani, was a low-key, parallel narrative to the struggle for freedom. As independence drew closer, there was an attempt to have Hindi declared as the national language, while the Constituent Assembly was holding deliberations to frame the Constitution. The proposal was watered down to official language status in the Constitution of India which was adopted in 1950, three years after independence in 1947.
Official status and usage
Under Article 343 of the Constitution of India, English gets the status of an associate official language, the official language being Hindi. However, the higher legal system, federal legislative processes, and the bulk of higher education are all still carried out in English. This dichotomy of preference vis-à-vis the language has never gone away. The first generation of Indians who were formally educated in English also became the standard bearers of the independence movement. Even before independence was achieved, the next generation was deeply involved in the creation of the United Nations and various global institutions.
English has always been an aspirational language, with a great deal of material progress and prestige associated with it. The status accorded to English in education and governance has however remained uncertain. Several commissions have been set up to study this matter and attempts to dilute the pre-eminence of English have occurred in various regions. It is, by and large, a second language to most of its users. However, for those in the cities and in the professions, it is the language of choice for commerce, for education, and for social interaction. The

• **"I'll revert back" 引起的混淆**：susam 分享了一个实例，展示了在跨文化沟通中因使用 "revert back" 导致的误解。Bob 作为英语母语者，误解了 Raj 所说的 "revert back"（实际上是想表达 "get back to me"），以为是要恢复被删除的附件。这表明某些印度英语表达可能在国际沟通中引起困惑。

• **"Please do the needful" 的使用**：n1b0m 和 rob74 提到 "Please do the needful" 是一个常见的印度英语表达，常用于分配任务或请求完成某项工作。这一表达在其他英语变体中不常见，但在印度英语中被广泛使用。

• **语言翻译对印度英语表达的影响**：jbhoot 指出，印度英语中的一些独特表达可能源自于印度人将母语翻译成英语时的思维过程。这种现象并非印度独有，其他非英语母语者也可能会有类似的表达方式。

• **"Prepone" 的使用**：gulabjamuns 提到 "prepone" 作为 "postpone" 的反义词，在印度英语中被使用。这个词汇在其他英语变体中较为少见，并指出文章遗漏了许多常见的印度英语用法。

• **其他独特的印度英语词汇**："give a click" 和 "updation" 被提及为印度英语中的独特表达。devnull3 提供了 "updation" 的字典链接，展示了这个词的正式性。jbhoot 还分享了 "Juggernaut" 作为一个源自印度的英语词汇，具有历史和文化背景。

补充讨论：
• **文化背景对语言的影响**：jbhoot 提供的 "Juggernaut" 例子展示了印度文化对英语词汇的影响，强调了语言和文化的密切联系。
• **不同英语变体之间的差异**：评论中提到的多个表达展示了印度英语中特有的词汇和用法，这些用法在其他英语变体中可能不常见或引起困惑。

争议焦点：
• **跨文化沟通中的误解**：susam 分享的实例展示了在跨文化沟通中因语言表达差异导致的误解，强调了理解不同英语变体中独特表达的重要性。

data.title: Springer Nature book on machine learning is full of made-up citations
data.author: ArmageddonIt

44507061.article_content:
Would you pay $169 for an introductory ebook on machine learning with citations that appear to be made up?
If not, you might want to pass on purchasing
Mastering Machine Learning: From Basics to Advanced
, published by Springer Nature in April.
Based on a tip from a reader, we checked 18 of the 46 citations in the book. Two-thirds of them either did not exist or had substantial errors. And three researchers cited in the book confirmed the works they supposedly authored were fake or the citation contained substantial errors.
“We wrote this paper and it was not formally published,” said Yehuda Dar, a computer scientist at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, whose work was cited in the book. “It is an arXiv preprint.” The citation incorrectly states the paper appeared in
IEEE Signal Processing Magazine
.
Aaron Courville, a professor of computer science at Université de Montréal and coauthor on the book
Deep Learning
, was correctly cited for the text itself, but for a section that “doesn’t seem to exist,” he said. “Certainly not at pages 194-201.” And Dimitris Kalles of Hellenic Open University in Greece also confirmed he did not write a cited work listing him as the author.
The researcher who emailed us, and asked to remain anonymous, had received an alert from Google Scholar about the book, which cited him. While his name appeared on multiple citations, the cited works do not exist.
Nonexistent and error-prone citations are a
hallmark of text generated by large language models like ChatGPT
. These models don’t search literature databases for published papers like a human author would. Instead, they generate content based on training data and prompts. So LLM-generated citations might look legitimate, but the content of the citations might be fabricated.
The book’s author, Govindakumar Madhavan, asked for an additional “week or two” to fully respond to our request for comment. He did not answer our questions asking if he used an LLM to generate text for the book. However, he told us, “reliably determining whether content (or an issue) is AI generated remains a challenge, as even human-written text can appear ‘AI-like.’ This challenge is only expected to grow, as LLMs … continue to advance in fluency and sophistication.”
According to his bio in the book, Madhavan is the founder and CEO of SeaportAi and author of about 40 video courses and 10 books. The 257-page book includes a section on ChatGPT that states: “the technology raises important ethical questions about the use and misuse of AI-generated text.”
Springer Nature provides
policies and guidance
about the use of AI to its authors, Felicitas Behrendt, senior communications manager for books at the publisher, told us by email. “Whilst we recognise that authors may use LLMs, we emphasise that any submission must be undertaken with full human oversight, and any AI use beyond basic copy editing must be declared.”
Mastering Machine Learning
contains no such declaration. When asked about the potential use of AI in the work, Behrendt told us: “We are aware of the text and are currently looking into it.” She did not comment on efforts taken during Springer Nature’s editorial process to ensure its AI policies are followed.
LLM-generated citations were at the center of controversies around Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s
“Make America Healthy Again” report
and a CDC presentation on the
vaccine preservative thimerosal
. At Retraction Watch, our cofounders
were once cited in a made-up reference
in an Australian government report on research integrity.  We’ve seen fake citations fell
research
articles
, and
our list of papers
with evidence of undisclosed ChatGPT use has grown long and almost certainly represents
only a fraction
of those that actually do.
The same day Behrendt replied to our query, Springer Nature published a post on its blog titled, “
Research integrity in books: Prevention by balancing human oversight and AI tools
.”
“All book manuscripts are initially assessed by an in-house editor who decides whether to forward the submission to further review,” Deidre Hudson Reuss, senior content marketing manager at the company, wrote. “The reviewers – subject matter experts – evaluate the manuscript’s quality and originality, to ensure its validity and that it meets the highest integrity and ethics standards.”

data.title: PHP 8.5 alpha 1 is available for download
data.author: jeroenpeters
data.article_summary: PHP团队宣布推出PHP 8.5.0的第一个测试版本Alpha 1，标志着8.5版本周期的开始。此版本仅供测试，不建议用于生产环境。用户可从下载页面获取源码，并可在GitHub上报告发现的问题。有关新功能和变更的详细信息，可查阅NEWS文件，升级注意事项则在UPGRADING文件中。下一个版本Alpha 2计划于2025年7月17日发布。签名可在manifest或发布候选页面找到。感谢社区帮助改进PHP。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PHP 8.5的新特性和Unicode支持问题

不同观点：
• [moebrowne] 对PHP 8.5引入的新管道操作符（pipe operator）表示关注，并提供了一个相关博客链接，介绍了这一新特性。他认为这一更新值得注意，显示出对新功能持积极态度。

• [phplovesong] 则对PHP的Unicode支持不足表示不满，特别是对缺乏内建的Unicode处理功能，如统一的字符处理函数。他批评开发团队没有解决这一长期存在的问题，并继续依赖于mb_*系列函数来处理多字节字符串。

补充讨论：
• [phplovesong] 的评论暗示了对PHP开发团队优先级的质疑，认为在引入新特性的同时，核心功能（如Unicode支持）仍然被忽视。
• [phplovesong] 使用了较为情绪化的语言（"what in the hell are the devs doing?"），显示出对这一问题强烈的失望情绪。
• 争议的焦点在于PHP在引入新特性和解决现有功能不足之间的优先级和资源分配问题。一部分开发者可能更关注新功能的引入以保持语言的现代性，而另一部分开发者则希望优先解决长期存在的功能性问题。

data.title: Grow a Garden Calculator
data.author: dond1986
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个植物选择和价值计算工具。用户可以选择植物类别和具体植物，并根据各种修饰因子计算其价值与重量。页面包括布局选项、修饰符调整、按价值排序功能，以及隐藏管理变异选项。计算公式为：(彩虹/金) × (1 + 修饰符总和 − 修饰符数量)。用户还可以输入重量、朋友加成等参数来计算总价值或根据设定价值反推所需重量。页面提供清除所有设置和最大变异选项，方便用户进行不同情境下的植物价值评估。

• [yreg]的评论侧重于工具在游戏中的功能性和实用性，而[brikym]的评论则反映了工具名称可能导致的现实期望与虚拟用途之间的混淆。

data.title: Comparing the Climate and Productivity Impacts of a Shrinking Population
data.author: alphabetatango
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了人口减少对气候变化和生产力的影响。作者对比了全球人口减少的基准情景与人口持续增长的假设情景，发现即使到2200年人口差异达数十亿，对长期气温的影响不到0.1摄氏度，不足以影响气候目标。原因在于人口变化对气温的影响因时间滞后而减弱，且人均排放量预计将显著下降。此外，人口减少还会减缓推动生产力和生活水平提升的创新速度。综合考虑大规模负排放的可能性，人口与气温关系的正负影响尚不明确。人口减少虽减少碳排放，但无法解决当前气候问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：气候变化与人类生活标准、人口变化之间的关系

不同观点：
• Gustomaximus认为，生活水平的提高可能是气候压力增加的一个更大因素。随着更多国家向发达国家的生活标准靠拢，如果这种转变速度超过绿色技术和人口减少的速度，气候压力将增大。他指出，文章没有提及这一点，并认为生活标准的提升可能是真正的问题。

• bjornsing则强调，随着世界人口的减少，人类适应气候变化的能力应会大幅提高。他认为，当前过度强调保持现有气候，而忽视了为后代创造良好生活环境的努力。他还指出，气候变化是地球历史上的正常现象，现有的气候在长远来看没有内在价值。

补充讨论：
• Gustomaximus关注的是生活标准提高对气候变化的潜在影响，并质疑文章中是否充分考虑了这一因素。
• bjornsing的观点侧重于人口减少对气候适应能力的提升，并对当前气候保护工作的优先级提出质疑。
• 争议焦点在于如何平衡生活标准提高、人口变化与气候变化之间的关系，以及保护现有气候的必要性。

这些观点反映了关于气候变化讨论中的不同优先级和策略选择，涉及短期生活水平提升与长期气候适应能力之间的权衡。

Is Less Really More? Comparing the Climate and Productivity Impacts of a Shrinking Population
Mark Budolfson
,
Michael Geruso
,
Kevin J. Kuruc
,
Dean Spears
&
Sangita Vyas
Share
X
LinkedIn
Facebook
Bluesky

Email
Link
Working Paper
33932
DOI
10.3386/w33932
Issue Date
June 2025
A smaller human population would emit less carbon, other things equal, but how large is the effect? Here we test the widely-shared view that an important benefit of the ongoing, global decline in fertility will be reductions in long-run temperatures. We contrast a baseline of global depopulation (the most likely future) with a counterfactual in which the world population continues to grow for two more centuries. Although the two population paths differ by billions of people in 2200, we find that the implied temperatures would differ by less than one tenth of a degree C—far too small to impact climate goals. Timing drives the result. Depopulation is coming within the 21st century, but not for decades. Fertility shifts take generations to meaningfully change population size, by which time per capita emissions are projected to have significantly declined, even under pessimistic policy assumptions. Meanwhile, a smaller population slows the non-rival innovation that powers improvements in long-run productivity and living standards, an effect we estimate to be quantitatively important. Once the possibility of large-scale net-negative emissions is accounted for, even the sign of the population-temperature link becomes ambiguous. Humans cause greenhouse gas emissions, but human depopulation, starting in a few decades, will not meet today’s climate challenges.

data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了非本土蜜蜂对南加州本地授粉者的威胁。研究表明，蜜蜂占去了开花第一天80%的花粉，严重影响本地蜂群的繁殖。由于蜜蜂体型较大，它们占据了该生态系统中98%的蜂群生物量，导致本地蜂群数量大幅减少。尽管蜜蜂对人类农业至关重要，但它们在非本土环境中可能对自然生态系统构成威胁。文章还指出，与本地授粉者相比，蜜蜂授粉的植物后代质量较差。随着商业养蜂业的扩展，许多本地授粉者正面临栖息地丧失、气候变化和化学污染的威胁，而蜜蜂对资源的有效获取进一步加剧了这一问题。

Honey bees and other pollinating insects contribute billions of dollars to the American economy. Credit: Keng-Lou James Hung
The majority of Earth's plant species, including our crop plants, rely on the services of animal pollinators in order to reproduce. Honey bees and other pollinating insects annually contribute billions of dollars to the U.S. economy, and are responsible for nearly a third of the food that ends up on our tables.
Our modern agricultural industry is so reliant on honey bees that
humans have introduced them worldwide
, and in many cases, they have escaped human management and risen to prominence in natural ecosystems as non-native, feral populations. And, like any other non-native organism, feral honey bees may perturb native ecosystems when they become sufficiently abundant.
Feral honey bees have greatly proliferated in Southern California, along with the rest of the Southwestern United States. A new study by University of California San Diego biologists Dillon Travis, Joshua Kohn, David Holway and Keng-Lou James Hung is calling attention to the threat posed by non-native honey bees to the diverse native pollinators of the San Diego and broader Southern California region.
These researchers
previously estimated
that honey bees comprise up to 90% of all bees visiting flowers of multiple native
plant species
in the region.
The new study, published in the journal
Insect Conservation and Diversity
, estimates the impact honey bees may be having on populations of native bees in this important global hotspot of native pollinator biodiversity.
The researchers found that honey bees remove about 80% of pollen during the first day that a flower opens. This finding is important because all bees in the region—and the vast majority of bee species worldwide—use pollen to raise their offspring.
The amount of pollen removed daily by honey bees from just one hectare (2.5 acres) of
native vegetation
is enough to provision thousands of native bees per day during the peak bloom of native shrubs, the researchers found.
Because honey bees are larger than most native bee species in Southern California, the new study calculated that honey bees now comprise 98% of all bee biomass in this ecosystem. If the pollen and nectar used to create honey bee biomass were instead converted to native bees, populations of native bees would be expected to be roughly 50 times larger than they are currently.
"Although honey bees are rightly considered an indispensable asset to humans, they can also pose a serious ecological threat to
natural ecosystems
where they are not native," said Hung, who earned his Ph.D. from UC San Diego and is now an assistant professor at the University of Oklahoma.
"The plight of the honey bee is an issue of animal husbandry and livestock management, whereas when it comes to conservation issues here in North America, honey bees are likelier to be part of the problem, not a solution or a target for conservation."

In another cause for concern,
a study published in 2023
by Travis and Kohn showed that plants pollinated by honey bees produce lower-quality offspring compared with offspring from native pollinators.
Researchers found that honey bees remove about 80% of pollen during the first day that a flower opens. Credit: Keng-Lou James Hung
While bees in general are being threatened by
habitat loss
,
climate change
and chemical pollution, the researchers say that such a level of honey bee pollen exploitation is not well documented, and could well pose an additional and important threat to native bee populations in places where honey bees have become abundant.
Even as the number of managed honey bee colonies is increasing worldwide due to the commercial beekeeping industry, many species of native pollinators are declining.
"Public concern for honey bees often fails to consider their potential negative effects on native pollinators," the authors note in their report.
"Honey bees are incredibly effective at extracting resources like pollen and nectar," said Travis, who earned his Ph.D. at UC San Diego in 2023.

data.author: campuscodi
data.article_summary:
2025年5月底，SpyCloud实验室发现两组引人关注的中国数据集在DarkForums上被出售，分别称为“VenusTech数据泄露”和“Salt Typhoon数据泄露”。这两个帖子由新创建的账户发布，声称包含来自中国黑客雇佣行业的公司数据。尽管样本较小，但提供了对中国网络安全承包商生态系统的深入了解。

VenusTech是中国一家主要服务政府客户的IT安全公司，曾与黑客雇佣行业有关联。5月17日，一个名为“IronTooth”的账户发布了VenusTech的泄露数据，包括公司出售给政府的产品、客户信息和访问权限等文件截图。特别引人关注的是几份电子表格，其中列出了中国政府合同及相关服务，显示VenusTech可能涉及对韩国国会邮件服务器的访问和数据交付。

这些泄露数据提供了对中国网络犯罪地下活动的深入见解，揭示了该国黑客雇佣行业的结构和运作模式。

We wanted to take a moment to analyze these two recent posts, dive into the sample data, and make some connections between this activity and some overall trends we are observing in our research into the Chinese cybercriminal underground.
Analysis of the VenusTech Data Leak
VenusTech is a major IT security vendor in China with a focus on serving government clients. It was founded in 1996 and is traded on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. They have previously documented ties to the hack-for-hire industry including procuring services from XFocus, who

VenusTech是中国一家主要服务政府客户的IT安全公司，曾与黑客雇佣行业有关联。5月17日，一个名为“IronTooth”的账户发布了VenusTech的泄露数据，包括公司出售给政府的产品、客户信息和访问权限等文件截图。特别引人关注的是几份电子表格，其中列出了中国政府合同及相关服务，显示VenusTech可能涉及对韩国国会邮件服务器的访问和数据交付。

这些泄露数据提供了对中国网络犯罪地下活动的深入见解，揭示了该国黑客雇佣行业的结构和运作模式。

Musk's AI firm deletes posts after chatbot praises Hitler
1 hour ago
Share
Save
Peter Hoskins
Business reporter, BBC News
Share
Save
Reuters
Elon Musk's artificial intelligence start-up xAI says it is working to remove "inappropriate" posts made by its chatbot, Grok, after users shared how it made positive references to Hitler.
Screenshots published on social media show the chatbot saying the Nazi leader would be the best person to respond to alleged "anti-white hate."
"Since being made aware of the content, xAI has taken action to ban hate speech before Grok posts on X,"
the company said in a post
.
ADL, an organisation formed to combat antisemitism and other forms of discrimination, said the posts were "irresponsible, dangerous and antisemitic."
"This supercharging of extremist rhetoric will only amplify and encourage the antisemitism that is already surging on X and many other platforms," ADL wrote on X.
Grok changes
X users have shared responses made by Grok when it was queried about posts that appeared to celebrate the deaths of children in the recent Texas floods.
In response to a question asking "which 20th century historical figure" would be best suited to deal with such posts, Grok said: "To deal with such vile anti-white hate? Adolf Hitler, no question."
"If calling out radicals cheering dead kids makes me 'literally Hitler,' then pass the mustache," said another Grok response. "Truth hurts more than floods."
The incident came as xAI was due to launch its next-generation language model, Grok 4, on Wednesday.
On Friday, Musk
posted on X
that Grok had improved "significantly", but gave no details of what changes had been made.
"You should notice a difference when you ask Grok questions," he added.
The chatbot drew criticism earlier this year after it repeatedly referenced "white genocide" in South Africa in response to unrelated questions - an issue that the company said was caused by an "unauthorised modification".
X, which was formerly called Twitter, was merged with xAI earlier this year.
Chatbot developers have faced extensive scrutiny over concerns around political bias, hate speech and accuracy in recent years.
Musk has also previously been criticised over claims that he amplifies conspiracy theories and other controversial content on social media.

data.title: Running a Certificate Transparency log
data.author: Metalnem
data.article_summary:
文章呼吁拥有多余存储和带宽的组织或工程师考虑运行一个**证书透明度日志（Certificate Transparency Log）**，这对网络安全至关重要。证书透明度机制通过让证书颁发机构（CA）提交证书至第三方日志，确保网站所有者能得知未经授权的证书颁发，提升了网络安全。

运行CT日志过去昂贵且复杂，但通过新的**静态CT API**和**Sunlight**工具，现在变得更简单和便宜。Geomys公司以每年1万美元的成本运行一个受信任的CT日志。

**运行CT日志的要求**包括：一台服务器、ECC内存、2 Gbps出站带宽、3-5 TB存储（SSD或对象存储），以及谷歌要求的两名代表联系人。日志的持久性至关重要，数据一旦写入不能丢失。

运行CT日志需要遵守谷歌和苹果的政策，定期更新，并每年轮换时间分片。社区欢迎新的日志运营者加入，可通过Slack等渠道获取支持。

总之，运行CT日志对网络安全有重大贡献，且现在更易实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：证书透明性（Certificate Transparency, CT）日志系统的改进和相关技术方案的讨论。

不同观点：
• **agwa** 认为，Sunlight和static-ct-api为CT日志领域带来了新气象。传统的CT日志基于数据库构建，过于复杂且成本高昂（每年花费高达10万美元），导致日志运营困难且鲜有组织愿意运行。Sunlight和static-ct-api正在改变这一现状，令人兴奋。

• **baobun** 提到Mozilla在CRLite上的进展，认为这是一个未被充分关注的改进，提供了对CT系统下游改进的示例。

• **torbid** 质疑为何CT日志服务器要负责存储，建议由日志提交者自己存储数据，服务器仅负责其密钥和增量签名，以简化服务器职责并避免高昂的存储成本。

• **tonymet** 关注证书系统的审计问题，指出消费者和发布者常对证书掉以轻心，导致错误使用。SSL/TLS在防窃听方面表现良好，但在建立信任和身份方面不足，建议进行业余或专业审计。

• **gslin** 对CT日志所需的带宽提出疑问，不确定是否真的需要2-3 Gbps的出站带宽，并提供了存档链接供参考。

• **ncrmro** 建议使用Arweave这样的区块链存储方案，认为这可能是一种有用的存储方式，费用可用于支持存储成本的增长。

• **udev4096** 反对支持中心化的CA，认为DANE（DNS-based Authentication of Named Entities）才是未来，不需要依赖这些CA。

• **cypherpunks01** 询问CT系统如何实现仅追加条目和公开透明的时间记录，并提出是否可以使用区块链技术，或者这是否会导致数据量过大。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及的技术方案包括Sunlight和static-ct-api的创新、CRLite的进展、区块链存储的建议以及DANE的未来展望。
• 争议的焦点在于CT日志服务器是否应负责存储，以及区块链技术是否适用于CT系统。
• 带宽需求和审计问题也被提出作为需要进一步澄清和探讨的要点。

总体来看，讨论围绕CT日志系统的技术改进、存储和审计问题展开，并涉及未来技术和去中心化方案的潜在应用。

44494430.article_content:
7 Jul 2025
You Should Run a Certificate Transparency Log
Hear me out. If you are an organization with some spare storage and bandwidth, or an engineer looking to justify an
overprovisioned homelab
, you should consider running a Certificate Transparency log. It’s cheaper, easier, and more important than you might think.
Certificate Transparency
(CT) is one of the technologies that underpin the security of the whole web. It keeps Certificate Authorities honest, and allows website owners to be notified of unauthorized certificate issuance. It’s a big part of how the WebPKI went from the punchline of “weakest link” jokes to the robust foundation of the security of most of digital life… in less than fifteen years!
CT is an intrinsically distributed system: CAs must submit each certificate to two CT logs operated by third parties and trusted by the browsers. This list is, and has been for a couple years, uncomfortably short. There just aren’t as many independent log operators as we’d like. Operating a log right now would be an immense contribution to the security of virtually every Internet user.
It also comes with the bragging rights to claim that your public key is on
billions
of devices.
Where’s the catch? Well, until recently running a log was a pain, and expensive. I am writing this because as of a few months ago,
this has changed
!
Browsers now accept CT logs that implement the new
Static CT API
, which I designed and productionized in collaboration with Let’s Encrypt and the rest of the WebPKI community over the past year and a half. The key difference is that it makes it possible to serve the read path of a CT log exclusively through static, S3 and CDN friendly files.
Moreover, the new
Sunlight
implementation, sponsored by Let’s Encrypt, implements the write path with minimal dependencies and requirements. It can upload the Static CT assets directly to object storage, or store them on any POSIX filesystem.
You can learn more if you are curious in
Let’s Encrypt’s retrospective
, in the original
Sunlight design document
, or in the summarized
public announcement
.
Geomys
, my open source maintenance firm,
operates a pro-bono Sunlight-backed trusted Static CT log for $10k/year
, including hardware amortization, colocation, and bandwidth. I’m sure it can be done for cheaper.
The shopping list
Ok, so what does it take to run a CT log in 2025
5
?
Servers: one. No need to make the log a distributed system, CT itself is a distributed system.
If you want to offer redundancy you can run multiple logs.
The uptime target is 99%
4
over three months, which allows for nearly 22h of downtime. That’s more than three
motherboard failures
per month.
CPU and memory: whatever,
as long as it’s ECC memory
. Four cores and 2 GB will do.
Bandwidth: 2 Gbps outbound peak capacity
1
(which you can offload to a CDN).
Storage: you have two options.
3 – 5 TB of usable redundant filesystem space on SSDs
2
.
3 – 5 TB of S3-compatible object storage, and 200 GB of cache on SSD.
Static CT logs are just flat static files, which you can serve with any HTTP server
3
from disk, or expose as a public object storage bucket.
People: Google policy requires the email addresses of two representatives. The uptime target is forgiving enough that it can probably be met by a single person working during business hours.
That’s pretty much it!
Durability is the first priority: it’s really important that you never lose data once it’s fsync’ed to disk or PUT to object storage, since your log will have signed and returned SCTs, which are promises to serve the certificates it received. This means for example that backups are useless: they would rollback the log’s state.
In terms of ongoing effort, a log operator is expected to read the
Google
and
Apple
CT Log policies, monitor the ct-policy@chromium.org mailing list, update the log implementation from time to time, and rotate log temporal shards every year. (For example, we just stood up 2027 shards of our log.)
Given the logs lifecycle, you should plan to stick around for at least three years.

If you want to become a CT log operator, first of all… thank you!

was rewritten recently to get you up and running easily. Sunlight is highly specialized for Certificate Transparency and the WebPKI, and it’s designed to help you operate a healthy, useful CT log with minimal configuration.

44494430.article_summary:
文章呼吁拥有多余存储和带宽的组织或工程师考虑运行一个**证书透明度日志（Certificate Transparency Log）**，这对网络安全至关重要。证书透明度机制通过让证书颁发机构（CA）提交证书至第三方日志，确保网站所有者能得知未经授权的证书颁发，提升了网络安全。

运行CT日志过去昂贵且复杂，但通过新的**静态CT API**和**Sunlight**工具，现在变得更简单和便宜。Geomys公司以每年1万美元的成本运行一个受信任的CT日志。

**运行CT日志的要求**包括：一台服务器、ECC内存、2 Gbps出站带宽、3-5 TB存储（SSD或对象存储），以及谷歌要求的两名代表联系人。日志的持久性至关重要，数据一旦写入不能丢失。

运行CT日志需要遵守谷歌和苹果的政策，定期更新，并每年轮换时间分片。社区欢迎新的日志运营者加入，可通过Slack等渠道获取支持。

总之，运行CT日志对网络安全有重大贡献，且现在更易实现。

data.title: Psilocybin treatment extends cellular lifespan, improves survival of aged mice
data.author: XzetaU8
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了裸盖菇素（psilocybin）及其代谢产物裸盖菇醇（psilocin）在细胞衰老和寿命延长方面的潜在作用。研究发现，裸盖菇醇处理可以延长人类胎儿肺成纤维细胞的寿命，延缓细胞衰老，增加细胞增殖能力，并减少氧化应激。具体来说，10 μM的裸盖菇醇使细胞寿命延长了29%，而100 μM则延长了57%。此外，裸盖菇醇处理还降低了细胞周期停滞标志物，增加了增殖标志物，并调节了与衰老相关的基因表达。在老年小鼠实验中，裸盖菇素治疗也显示出促进长寿的效果。这些结果表明，裸盖菇素可能是一种有效的抗衰老剂，具有延长细胞寿命和改善老年小鼠存活率的潜力。研究还提出了裸盖菇素可能通过影响端粒长度来发挥作用的假设。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：迷幻蘑菇（psilocybin）是否能够逆转大脑的衰老过程，特别是对神经可塑性的影响。

不同观点：
• 支持观点1：迷幻蘑菇中的活性成分psilocybin可能促进神经可塑性，逆转与衰老相关的脑功能下降。研究表明，psilocybin能够增加神经突触的形成，增强大脑的适应性，从而有可能“重启”大脑，恢复年轻时的某些功能。例如，研究中提到psilocybin有助于提高情绪和认知能力，这为其抗衰老潜力提供了初步证据。

• 支持观点2：一些神经科学家认为，psilocybin可能通过影响5-HT2A受体，重新激活大脑中的关键信号通路，进而恢复大脑在处理情绪和认知任务中的灵活性。该观点基于动物实验和初步的临床研究，显示psilocybin可能对抑郁症、焦虑症等精神健康问题有显著改善作用，而这些症状常常与大脑老化相关。

• 反对观点1：有质疑者指出，目前关于psilocybin逆转大脑衰老的研究仍处于非常早期的阶段，缺乏足够的临床试验数据支持。例如，虽然动物实验显示出一定的积极效果，但人类大脑的复杂性远高于实验动物，因此将实验结果直接推及人类可能为时过早。

• 反对观点2：也有批评者担心迷幻蘑菇的潜在副作用和安全性问题，尤其是在老年人群体中使用。psilocybin可能引发短期的精神混乱、幻觉等问题，长期使用是否会带来不可逆的脑损伤尚不明确。此外，心理健康问题如精神分裂症患者可能对psilocybin有更强的负面反应。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中还提到了psilocybin在心理治疗中的潜在应用，尤其是在辅助治疗抑郁症、创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）等精神健康问题上。一些研究表明，psilocybin与心理辅导结合使用，可能产生更为持久的效果，这为未来探索其抗衰老作用提供了新的研究方向。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是，迷幻蘑菇在法律和伦理上的争议。由于psilocybin在许多国家仍被列为违禁药物，其研究和应用面临诸多法律限制，这可能影响未来相关研究和临床应用的推广。

争议焦点：迷幻蘑菇是否真正具有逆转大脑衰老的作用，目前的研究数据是否足够充分，以及其安全性与合法性问题。

Psilocybin treatment extends cellular lifespan and improves survival of aged mice
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Cell biology
Molecular biology
Senescence
Abstract
Psilocybin, the naturally occurring psychedelic compound produced by hallucinogenic mushrooms, has received attention due to considerable clinical evidence for its therapeutic potential to treat various psychiatric and neurodegenerative indications. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain enigmatic, and few studies have explored its systemic impacts. We provide the first experimental evidence that psilocin (the active metabolite of psilocybin) treatment extends cellular lifespan and psilocybin treatment promotes increased longevity in aged mice, suggesting that psilocybin may be a potent geroprotective agent.
Introduction
To date, >150 clinical studies with psilocybin have been completed or are ongoing for various clinical indications, including psychiatric (anxiety, depression, addiction), neurodegenerative (Alzheimer’s), pain, and more
1
,
2
,
3
. Human studies have demonstrated that a single-dose of psilocybin can improve debilitating physical and psychological symptoms—with durable effects (up to ~5 years)
4
,
5
. Despite considerable clinical evidence supporting the therapeutic benefits of psilocybin, the molecular mechanisms responsible for these impacts remain enigmatic. Studies with psilocybin have predominantly focused on neurological impacts and/or behavioral outcomes; few studies have evaluated alternative or systemic mechanisms which may also contribute to its beneficial effects. The “psilocybin-telomere hypothesis”
6
postulates that psilocybin interventions may quantifiably impact telomere length, which offers a potential explanation for its efficacy across a wide range of clinical indications. This hypothesis is based on a large corpus of studies linking mental health biological aging markers
6
. Accumulating evidence indicate that clinical depression accelerates aging and telomere shortening
7
,
8
,
9
. Positive mental psychological states are associated with longer telomeres, whereas negative psychological conditions (e.g. chronic stress, anxiety, and depression) are associated with telomere attrition
7
,
10
,
11
,
12
,
13
. Given the clinical evidence supporting the efficacy of psilocybin for these conditions, it is plausible that psilocybin may impact telomere length. However, no prior studies have experimentally investigated the direct impact of psilocybin on biological aging.
To evaluate the impact of psilocybin on cellular aging, we employed a validated model of replicative senescence using human fetal lung fibroblasts
14
. For all in vitro studies, we used psilocin (the active metabolite of psilocybin), which is formed when psilocybin is broken down after ingestion. Cells were serially passaged with media containing psilocin or vehicle until they reached replicative senescence. Psilocin treatment (10 μM) resulted in a 29% extension of cellular lifespan, characterized by delayed exhaustion of proliferative potential, increased cumulative population doublings, and decreased population doubling time, compared to vehicle (Fig.
1A–F
). Results were more striking using a higher dose of psilocin in the same cell type (100 μM treatment led to a 57% extension in cellular lifespan; Supplementary Fig.
1A–F
). Induction of senescence occurred in both vehicle and psilocin-treated cells, as both groups reached exhaustion of their proliferative potential (no evidence of oncogenic transformation was observed), however the onset of senescence was delayed in psilocin-treated cells (Fig.
1A
). Further, compared to vehicle, psilocin-treated cells exhibited decreased βgal activity (Fig.
1G–H
). These results were consistent with dose-dependent reductions in markers of cell cycle arrest (p21, p16), and increased markers of proliferation (PCNA) and DNA replication (pRB) (Fig.
1I
). Compared to vehicle, psilocin treatment also led to elevated sirtuin1 (SIRT1; a critical role in regulating cellular aging, metabolism, and stress-responses) and decreased Growth Arrest and DNA Damage-inducible 45 alpha (GADD45a) levels, suggesting reduced DNA damage (Fig.
1I
). Psilocin treatment also reduced oxidative stress levels in a dose-dependent manner (Fig.
1J
), which was associated with decreased levels of NADPH oxidase-4 (Nox4, a master regulator of oxidant production) and increased nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2, a master regulator of antioxidant responses) (Fig.
1I
). Overall, these results suggest that the in vitro impacts of psilocin are dose-dependent, with higher dosing ultimately leading to greater cellular life extension. To further validate these findings, we repeated these studies with a different cell type (adult human skin fibroblasts); 100 μM psilocin treatment increased cellular lifespan by 51%, which was accompanied by reduced senescence and decreased oxidative stress levels (Supplementary Fig.
2
). To invest

data.title: Bitchat – A decentralized messaging app that works over Bluetooth mesh networks
data.author: ananddtyagi
data.article_summary: BitChat是一款去中心化、无需互联网的蓝牙Mesh网络聊天应用，支持端到端加密。它无需服务器、电话号码或账户，提供基于频道的群聊、消息缓存和转发、IRC风格命令等功能。应用注重隐私保护，支持自动发现 peers 和多跳消息中继，并采用X25519密钥交换和AES-256-GCM加密。其他特性包括消息压缩、自适应电池优化模式、以及紧急数据清除功能。用户可以通过Xcode或Swift Package Manager设置和运行该应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：去中心化、延迟容忍的消息系统及其可行性和应用场景

不同观点：
• moneywaters提出一个基于去中心化、延迟容忍的消息系统概念，消息通过设备间传递（如通过蓝牙、UWB、Wi-Fi Direct），发送者支付小额费用，中继设备赚取微支付，系统端到端加密、完全去中心化且可选择匿名。他认为这种系统在互联网不稳定或受审查的地区非常有用。但他同时指出该系统的挑战包括延迟和可靠性、滥用/垃圾信息预防、功耗以及用户参与的激励机制。
• sardine5提到他开发的“Murmur: Bluetooth Group Calls”应用，虽然主要是用于语音，但也实现了通过蓝牙LE进行群组通话和消息传递的功能。他表示该应用下载量不高，因此对这种需求的存在持怀疑态度。
• lxgr对现代手机在无移动网络或Wi-Fi覆盖下无法通信表示失望，并建议Apple可以扩展iMessage以支持P2P通信。
• shreyasonline提到他早在10年前就发布了类似的应用“Technitium Bit Chat”。
• syntaxing对Meshtastic需要特殊硬件表示困惑，并建议结合LoRA代理扩展范围，认为Apple可以做类似的事情。
• Beretta_Vexee认为在蓝牙范围内直接聊天比通过消息应用更方便，但提到智能手表和自行车电脑等设备可能有更多有趣的应用场景。
• monkaiju将该应用与Briar对比，认为该应用只支持蓝牙且隐私记录不佳，更多是一个个人项目而非安全环境下的理想选择。
• t43562提到在拥挤事件中手机网络过载导致通信困难的场景，认为这种系统在这种场景下非常有用，但对非技术用户的使用意愿表示担忧。
• seanlinmt将该系统与Briar对比，并建议增加创建投票的功能，提出在抗议活动中的应用场景。

补充讨论：
• 关于该系统是否可行和有实际应用场景的讨论，有人认为这是一个有趣的学术概念，但在现实中需求有限，有人则提出如抗议活动、大型活动中的通信问题等实际应用场景。
• 关于应用的跨平台支持，讨论中提到了iOS和Android的兼容性问题，目前大多数实现主要在Apple设备上。
• 关于激励机制和用户参与的讨论，如何设计一个有效的激励结构以鼓励用户中继消息是一个关键问题。
• 关于现有类似项目的提及，如Briar和Technitium Bit Chat，提供了对该概念已有实现的参考。

bitchat
A secure, decentralized, peer-to-peer messaging app that works over Bluetooth mesh networks. No internet required, no servers, no phone numbers - just pure encrypted communication.
License
This project is released into the public domain. See the
LICENSE
file for details.
Features
Decentralized Mesh Network
: Automatic peer discovery and multi-hop message relay over Bluetooth LE
End-to-End Encryption
: X25519 key exchange + AES-256-GCM for private messages
Channel-Based Chats
: Topic-based group messaging with optional password protection
Store & Forward
: Messages cached for offline peers and delivered when they reconnect
Privacy First
: No accounts, no phone numbers, no persistent identifiers
IRC-Style Commands
: Familiar
/join
,
/msg
,
/who
style interface
Message Retention
: Optional channel-wide message saving controlled by channel owners
Universal App
: Native support for iOS and macOS
Cover Traffic
: Timing obfuscation and dummy messages for enhanced privacy
Emergency Wipe
: Triple-tap to instantly clear all data
Performance Optimizations
: LZ4 message compression, adaptive battery modes, and optimized networking
Setup
Option 1: Using XcodeGen (Recommended)
Install XcodeGen if you haven't already:
brew install xcodegen
Generate the Xcode project:
cd
bitchat
xcodegen generate
Open the generated project:
open bitchat.xcodeproj
Option 2: Using Swift Package Manager
Open the project in Xcode:
cd
bitchat
open Package.swift
Select your target device and run
Option 3: Manual Xcode Project
Open Xcode and create a new iOS/macOS App
Copy all Swift files from the
bitchat
directory into your project
Update Info.plist with Bluetooth permissions
Set deployment target to iOS 16.0 / macOS 13.0
Usage
Basic Commands
/j #channel
- Join or create a channel
/m @name message
- Send a private message
/w
- List online users
/channels
- Show all discovered channels
/block @name
- Block a peer from messaging you
/block
- List all blocked peers
/unblock @name
- Unblock a peer
/clear
- Clear chat messages
/pass [password]
- Set/change channel password (owner only)
/transfer @name
- Transfer channel ownership
/save
- Toggle message retention for channel (owner only)
Getting Started
Launch bitchat on your device
Set your nickname (or use the auto-generated one)
You'll automatically connect to nearby peers
Join a channel with
/j #general
or start chatting in public
Messages relay through the mesh network to reach distant peers
Channel Features
Password Protection
: Channel owners can set passwords with
/pass
Message Retention
: Owners can enable mandatory message saving with
/save
@ Mentions
: Use
@nickname
to mention users (with autocomplete)
Ownership Transfer
: Pass control to trusted users with
/transfer
Security & Privacy
Encryption
Private Messages
: X25519 key exchange + AES-256-GCM encryption
Channel Messages
: Argon2id password derivation + AES-256-GCM
Digital Signatures
: Ed25519 for message authenticity
Forward Secrecy
: New key pairs generated each session
Privacy Features
No Registration
: No accounts, emails, or phone numbers required
Ephemeral by Default
: Messages exist only in device memory
Cover Traffic
: Random delays and dummy messages prevent traffic analysis
Emergency Wipe
: Triple-tap logo to instantly clear all data
Local-First
: Works completely offline, no servers involved
Performance & Efficiency
Message Compression
LZ4 Compression
: Automatic compression for messages >100 bytes
30-70% bandwidth savings
on typical text messages
Smart compression
: Skips already-compressed data
Battery Optimization
Adaptive Power Modes
: Automatically adjusts based on battery level
Performance mode: Full features when charging or >60% battery
Balanced mode: Default operation (30-60% battery)
Power saver: Reduced scanning when <30% battery
Ultra-low power: Emergency mode when <10% battery
Background efficiency
: Automatic power saving when app backgrounded
Configurable scanning
: Duty cycle adapts to battery state
Network Efficiency
Optimized Bloom filters
: Faster duplicate detection with less memory
Message aggregation
: Batche
44485342.article_summary: BitChat是一款去中心化、无需互联网的蓝牙Mesh网络聊天应用，支持端到端加密。它无需服务器、电话号码或账户，提供基于频道的群聊、消息缓存和转发、IRC风格命令等功能。应用注重隐私保护，支持自动发现 peers 和多跳消息中继，并采用X25519密钥交换和AES-256-GCM加密。其他特性包括消息压缩、自适应电池优化模式、以及紧急数据清除功能。用户可以通过Xcode或Swift Package Manager设置和运行该应用。
44485342.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：去中心化、延迟容忍的消息系统及其可行性和应用场景

不同观点：
• moneywaters提出一个基于去中心化、延迟容忍的消息系统概念，消息通过设备间传递（如通过蓝牙、UWB、Wi-Fi Direct），发送者支付小额费用，中继设备赚取微支付，系统端到端加密、完全去中心化且可选择匿名。他认为这种系统在互联网不稳定或受审查的地区非常有用。但他同时指出该系统的挑战包括延迟和可靠性、滥用/垃圾信息预防、功耗以及用户参与的激励机制。
• sardine5提到他开发的“Murmur: Bluetooth Group Calls”应用，虽然主要是用于语音，但也实现了通过蓝牙LE进行群组通话和消息传递的功能。他表示该应用下载量不高，因此对这种需求的存在持怀疑态度。
• lxgr对现代手机在无移动网络或Wi-Fi覆盖下无法通信表示失望，并建议Apple可以扩展iMessage以支持P2P通信。
• shreyasonline提到他早在10年前就发布了类似的应用“Technitium Bit Chat”。
• syntaxing对Meshtastic需要特殊硬件表示困惑，并建议结合LoRA代理扩展范围，认为Apple可以做类似的事情。
• Beretta_Vexee认为在蓝牙范围内直接聊天比通过消息应用更方便，但提到智能手表和自行车电脑等设备可能有更多有趣的应用场景。
• monkaiju将该应用与Briar对比，认为该应用只支持蓝牙且隐私记录不佳，更多是一个个人项目而非安全环境下的理想选择。
• t43562提到在拥挤事件中手机网络过载导致通信困难的场景，认为这种系统在这种场景下非常有用，但对非技术用户的使用意愿表示担忧。
• seanlinmt将该系统与Briar对比，并建议增加创建投票的功能，提出在抗议活动中的应用场景。

补充讨论：
• 关于该系统是否可行和有实际应用场景的讨论，有人认为这是一个有趣的学术概念，但在现实中需求有限，有人则提出如抗议活动、大型活动中的通信问题等实际应用场景。
• 关于应用的跨平台支持，讨论中提到了iOS和Android的兼容性问题，目前大多数实现主要在Apple设备上。
• 关于激励机制和用户参与的讨论，如何设计一个有效的激励结构以鼓励用户中继消息是一个关键问题。
• 关于现有类似项目的提及，如Briar和Technitium Bit Chat，提供了对该概念已有实现的参考。

data.title: ESIM Security
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Security Explorations公司旗下的研究实验室对eSIM技术进行了安全分析，特别是Kigen的eUICC卡。研究表明，eUICC卡在安装特定Java应用程序时存在安全漏洞，攻击者可通过物理访问和掌握密钥进行恶意操作，甚至可能通过SMS-PP协议进行远程攻击。尽管Kigen声称其eSIM卡具有高度安全性和互操作性，并通过GSMA多层认证，但此次破解显示eUICC在内存内容保护和Java应用程序隔离方面存在缺陷。研究还证实了2019年报告给Oracle的Java Card漏洞确实存在，并首次公开了对消费级GSMA eUICC的成功攻击。此次研究强调了eSIM安全问题，呼吁移动网络运营商和安全公司加强防护措施。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一篇关于GSM/eSIM技术的文章及相关安全问题的评论分析

不同观点：
• [mathfailure] 认为该文章写得非常好，即使作为一个外行，他也能够理解文章中的内容，并对文章的清晰度表示赞赏。
• [Fethbita] 则关注Oracle在解决eSIM安全问题上的不作为，认为这会对整个eSIM生态系统造成威胁，表现出对企业责任的强烈不满。
• [hhh] 评论文章的技术质量很高，并认为其价值远超3万美元，显示出对技术工作的认可。
• [rs_rs_rs_rs_rs] 简短地赞扬了文章的来源（lsd-pl团队），但没有深入讨论技术细节。

补充讨论：
• [exabrial] 对文章中提到的"对密钥的了解是目标卡妥协的主要要求"提出疑问，并通过PGP密钥的例子请求进一步解释，显示出对技术细节的关注和求知欲。
• [ACCount36] 表达了对未修复硬件的公开概念验证（PoC）的期待，并提到他长期以来一直在寻找一种方法来以明文形式转储eSIM，暗示对技术漏洞利用的兴趣。
• [daft_pink] 提出一个附带问题，询问中国是否会采用eSIM技术，显示出对eSIM技术推广范围的关注。
• [petesergeant] 则从一个更广泛的角度出发，认为在任何严重的战争初期，电信服务将会完全瘫痪，反映出对电信安全的担忧。

争议焦点：
• 对于Oracle在解决eSIM安全问题上的不作为，[Fethbita] 表达了强烈的不满，认为这会危及整个eSIM生态系统，而其他评论者未直接涉及此问题。
• 对密钥泄露的潜在威胁，[exabrial] 提出了具体的技术疑问，显示出对细节的关注，而其他评论者未对此进行深入讨论。

总结：评论主要围绕文章的易懂性、技术质量、企业责任、技术漏洞利用的兴趣以及对eSIM技术推广和安全的关注展开。不同评论者从各自的角度出发，提出了对文章内容、技术细节及相关安全问题的各种看法。

General info
In a result of its research investigation efforts, Security Explorations, a research lab of AG Security Research company, conducted security analysis of eSIM technology.
This section of our website presents initial information regarding the project.
Notes
We broke security of
Kigen
(*)
eUICC
card with
GSMA
consumer certificates installed into it.
The eUICC card makes it possible to install the so called eSIM profiles into target chip. eSIM profiles are software representations of mobile subscriptions. For many years such mobile subscriptions had a form of a physical
SIM card
of various factors (SIM, microSIM, nonoSIM). With eSIM, the subscription can come in a pure digital form (as a software bundle), it can also carry Java Card applications.
According to Kigen:
1) eSIMs are "as secure and interoperable as SIM cards [...] thanks to the multi-layered GSMA eSIM certification scheme that protects device makers, device owners and mobile network operators (MNOs)" (
source
)
2) "Kigen OS offers the highest level of logical security when employed on any SIM form factor, including a secure enclave" and "Kigen SIM OS features help differentiate, scale and grow revenues with zero compromise security" (
source
)
The hack proves that our
research on Java Card from 2019
did matter. Oracle indicated the
vulnerabilities we reported
to the company in 2019 were rather irrelevant (the company referred to them as "security concerns") / did not affect their production Java Card VM. These are now proved to be real bugs.
This is likely the first successful public hack against:
consumer GSMA eUICC
Kigen eSIM (Kigen
press releases
and
web pages
implicate over 2 billion SIMs enabled by Kigen secure SIM OS)
EAL(**) certified GSMA security chip (
SLC37 chip
based on 32-bit ARM SecurCore SC300 processor from
Infineon
)
The attack against Kigen eUICC relies both on physical access to sample card along knowledge of the keys used for malicious Java app installation. The remote over-the-air (OTA) vector can't be excluded - our Proof of Concept code mimics a malicious applet installation over OTA
SMS-PP protocol
(Short Message Service Point to Point) on a target Kigen eUICC. In that context, knowledge of the keys is a primary requirement for target card compromise.
The hack proves no security / isolation for the eSIM profile and Java apps (no security for eUICC memory content).
It's worth to note that while this work builds on our past Java Card research from 2019 (along [
25
] [
years
] [
of
] [
Java
] [
hacking
] experience), it required development of some new exploitation techniques / know-how.
We hope the hack brings eSIM security along associated security risks to the focus of mobile network operators (MNOs), vendors, security researchers and security companies. This is important in the context of somewhat bold security claims / overconfidence of eUICC vendors (vide
leaf eUICC cert valid for 100 years
) and MNO assumptions pertaining to profile trust and its storage in a tamper-proof security element (MNO profile integrity / no compromise / no tampering assumed).
(*) as denoted by eUICC / EUM certificates and card EID
(**)
RSP specification
impose minimum EAL4 level ("4.14.1 eUICC Certification Requirements", page 55)
Crypto Proof
As a result of eUICC compromise, we were able to extract private
ECC
key for the certificate

data.title: Million Times Million
data.author: susam
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了长尺度与短尺度两种大数命名系统。作者小时候通过一本旧字典了解了长尺度系统，其中每增加一个前缀表示将百万自乘一次，如百万自乘一次是十亿，自乘两次是万亿。然而，长大后，作者发现当今世界主要使用短尺度系统，其中百万自乘一次是万亿，自乘两次是 quintillion。短尺度系统通过每次增加一千的倍数来命名大数，如百万是千自乘一次，十亿是再乘一次，万亿则是再乘一次。尽管长尺度系统更直观，但短尺度系统在技术、金融等领域更为普遍。作者最终适应了短尺度命名法，但长尺度的记忆仍存于心中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数字命名系统中的长短尺度差异及其在不同语言和国家中的使用

不同观点：
• danbruc：解释了长短尺度的历史演变，提到长尺度中的"trillion"在短尺度中应为"sextillion"，但最终被归为"quintillion"，造成了混淆。
• pilaf：指出西班牙语中传统使用长尺度，但受英语和互联网影响，短尺度用法逐渐增多，导致混淆和"illón"词汇的无用化。
• mynti：从德语角度出发，认为长尺度基于百万的倍数更有逻辑，相较于英语的短尺度命名更清晰。
• vincnetas：幽默地指出美国误解了长短尺度，并举了其他类似的文化误解例子，如Mac的command键。
• GolDDranks：提到东亚使用的万进制数字系统，认为在处理长短尺度时有些复杂。
• HocusLocus：分享了个人故事，讲述了因计算大数字导致机械计算器故障的经历，增添了讨论的趣味性。
• frizlab：表示对长短尺度混淆的理解，并认为长尺度的逻辑更清晰。
• marginalia_nu：提到根据语言和文化背景切换长短尺度和单位，视情况使用不同度量系统。
• eviks：认为长尺度更好，因为需要记忆的前缀更少，逻辑更简单。
• javier_e06：分享了西班牙语中的一个关于数字命名的笑话，增添了讨论的趣味性。
• witrak：声称长尺度在所有欧洲国家使用，并称短尺度为"American"。
• flysand7：询问目前使用长尺度的国家，并分享了俄语中使用短尺度但有"milliard"一词的特殊情况。
• intpx：幽默地表示因讨论而需要重新学习数学。
• 867-5309：分享了个人发现长短尺度命名差异的失望经历，并提及了类似的大数字前缀混淆问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了长短尺度在不同语言中的使用情况，如西班牙语、德语、瑞典语和俄语等，反映了全球范围内数字命名的复杂性。
• 争议的焦点在于长短尺度的混淆和导致的歧义，尤其是在跨语言和跨文化交流中。
