👉
Check out our list of guides
👈
1. Best gaming laptop:
Razer Blade 16
2. Best gaming PC:
HP Omen 35L
3. Best handheld gaming PC:
Lenovo Legion Go S SteamOS ed.
4. Best mini PC:
Minisforum AtomMan G7 PT
5. Best VR headset:
Meta Quest 3
Zukowski reckons that's just not the issue: "The reason Steam makes indies so much money compared to all the other platforms is that they have built up an audience that is full of super die-hard hobbyists… Basically, hobbyists buy stuff not because they actually want to consume it, but because they are collecting it."
This is illustrated by the so-called "pile of shame" from various hobbies: great stacks of Lego sets waiting to be built; a room crammed with Warhammer model kits; the Everest-like mounds of yarn that knitters call their "stash." Apparently the Japanese even have a word for those who buy books and pile them up knowing they won't read them: "tsundoku."
We make a brief stop by an older article from Simon Carless that analysed Steam collections and found the median player on there has
51.5% of their collection unplayed
. The take-home message?
"Valve cracked the problem that Netflix was struggling with: how do you sell to people who have so much entertainment at their fingertips that they don’t have enough hours in the day to play and watch it all," says Zukowski. "Valve basically added infinite hours to a gamer’s day, it is a theoretical future day where gamers might someday spend hours playing your game (but let’s be honest, won’t).

Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
"The reason game developers are willing to give Valve 30% of their revenue is because the Steam marketplace is packed with super gamers who throw money at games they have no intention of playing."
(Image credit: Valve)
While there's no denying Zukowski has a point, I would just slightly put the brakes on before applying this to Steam as a whole. Player habits are constantly changing, and so are players themselves. I'd definitely have fitted this description of Steam players years ago, and remain guilty as charged when it comes to the tsundoku label, but these days am much more careful about what I buy on Steam: purely because I've had that experience of blowing $40 in a Steam sale on a dozen games that I never played, multiple times. I agree that most of us are hoarders of some sort: I'm just not sure that behaviour persists across our lifetime on Steam. Anyway.
"Steam players get satisfaction out of finding a hidden gem and adding it to their collection," posits Zukowski, because "...hobbyists find satisfaction in collecting. Even if they know deep down that they will never actually play it." The fact that loads of people will buy a game but never play it is actually, drum roll please, a massive boon for developers.
"If Steam shoppers were rational and only bought games they were going to play, we would sell a lot fewer games," says Zukowski. "Half this industry would be gone.
"Knowing Steam players are hoarders explains why you give [Valve] that 30%: you get access to a bunch of drunken sailors who spend money irresponsibly."
There are a lot of common sense observations Zukowski makes about this: developers can't really take advantage of such information, and ratios of played / not played aren't worth obsessing over. If a game is either popular or in some sort of bundle, it's also more likely to have higher numbers of owners who haven't played it. Zukowski also has a pet theory, which I find persuasive, that having a clear genre helps games do better on Steam: because people know that they like, for example, open world survival crafting games, and will buy yours even though they've got 20 more in their library to get through

  - **vjk800**：习惯在Steam促销时购买大量游戏，尽管知道不会全玩，因为未来可能有兴趣玩，且促销时不买以后可能错过折扣。
  - **PaulHoule**：游戏积压（backlog）是普遍现象，不仅限于Steam，其他平台如XBOX也有类似情况。购买打折游戏是一种消费习惯，和买衣服等实物商品类似。

• **关于打折和积压游戏的争议**：
  - **octaane**：打折捆绑销售（如Humble Bundle）和购买全价AAA游戏的消费不能等同，前者可能导致虚高的游戏数量统计。
  - **gwbas1c**：质疑Steam上玩家未玩游戏的比例，询问其中有多少是通过免费样品或捆绑包获得的。
  - **gharman**：类似情况不仅限于游戏，其他数字媒体如BJJ Fanatics的教学视频也有类似消费和使用模式。
  - **watwut**：认为51.5%的未玩游戏比例并不算高，尤其是游戏价格低廉且不占用物理空间，批评文章对这一现象的道德化描述。

补充讨论：
- **Steam的垄断地位与竞争**：部分讨论者提到Steam的垄断地位使其能够收取30%的高分成，期待未来有更多竞争以迫使Steam降低分成比例。
- **游戏消费的文化现象**：游戏积压和打折购买成为一种普遍的消费习惯，类似于其他实物商品的购买行为。
- **独立开发者的困境**：独立开发者不仅面临高额税收和分成，还需应对玩家社区管理问题，整体环境充满挑战。

data.author: avadhesh18
data.article_summary: OffChess是一款提供超过10万个离线国际象棋题目的应用程序，用户无需联网即可在任何地方练习。每个谜题都设有评分系统，用户根据自己和谜题的评分获得或失去积分。通过跟踪解题数据，用户可以提高自己的国际象棋技巧。应用还提供多种棋盘主题供选择，让用户个性化设置。可从App Store或Play Store下载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个新推出的国际象棋应用的各种功能、价格、技术实现以及用户体验的反馈和建议。

不同观点：
• [laurentlb] 认为该应用需要一次性支付4.29欧元才能每天解超过7个谜题，同时提到Lichess也是一个不错的替代选择，但其离线支持有限。
• [thethimble] 建议增加“预移动”功能，以便在当前动画完成前输入下一步，从而保持更高水平的用户体验，尤其是对有经验的用户。
• [fractalf] 指出该应用在其无Google服务的Android设备上无法运行，要求修复此问题。
• [dan_can_code] 认为应用的适应性设计不错，但有时目标不明确，尤其是某些谜题的描述容易引起误解，例如“win”在国际象棋中的含义。
• [chatmasta] 对Lichess限制离线下載至50个谜题表示不解。
• [modernerd] 提供了几个小建议：默认关闭文字提示、自动进入下一个谜题、修正类别列表中的拼写错误“Egnlish Opening”。
• [mansoor_] 对应用的技术栈感兴趣，希望了解所使用的技术和原因。
• [ptrkrlsrd] 因不满chess.com的月费而转用该应用，并表示赞赏。
• [JoeDaDude] 推荐了另一个国际象棋谜题应用World Champs，供喜欢此类内容的用户参考，同时强调自己很快会使用该应用。
• [noja] 建议提示不应显示完整的移动，只显示棋子和移动方向即可。
• [bambax] 希望该应用也能有一个网页版，供不常使用手机的用户使用。
• [tigroferoce] 高度赞赏应用无广告、无订阅，并表示愿意付费支持独立开发者。
• [valtism] 提到在即将进行的长途国际航班前发现该应用非常合适，同时指出价格按钮显示与其当地货币不符的问题。
• [tajd] 赞赏应用符合“本地优先软件”的理念，并期待使用。
• [eajr] 认为chess.com费用过高，Lichess界面简陋且谜题支持不足，因此更喜欢该应用的类别选择功能。

补充讨论：
• 用户对价格、功能（如提示和预移动）、拼写错误、设备兼容性及技术实现等方面提出了具体建议和反馈。
• 争议焦点主要集中在应用的目标描述不明确以及价格显示不一致的问题。
• 用户普遍赞赏应用的设计和功能，但对Lichess和chess.com有不同程度的批评和比较。

Pyhoff
Description
The pyhoff package allows you to read and write the most common
Beckhoff and WAGO bus terminals ("Busklemmen") using the Ethernet bus
coupler ("Busskoppler") BK9000, BK9050, BK9100, or WAGO 750_352
over Ethernet TCP/IP based on ModBus TCP.
Key Features
Supports a wide range of Beckhoff and WAGO analog and digital bus
terminals.
Very lightweight: no dependencies; compact code base
Easy to extend
Using standardized ModBus TCP.
Provides high-level abstractions for reading and writing data
from/to IO-terminals with minimal code
Usage Scenarios
Industrial test setups.
Research automation setups.
Data acquisition and monitoring.
Installation
The package has no additional decencies. It can be installed with pip:
pip install pyhoff
Usage

Contributing
Other analog and digital IO terminals are easy to complement. Contributions are welcome!
Please open an issue or submit a pull request on GitHub.
Developer Guide
To get started with developing the
pyhoff
package, follow these steps:
Clone the Repository
First, clone the repository to your local machine using Git:
git clone https://github.com/Nonannet/pyhoff.git
cd
pyhoff
Set Up a Virtual Environment
It is recommended to use a virtual environment to manage dependencies. You can create one using
venv
:
python -m venv venv
source
venv/bin/activate
#
On Windows use `venv\Scripts\activate`
Install Dev Dependencies
Install pyhoff from source plus the dependencies required for development using
pip
:
pip install -e .[dev]
Run Tests
Ensure that everything is set up correctly by running the tests:
pytest

data.title: Parliament in Austria has approved tracking messages in chat applications
data.author: thm
data.article_summary: 奥地利议会通过了一项法律，允许安全部门监控WhatsApp、Messenger和Signal等聊天应用中的加密通讯。该法律仅在涉嫌恐怖活动或违宪活动等有限情况下进行监控，且监控许可有效期为三个月，可延长。尽管内政部长称此举有助于安全，反对党如自由党（FPÖ）和绿党则批评此举可能被滥用，绿党甚至考虑诉诸宪法法院。法律通过前需多层审批，以确保合法性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：监控措施的实施范围及其潜在的滥用风险

不同观点：
• 观点一：监控应仅限于涉嫌恐怖活动或违宪行为等特定情况。这种限制可以防止监控措施被滥用。（[bn-l]的支持立场）
    - 论据：监控的范围应严格限定，以避免历史上出现的滥用问题。
    - 例子：过去曾有对监控权力的滥用，表明限制的必要性。

• 观点二：监控分类标准具有主观性，过去存在滥用现象，因此不应轻易扩大监控范围。（[bn-l]的批评立场）
    - 论据：分类的标准（如恐怖活动或违宪行为）是主观的，容易被操纵或误用。
    - 例子：历史上的滥用案例表明这些标准常常被扩大解释，导致对公民权利的侵害。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：监控权力的边界和分类标准的客观性。一方认为在特定情况下可以实施监控，但另一方担心这些情况的主观性和历史上的滥用记录会导致公民自由受到侵害。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是，如何在保障安全和防止滥用之间取得平衡，这涉及到法律和制度层面的设计与监督。

Politics
Parliament in Austria has approved tracking messages in chat applications
by
Andrea
09.07.2025
written by
Andrea
09.07.2025
0 comments
10
The Austrian Parliament has passed a law that will allow security forces to monitor encrypted communication in applications such as WhatsApp, Messenger and Signal.
MEPs approved the Dolni Chamber of the Austrian Parliament (National Council) on Wednesday with a vote ratio of 105 to 71 government proposal for monitoring both unrequited and encrypted messages in chatting applications such as Messenger, WhatsApp or Signal. Monitoring will only be possible in a significant limited range of cases where terrorist or unconstitutional activities are suspected or spying. TASR informs about this, referring to APA.
In principle, the permission for communication monitoring can only be granted for a period of three months, and it is allowed to extend it. Before implementation, several levels of approval are built in which the Plenipotentiary plays a key role for legal protection and the Federal Administrative Court.
Criticism of the opposition
The proposal were not only opposition free (FPÖ) and Greens, but also two deputies of the coalition party NEOS. FPÖ considers the use of “citizens ‘spying software” and thinks that individuals’ real aim, such as critics of measures introduced during the coronavirus pandemic, is the real goal.
According to the Green MP Süleyman Zorba, the question in starting the tracking is not whether he will be misused, but when. It also doubts that technically it will only be possible to monitor a specific application. The Greens therefore consider to turn to the Constitutional Court.
Minister’s statement
After approval of the proposal, the Austrian Interior Minister Gerhard Karner stated that today is an extraordinary day for Austria’s security, the police and especially for the Office for the Protection of the Constitution. He recalled that the executive power has so far been able to open letters and intercept calls from fixed lines, but terrorists are no longer using these means of communication.

data.title: When Figma starts designing us
data.author: bravomartin
data.article_summary: 文章作者回顾了自2013年首次接触Figma以来的体验，肯定了Figma在远程设计工作中的核心作用，但也表达了对Figma推动设计工具工程化倾向的担忧。作者认为，Figma的一些功能（如智能组件、变量、自动布局和交互原型）虽然在表面上提升了设计与工程的一致性，但实际上限制了设计的创造性和可能性。例如，自动布局功能虽然方便，却使设计师在早期探索阶段就被迫以工程思维工作，限制了自由表达和实验。此外，开发者模式强调了设计的精细化，导致大量时间被用于制作复杂原型，而这些原型最终往往被代码取代。作者呼吁设计师警惕这种过早优化的趋势，强调设计应从草图开始，快速进入代码迭代，以保持创造性和灵活性。Figma虽然强大，但设计师应注意其对工作方式的潜移默化影响，确保工具为创意服务，而不是被工具束缚。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Figma的设计工具功能及其对设计和开发流程的影响

不同观点：
• miiiiiike认为Figma在设计系统的实现上不够强大，尤其是在处理变量、模式和响应式设计时存在性能问题和限制。他认为Figma过于“设计师化”，无法满足工程师的需求，最终选择用代码实现设计系统。
• mananaysiempre指出设计不应忽视媒介的限制，设计工具应该允许在约束内进行设计，而不是完全脱离这些限制。他认为Figma的约束是合理的，因为它们反映了实际开发中的问题。
• Lalabadie同意miiiiiike的观点，认为Figma过于强调“开发就绪”，影响了设计的探索阶段。他怀念Photoshop的自由探索过程，认为Figma在早期设计阶段会产生优先级冲突。
• bbx则高度赞赏Figma的Auto Layout功能，认为它解决了设计中重复性和响应式布局的问题，极大地提高了设计效率。
• karaterobot反驳了对Auto Layout的批评，认为其实际上提高了设计的效率和灵活性，并指出“开发就绪”只是工作流程中的一个状态，不意味着设计的终结。
• pyrale支持miiiiiike的观点，认为设计应该快速进入代码阶段，并在团队中进行迭代，而不是在设计完成后再交给开发团队。
• samsolomon认为没有理想的工作流程，Figma在许多产品组织中表现良好，特别是在大型团队中，设计和代码的紧密对应是必要的。
• zelphirkalt批评许多网页设计师缺乏对HTML和CSS的了解，认为Figma中的设计不应脱离实际开发的可能性。
• asoneth指出设计中有探索性设计和使用已有模式的区别，Figma适用于大多数使用常规设计模式的情况，而探索性设计需要更广泛的工具集。
• jjcm（Figma的设计系统PM）回应文章，承认Figma的目标是允许自由和结构化设计的结合，强调结构化设计可以加速设计过程，但这些功能是可选的，不是强制的。
• travisgriggs分享了与设计外包公司合作的经历，该公司坚持Figma是唯一工具，文章中对Dev Mode的批评引起了他的共鸣。
• drewbeck认为工具对工作流程有影响，但组织和领导层才真正决定了工作流程，Figma并没有阻止作者期望的工作流程。
• burnt-resistor提到工具对创造性表达的影响，建议工具制作者应更密切地倾听设计师的需求。
• meteyor认为Figma的新功能让设计失去了个性，行业正在将角色合并，使得设计变得缺乏人性化。

补充讨论：
• Figma是否过于强调“开发就绪”而影响了设计的探索和创造性。
• Auto Layout功能的价值和其对设计效率的影响。
• 设计工具对工作流程的影响以及组织在选择工具和制定流程中的角色。
• 设计师是否需要深入了解HTML和CSS以更好地进行网页设计。
• 工具对设计过程和创造性表达的影响。

争议焦点：
• Figma的Auto Layout和其他结构化功能是否限制了设计的自由和创造性。
• 设计工具是否应该更注重自由探索阶段或更接近实际开发阶段。

44479502.article_content:
I first encountered Figma in 2013, when Dylan Field demoed an early prototype
to me at O’Reilly’s Foo Camp. I remember the pen tool feeling surprisingly
elegant, but I missed the bigger picture: the radical implications of a design
tool that ran in the browser. A decade later, Figma is a core part of our
creative process, and without it, we wouldn't have been able to build a fully
remote design practice. That’s probably why Dylan is a near-billionaire and
I’m not.
However, over the course of the last five years, I’ve grown increasingly
worried about what Figma is doing to the field of design by pushing designers
toward an engineering-centric way of working. This can be seen in their
feature releases: Smart Components, Variables, Auto Layout, and Interactive
Prototypes. These features are often celebrated as steps toward parity with
engineering, but in practice, they encourage a mode of working that narrows
the field of possibility at precisely the moment when it should be expanding.
A concrete example is Auto Layout. It may seem harmless at first to introduce
a DOM-like layout mechanism in a design tool, and it certainly has advantages
in mature design files where the structure rarely changes. But many design
teams today use Auto Layout to create full page designs of their digital
products from the get-go. In practice, this locks the design in place and
severely limits the possible expressions. You can’t drag things around freely
or try odd combinations of layouts. You can’t simply paste something into a
frame without it snapping to the bottom of the stack. The result is that
designers are nudged into thinking like engineers during the earliest stages
of exploration just when they should be working messily, freely, and loosely.
It might feel convenient at first, but it comes at a cost. Have you ever
opened a Figma file and tried to make a small change, only to find yourself
wrestling with the layout? I’ve encountered this more often than I’d like, and
it seems to be increasing in frequency.
Another feature is Dev Mode, which, in theory, is the missing bridge between
the design specification and the technical implementation. However, it
enforces a mindset where designers polish designs far away from the technology
they are designing for, and where enormous amounts of time are spent on
building complex prototypes, only for them to be discarded and rebuilt in
code. This is all done in the name of making something ready for development.
This is contrary to my belief that any digital design process should start
with rough sketches, but move quickly into code and iterate from there. Those
sketches might even be done in code. A design is never “ready for dev”,
because a lot of what we consider to be design decisions – interaction,
animation, loading of data – can really only be prototyped in code. “Ready for
dev” implies that the creation is done and that the developer is merely there
to execute the designer’s vision, implicitly preventing them from questioning
any of the decisions when the rubber hits the road.
These are just two examples, but it illustrates a worrying trend towards a
premature optimization of design. These features encourage designers to make
decisions too early, to over-structure ideas before they’ve had a chance to
unfold. The result is a narrowing of the design space, where the flexibility
needed for creative discovery is replaced by enforced consistency and
structure. This comes on top of the incredible number of
structured tasks
that most modern design teams adhere to. This inevitably contributes to the
growing monoculture in digital design where everything starts to look and feel
the same, not because of shared intent, but because of shared constraints.
I’ve spent the last 15 years advocating for deeper collaboration between
designers and engineers, so it might seem contradictory to critique a tool
that brings those disciplines closer together. But interdisciplinary work
doesn’t mean collapsing into one way of thinking. The goal isn’t for designers
to adopt engineering practices, but to bring distinct perspectives through an
interdisciplinary way of collaborating.
Figma is extremely powerful, but it is bending us toward a way of working that
prioritizes structure over spontaneity. As designers, we should remain alert
to this shift, not because Figma is inherently bad, but because the values it
encodes can quietly reshape our practices. The best design work rarely starts
with order. It starts with questions, with play, with a lot of mess. We need
tools that make room for that. Because if everything is neatly aligned from
the beginning, we may never discover what lies just outside the grid.

data.title: Adding a feature because ChatGPT incorrectly thinks it exists
data.author: adrianh
data.article_summary: Adrian Holovaty讲述了Soundslice遇到的一个奇怪现象。他们的乐谱扫描系统本应用于将图片中的乐谱数字化，但近期错误日志中出现大量ChatGPT截图，这些截图包含ASCII吉他谱，而非实际乐谱图片。调查发现，ChatGPT错误地指导用户使用Soundslice上传ASCII吉他谱以获取音频回放，而实际上Soundslice并不支持该功能。为应对这一误解，团队决定开发ASCII吉他谱导入工具，以满足用户需求，尽管最初并未计划在2025年开发此功能。Holovaty对这种情况感到复杂，一方面乐于帮助用户，另一方面对因误传而开发功能感到不安。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕GPT-4在编程和产品开发中的应用及其引发的问题和机遇的讨论。

不同观点：
• Kragen认为GPT-4在编程中通过“猜测”API功能，可以提供创造性的解决方案，帮助改进API的可猜测性和可理解性。他指出，这种方法依赖于GPT-4的“幻想”能力，而不是准确的信息提供。不过，这种方法只能解决API不直观的问题，无法改善效率、可靠性或组合性等问题。
• JimDabell补充说，这种“幻想”特性不仅适用于API开发，还可以用于产品功能开发，类似于测试驱动开发（TDD）的效果。
• ShermanTanktop通过音乐记谱工具的例子说明，GPT-4可以“幻想”出新的用户需求，例如Soundslice功能，尽管目前用户需求不明显，但未来可能会有所改变。
• Gortok则担心这种“幻想”特性可能带来负面影响，认为这是技术提供者应该避免的问题，而不是庆祝的创新。
• Ahstilde从市场营销的角度看待这个问题，认为这是产品与渠道契合的例子，通过捕捉新的用户需求来增加产品曝光。
• Deweller提出，AI系统通过市场力量影响现实世界，而不是通过人们通常担心的机器人统治等方式。
• Jrochkind1关注AI聊天机器人对网站流量的引导作用，并预测这将成为巨大的商业机会。
• Oasisbob从销售团队快速响应AI“幻想”功能的角度，认为这在B2B初创公司中并不罕见。
• Simonw认为，解决GPT-4“幻想”问题比添加新功能更困难，并幽默地指出，这比让OpenAI修复问题更容易。
• Felixarba认为用户不应责怪产品提供者，而应责怪GPT-4的“幻想”问题。
• Adamgordonbell分享了他们在使用AI聊天机器人时遇到的类似问题，并将其视为产品反馈。
• Chaboud在无网络环境下使用Lama模型时也遇到了类似问题，并通过实现自定义功能解决了代码生成问题。
• Jivings则抱怨他们的流量大量来自ChatGPT的“幻想”功能，并表示不希望进入ChatGPT驱动的开发模式。
• Alex-moon认为ChatGPT在此过程中扮演了“市场研究”工具的角色，帮助识别用户需求，但这不是开发新功能的直接动力。
• Rorylaitila通过使用OpenAI视觉工具进行索引构建，发现AI有时会提供意想不到的好主意，例如提取名人名字，但也会有不遵循指令的情况。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中反复提到GPT-4的“幻想”特性，既被视为创造性解决方案的来源，也被视为潜在问题。
• 不同参与者从技术、市场和产品开发等多个角度分析了AI聊天机器人在实际应用中的影响和挑战。
• 争议焦点在于“幻想”特性带来的机会与风险，以及如何有效利用或控制这种特性。

44491071.article_content:
Adrian Holovaty
>
Writing
Adding a feature because ChatGPT incorrectly thinks it exists
Written by
Adrian Holovaty
on July 7, 2025
Well, here’s a weird one.
At Soundslice, our
sheet music scanner
digitizes music from photographs, so you can listen, edit and practice. We continually improve the system, and I keep an eye on the error logs to see which images are getting poor results.
In the last few months, I started noticing an odd type of upload in our error logs. Instead of images like this...
...we were starting to see images like this:
Um, that’s just a screenshot of a ChatGPT session...! WTF? Obviously that’s not music notation. It’s
ASCII tablature
, a rather barebones way of notating music for guitar.
Our scanning system wasn’t intended to support this style of notation. Why, then, were we being bombarded with so many ASCII tab ChatGPT screenshots? I was mystified for weeks — until I messed around with ChatGPT myself and got this:
Turns out ChatGPT is telling people to go to Soundslice, create an account and import ASCII tab in order to hear the audio playback. So that explains it!
Problem is, we didn’t actually have that feature. We’ve never supported ASCII tab; ChatGPT was outright lying to people. And making us look bad in the process, setting false expectations about our service.
So that raised an interesting product question. What should we do? We’ve got a steady stream of new users who’ve been told incorrect facts about our offering. Do we slap disclaimers all over our product, saying “Ignore what ChatGPT is saying about ASCII tab support”?
We ended up deciding: what the heck, we might as well meet the market demand. So we put together a bespoke
ASCII tab importer
(which was near the bottom of my “Software I expected to write in 2025” list). And we changed the UI copy in our scanning system to tell people about that feature.
To my knowledge, this is the first case of a company developing a feature because ChatGPT is incorrectly telling people it exists. (Yay?) I’m sharing the story because I think it’s somewhat interesting.
My feelings on this are conflicted. I’m happy to add a tool that helps people. But I feel like our hand was forced in a weird way. Should we really be developing features in response to misinformation?

data.title: SIMD.info – Reference tool for C intrinsics of all major SIMD engines
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: 这篇文章对比了几种不同的指令集架构：GO（未明确具体类型，可能指代GPU相关的计算）、VSX（IBM Power架构的向量计算指令集）、NEON（ARM处理器的SIMD指令集）、SSE4.2、AVX2和AVX-512（均为英特尔和AMD的x86指令集）。文章主要讨论了这些指令集在并行计算、向量操作以及在不同硬件平台上的性能表现和适用场景。SSE4.2和AVX2广泛用于消费级处理器，而AVX-512则面向高性能计算，NEON和VSX则分别针对移动设备和企业级服务器。各指令集在计算能力、功耗和应用场景上各有优劣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个提供指令搜索功能的参考网站的评价与建议

不同观点：
• syockit：认为该网站的搜索功能不错，但指令详情不够详细，尤其是与x86其他参考资料（如Felix Cloutier和Intel文档）相比，缺少图示和伪代码等细节。
• Const-me：指出该网站的ISA扩展标签不准确，例如将SSE2到SSE4.1的intrinsics都归为SSE 4.2，以及所有FMA3 intrinsics归为AVX2。并提到有一个处理器支持AVX2但不支持FMA3，同时批评搜索功能不理想，搜索FMA时无法找到AMD64相关的intrinsics。
• Sesse__：批评搜索结果过于 sparse，缺少函数原型，且示例页面冗长、格式不合理（如保留了"e.g."前缀导致零结果），并提到示例对比度低，难以阅读。
• convery：认为搜索功能在不知道具体指令时使用不便，例如搜索'SHA'时由于未选平台而没有结果，而搜索'hash'则得到无关结果。
• fancyfredbot：提到使用Claude工具将标量代码转换为AVX512时遇到问题，尤其是在处理嵌套if语句转换为mask操作时，Claude会遗忘合并内外mask。
• mshockwave：询问是否有计划添加ARM SVE和RISC-V V扩展支持。
• llm_nerd：认为该工具很有趣，但质疑是否很多人直接使用SIMD指令，建议使用跨平台的库可能更实际，并指出讨论SIMD更多是出于乐趣和知识追求。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是搜索功能的有效性和结果的相关性。
• 另一个焦点是指令详情和参考资料的丰富程度，尤其是与x86其他资源的对比。
• 用户对添加更多架构（如ARM SVE和RISC-V V）的支持表现出兴趣。
• 有用户提到使用自动化工具（如Claude）进行SIMD代码转换时遇到的实际问题。
• 对直接使用SIMD指令的实际需求存在质疑，部分用户认为使用现成库更合理。

data.title: François Chollet: The Arc Prize and How We Get to AGI [video]
data.author: sandslash
data.article_summary: 本文简要列出了与Google相关的各类信息和资源。内容包括关于Google的介绍、新闻发布、版权声明、联系方式、创作者信息、广告、开发者选项、条款规定、隐私政策、安全指引以及YouTube的功能测试和NFL Sunday Ticket服务。同时，文章底部标明了版权归属为2025年Google LLC所有。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AGI（通用人工智能）的定义和衡量标准，特别是ARC评估测试是否能有效衡量AGI。

不同观点：
• qoez：认为ARC评估测试的高分并不等同于AGI，因为该测试主要考察模式识别能力，而人类的智力有多种类型，仅仅在IQ测试中表现优异并不代表真正的聪明。
• esbranson：指出AGI并不等于意识，且AGI并不需要超人类智力。普通的10岁儿童拥有一般智力，但在这些测试中未必表现优异。同时，AGI的定义应更关注于完成人类容易完成的任务。
• TheAceOfHearts：ARC数据集的预览是一个亮点，但Chollet的观点已在其他场合重复多次。讨论中提到持续学习能力可能是构建AGI的关键因素。
• EigenLord：提到AGI与No Free Lunch Theorem的冲突，认为科学并未主导AGI的叙事，而是金钱。还质疑“人类般的智力是否真正通用”，并引用David Wolpert的工作来说明某些类型的全知智能是不可能的。
• stared：不喜欢AGI这个术语，认为 intelligence 总是涉及权衡。ARC-AGI高分并不代表通用智力，而是AI在解决一类以前无法解决的问题上取得了进展。
• modeless：将ARC-AGI与PuzzleScript游戏相比较，建议可以创建一个PuzzleScript AGI基准。
• visarga：认为智力是搜索，是探索和学习的结合，智力在于模型和环境之间的相互作用，而非单独存在于模型或环境中。
• GarnetFloride：提出AGI可能需要采取统计方法，像教孩子一样建立一个可以根据情况更新知识的系统。
• PostOnce：通过实际例子说明当前AI系统在处理简单任务时的不足，认为AGI还有很长的路要走。
• bogtog：讨论了ARC测试中的视觉特性，认为这些特性对人类容易但对LLM（大型语言模型）困难，模型在解释字符网格时表现不佳。
• kcaj：引用谈话中对智力的定义，提出一般智力的转换率问题，并质疑一般智力的定义是否是不可计算的。
• noiv：提到Bongard Problems，并对o1在此类问题上的表现表示怀疑。
• lawlessone：质疑AGI的定义，认为AGI应是 constantly aware 的，像生物大脑一样不断更新和存储记忆。
• gtech1：提出一个简单定义AGI的方法，即能回答人类无法回答的问题的系统。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于ARC评估测试是否能够真正衡量AGI，特别是它是否过于侧重模式识别和特定类型的智力。
• 另一个讨论点是AGI的定义，包括是否需要持续意识和记忆更新能力。
• 还有人提出AGI可能需要具备持续学习能力和统计方法，以便在不同情况下更新知识。
• 科学与商业利益在AGI叙事中的角色也被提及，认为当前的AGI发展更多受到金钱驱动而非科学主导。

data.title: Show HN: NYC Subway Simulator and Route Designer
data.author: HeavenFox
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：地铁模拟项目的多方面反馈与建议

不同观点：
• [avianlyric] 认为默认的列车停站时间过短，尤其是在高运力的系统中，停站时间是限制乘客容量的关键因素。他以伦敦维多利亚线的例子说明，30秒是较为实际的最低停站时间，并指出停站时间包括开门、关门、安全检查等多个环节，而不仅仅是乘客上下车。此外，他还提到纽约地铁使用固定闭塞系统，而非模拟中使用的移动闭塞系统，后者效率更高。

• [darthplagius] 表示自己为MTA（纽约大都会运输署）外包工作，特别是AI和创新团队，并计划将该模拟项目展示给团队，认为他们会感兴趣。

• [blehn] 对项目的视觉设计提出建议，认为应根据线路颜色匹配轨道和列车颜色，并提出使用不同的视觉指标来表示列车的不同状态，例如 stopped、at station 等。

• [xnx] 提到在编辑路线时遇到技术问题，点击“<- Add”按钮后出现控制台错误并导致页面空白。

• [Aaronstotle] 表达了对创建跨公园地铁线路的期望。

• [kiwibyproxy] 建议在readme中提供更多关于项目结构的信息，以及如何适应其他城市的指南。

• [konsalexee] 对项目表示赞赏，并建议增加时间旅行滑块功能。

• [fsckboy] 幽默地指出模拟中未考虑高峰时段车厢内恶劣气味和地板积水对乘客行为的影响。

• [indoordin0saur] 表示自己也曾有做类似项目的念头。

• [zerojames] 简单地对项目表示赞赏。

• [shiroiuma] 质疑设计自定义路线的意义，认为纽约 unlikely 会建设新线路。

• [ars] 提到在模拟中无法添加从Bay Ridge到Clinton的路线，并通过研究发现斯塔滕岛到新泽西的公共交通极其有限，除非将地铁线路延长至Goethals Bridge。

• [pimlottc] 指出项目的移动端体验不佳，地图控件遮挡了大部分地图，建议增加最小化控件的功能以改善移动端体验。

补充讨论：
• 技术问题：[xnx] 和 [ars] 提到了在使用过程中遇到的技术问题和路线设计限制。
• 视觉设计：[blehn] 对项目视觉语言提出了具体改进建议。
• 功能建议：[kiwibyproxy] 和 [konsalexee] 分别提出了增加项目文档和时间旅行功能的建议。
• 现实应用：[avianlyric] 和 [shiroiuma] 讨论了模拟项目在现实中的应用和限制。

争议焦点：停站时间的合理性和现实适应性，[avianlyric] 强调现实中的复杂性，而项目可能过于简化。

Solving Wordle with uv's dependency resolver
7th Jul 2025
•
12 min read

Tags:
programming

tech

why

disgusting hacks
Table of Contents
Introduction
Background: Sudoku and Python dependency resolution
What is Wordle
Analysis
Basic building blocks
Greens and yellows
Python dependency rules?
Possible position packages
Feedback packages
Putting this all together: the cursed neural network
Implementation
Package examples
--find-links and wheels
Harness
Bonus round: more efficient guessing
Blooper reel
GitHub
Introduction
In a previous life, I wrote a
Sudoku solver that relied on Poetry's dependency resolver
. We ended up selling that startup to EDB (not because of the Poetry hack), which means that they now own this IP. And, since then, Python packaging has advanced, with
uv
taking the world by storm.
This means that it's time for a refresh. Can we use
uv
instead of Poetry? And can we solve a Wordle instead of a Sudoku?
For the impatient: you can get the solver from
my GitHub
. Run
uv run main.py run
and watch it go.
Background: Sudoku and Python dependency resolution
The short summary of the Sudoku + Poetry post is that unlike Rust or JavaScript, a single Python project cannot use more than one version of a specific Python package. This means that we can easily represent a Sudoku grid as 81 Python packages, each with 9 possible versions. If a certain cell has a specific number (version), cells in the same row, column and a 3x3 square it belongs to cannot have that same number.
We can encode these rules as version constraints on other packages representing our cell's neighbours.
Once we have our 81 packages, all that remains is encoding our problem by making another package, specifying the precise versions of the cells where we already have numbers, leaving the rest as wildcards, and then letting Poetry generate a lockfile that will assign each number (version) to every cell (package), thus solving the puzzle.
What is Wordle
This
is Wordle.
You have six attempts to guess a five-letter word. On each guess, you get what I'll be calling "feedback": each letter in your guess becomes green (correct letter in the correct position), yellow (correct letter, wrong position) or nothing (wrong letter).
In this post, I'll represent it as a string
YGG..
, meaning that the feedback we got for our answer is:
Yellow at position 1
Green at positions 2 and 3
Blank or "dot" at positions 4 and 5
Analysis
It is said that if you ask an LLM to think really hard about its answer and write down its thinking before giving the final response, then it can successfully count the number of r's in the word
strawberrry
and help you sell more inference tokens.
Let's do exactly that and break this down.
Basic building blocks
Let's start simple. The solution to a Wordle is a five-letter word, and we'd like our system to choose one possible word given all information that we feed into it. We can encode this as a single Python package with multiple possible versions, where each version represents a single word. This is a useful building block.
The other building block is that each position can only have one letter in it. We can easily represent this as five "position" packages, each of which can have 26 versions. If the position package 1 has version 2, that means "B" is in that position.
We can then draw dependencies between a specific version of our "word" package to specific versions of our "position" packages. If our word is
STALL
, then it'll depend on:
position package 1, version 19 (S)
position package 2, version 20 (T)
position package 3, version 1 (A)
position packages 4 and 5, version 12 (L)
Greens and yellows
However, this is not enough. We need to encode some more complex facts about the solution in Wordle than we did with Sudoku. For example, let's assume that we guessed
CHILD
and the feedback we got is
..YG.
. This means:
The fourth letter is L
The third letter is not I
But there is at least one I somewhere in the word
None of the letters are C, H or D
Is this correct though? There is a bit of nuance here.
Let's try again, this time with a different guess but the same word. We try
ATOLL
(it's not an optimal play, but as a demonstration) and get
...GY
. Here, we can't just say that there is an L somewhere in the word (because there already is). We have to say that there is at least one L in the first, second or third position.
Now let's say we guess
LILLE
and get
.GGG.
. What does this mean? Just because L in the first position gave us a dot doesn't mean there are no Ls in the word at all (there clearly are). Instead, we need to say that the first and the fifth position don't contain an L.
One thing that stems from this is that the feedback we get for a specific letter in a specific position will change based on other letters in our guess. For example, let's say the real world is
BUNNY
. If we guess
NNNON
, we'll get
YYG.Y
. And if we then guess
NNNNN
, we'll get
..GG.
. Because we discovered all Ns in the word, the first, secon

data.title: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
data.author: GavCo
data.article_summary: Biomni是一款通用的生物医学AI代理，旨在自动执行各种生物医学研究任务，通过整合大型语言模型（LLM）推理、检索增强规划和基于代码的执行，帮助科学家大幅提高研究效率并生成可测试的假设。用户可以通过设置脚本安装Biomni，并使用自然语言执行如CRISPR筛选、单细胞RNA测序注释和化合物ADMET性质预测等任务。Biomni是一个开放科学项目，鼓励社区贡献新工具、数据集、软件和基准等。当前正开发下一代版本Biomni-E2，贡献者将有机会在顶级期刊上共同署名发表论文。Biomni基于Apache-2.0许可证发布，但某些集成工具可能有更严格的商业许可证。更多信息和使用方法可访问biomni.stanford.edu。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具在生物医学研究中的应用及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• deepdarkforest：认为该工具通过预设的150多个特定工具，能够减少错误率，并提高分析的准确性，特别是在处理标准化的数据时。但也指出实际数据往往更复杂，工具的适用性可能有限。同时，对长期使用专有数据集的优势持保留态度。
• Edmond：对AI在科学研究中的应用潜力表示乐观，并提到构建智能工作空间的可能性，以辅助科学研究。
• andy99：关注该工具在生物威胁方面的潜在风险，担心其可能被用于制造生物武器，但对LLM当前的能力持怀疑态度。
• freedomben：对AI在医学研究中的潜力表示兴奋，尤其在数据模式识别和新药物开发方面，认为AI可以带来重大突破。
• teenvan_1995：对提供150多个工具的实用性表示怀疑，认为需要在实际应用中验证其效果，特别是考虑到上下文限制。
• epistasis：对该工具的发布表示兴奋，并提到自己一直在等待试用该工具。
• dmezzetti：分享了自己在生物医学文献分析方面的开源项目，提供了相关工具的链接，认为这些工具可以与该项目互补。
• AIorNot：对该工具的实用性表示认可，并提到已推荐给在Crispr实验室工作的朋友。
• SalmoShalazar：认为当前许多类似软件的开发缺乏创新，主要是围绕LLM API调用进行特定领域的专业化，整体创新有限。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：该工具的实用性和创新性。deepdarkforest和teenvan_1995对其在实际数据处理中的效果持保留态度，而SalmoShalazar则认为当前类似软件的创新性不足。
• 潜在风险：andy99提出了该工具在生物威胁方面的潜在风险，尽管其他评论者对此未有深入讨论。
• 开源项目：dmezzetti分享了相关的开源项目，提供了更多资源以供参考和互补使用。
• 积极评价：Edmond、freedomben和epistasis对该工具在科学研究中的潜力表示乐观，并期待其实际应用效果。

Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
Overview
Biomni is a general-purpose biomedical AI agent designed to autonomously execute a wide range of research tasks across diverse biomedical subfields. By integrating cutting-edge large language model (LLM) reasoning with retrieval-augmented planning and code-based execution, Biomni helps scientists dramatically enhance research productivity and generate testable hypotheses.
Quick Start
Installation
Our software environment is massive and we provide a single setup.sh script to setup.
Follow this
file
to setup the env first.
Then activate the environment E1:
conda activate biomni_e1
then install the latest biomni package:
pip install biomni --upgrade
Or install from the github source version.
Lastly, configure your API keys in bash profile
~/.bashrc
:
export
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
"
YOUR_API_KEY
"
export
OPENAI_API_KEY=
"
YOUR_API_KEY
"
#
optional if you just use Claude
Basic Usage
Once inside the environment, you can start using Biomni:
from
biomni
.
agent
import
A1
# Initialize the agent with data path, Data lake will be automatically downloaded on first run (~11GB)
agent
=
A1
(
path
=
'./data'
,
llm
=
'claude-sonnet-4-20250514'
)
# Execute biomedical tasks using natural language
agent
.
go
(
"Plan a CRISPR screen to identify genes that regulate T cell exhaustion, generate 32 genes that maximize the perturbation effect."
)
agent
.
go
(
"Perform scRNA-seq annotation at [PATH] and generate meaningful hypothesis"
)
agent
.
go
(
"Predict ADMET properties for this compound: CC(C)CC1=CC=C(C=C1)C(C)C(=O)O"
)
🤝 Contributing to Biomni
Biomni is an open-science initiative that thrives on community contributions. We welcome:
🔧 New Tools
: Specialized analysis functions and algorithms
📊 Datasets
: Curated biomedical data and knowledge bases
💻 Software
: Integration of existing biomedical software packages
📋 Benchmarks
: Evaluation datasets and performance metrics
📚 Misc
: Tutorials, examples, and use cases
🔧 Update existing tools
: many current tools are not optimized - fix and replacements are welcome!
Check out this
Contributing Guide
on how to contribute to the Biomni ecosystem.
If you have particular tool/database/software in mind that you want to add, you can also submit to
this form
and the biomni team will implement them.
🔬 Call for Contributors: Help Build Biomni-E2
Biomni-E1 only scratches the surface of what’s possible in the biomedical action space.
Now, we’re building
Biomni-E2
— a next-generation environment developed
with and for the community
.
We believe that by collaboratively defining and curating a shared library of standard biomedical actions, we can accelerate science for everyone.
Join us in shaping the future of biomedical AI agent.
Contributors with significant impact
(e.g., 10+ significant & integrated tool contributions or equivalent) will be
invited as co-authors
on our upcoming paper in a top-tier journal or conference.
All contributors
will be acknowledged in our publications.
More contributor perks...
Let’s build it together.

Biomni 101
- Basic concepts and first steps
More to come!

Experience Biomni through our no-code web interface at
biomni.stanford.edu
.

A tutorial on how to contribute to Biomni

This release was frozen as of April 15 2025, so it differs from the current web platform.
Biomni itself is Apache 2.0-licensed, but certain integrated tools, databases, or software may carry more restrictive commercial licenses. Review each component carefully before any commercial use.

jank programming language - Clojure/LLVM/C++
The jank programming language
jank is a
general-purpose programming language
which embraces the
interactive, value-oriented
nature of Clojure as well as the desire for
native compilation and minimal runtimes
. jank is
strongly compatible with Clojure
and considers itself a dialect of Clojure. Please note that jank is under heavy development; assume all features are planned or incomplete.
Where jank differs from Clojure JVM is that its host is C++ on top of an
LLVM-based JIT
. This allows jank to offer the same benefits of
REPL-based development
while being able to
seamlessly reach into the native world
and compete seriously with JVM's performance.
Still, jank is a Clojure dialect and thus includes its
code-as-data philosophy and powerful macro system
. jank remains a functional-first language which builds upon Clojure's rich set of
persistent, immutable data structures
. When mutability is needed, jank offers a software transaction memory and reactive agent system to ensure
clean and correct multi-threaded designs
.
Current progress
Github
Sponsor
Wide spectrum dynamics
Enjoy both REPL iteration with JIT compilation and static AOT compilation to native executables.
01
Iterate like you would with Clojure
Iterate in the REPL and build your program from the ground up without leaving your editor.
(
defn
-main
[
& args
]
(
loop
[
game-state
(
new-game!
)]
(
when
(
done?
game-state
)
(
end-game!
game-state
)
(
recur
(
next-state
game-state
)))))
02
Reach into the native world
Seamlessly switch to inline C++ within your Clojure source, while still having access to your Clojure code using interpolation.
(
defn
create-vertex-shader!
[]
(
c++/glCreateShader
c++/GL_VERTEX_SHADER
))
(
defn
set-shader-source!
[
shader source
]
(
let
[
shader
(
int
shader
)
source
(
str
source
)]
(
c++/glShaderSource
shader
1
source c++/nullptr
)))
(
defn
compile-shader!
[
shader
]
(
c++/glCompileShader
(
int
shader
)))
03
Compile to machine code
jank is built on an LLVM-based JIT. With AOT enabled, both statically and dynamically linked executables can be generated. The jank compiler itself has very speedy start times and low memory usage.
$
time
taskset
0x1
clj
hello-world.clj
hello
world
real
0m1.127s
user
0m0.997s
sys
0m0.111s
$
time
taskset
0x1
jank
run
hello-world.clj
hello
world
real
0m0.086s
user
0m0.045s
sys
0m0.040s
04
World-class errors
jank stands in its own category among lisps for its error reporting quality. No bloated JVM stack traces, opaque errors, or lack of context.
jank builds upon Clojure.
Keep your existing code; gain more confidence and more speed.
Strongly compatible with Clojure
If it works with Clojure JVM and it works with ClojureScript, it should work with jank. There's a
:jank
reader conditional for when you need it.
REPL and native JIT
Use your favorite nREPL editor plugin. jank uses an LLVM-based JIT to compile machine code on the fly.
Go native
Reach into native libraries or interact directly with your native code base. Seamlessly write both C++ and Clojure in the same file.
Tooling friendly
Leiningen, LSP, nREPL planned from the start. jank's compiler is also written with tooling in mind, so it can be used for lexing, parsing, and analysis.
jank examples
All of the following examples are also valid Clojure code.

jank has very powerful capabilities for representing and transforming arbitrary data. Here, idiomatic usages of
reduce
,
zipmap
,
repeat
, and
merge-with
help create an index from genre to movie id with ease. No lenses are required for working with nested data.

{

fn

acc

genres

data.title: Configuring Split Horizon DNS with Pi-Hole and Tailscale
data.author: gm678
data.article_summary:
作者过去使用OpenVPN，但后来转向了基于Wireguard协议的Tailscale，因为它速度更快。Tailscale是加拿大公司，无法查看连接内容，用户也可自行托管。作者设置了Tailscale网络（tailnet），但未配置分离DNS。最初，反向代理服务器被配置为向其局域网IP发送路由。本文介绍了如何配置Pi-hole实现分离DNS：让tailnet客户端获取tailnet IP，局域网客户端获取局域网IP。

某些服务（如Nextcloud）客户端不支持额外认证，导致反向代理配置问题。作者曾通过地理封锁减少攻击面，但这限制了连接灵活性。通过在tailnet上实现分离DNS，可以避免这些问题，并有可能关闭广域网（WAN）访问，强制通过局域网或tailnet访问服务。

Pi-hole利用dnsmasq的分支pihole-FTL实现此功能，根据查询接口返回相应IP地址。这使得不同网络的客户端能获取适合其网络的地址。目前此功能仅支持IPv4。

主要讨论点：DNS和网络流量的管理和安全

不同观点：
• elashri：通过在路由器上设置Adguard Home和unbound，强制所有通过端口53的普通DNS请求使用本地DNS，并通过收集GitHub上的列表来阻止常见的DoH（DNS over HTTPS）地址。虽然这不是万无一失的解决方案，但在没有企业级网络设备和复杂的设置情况下，这是他能做到的最好的方法。

• dolmen：引用Tailscale的条款变更，指出Tailscale在2024年9月3日之后的新用户账户将受到Tailscale US Inc.的约束，这可能对隐私有影响，不同于之前加拿大公司的条款。

• leipert：提到Chromecasts会忽略本地DNS，并建议是否可以通过强制将8.8.8.8/8.8.4.4（特别是端口53）的流量重定向到PiHole来解决。

• udev4096：对IP范围允许规则的安全性提出疑问，询问是否可能通过伪造IP进行SSRF攻击，或者nginx是否能有效检测这种攻击。

• snvzz：使用headscale并选择通过VPN运行所有流量，包括局域网内的流量，以确保所有流量都是加密的，从而不必担心SMB等协议的明文传输问题。

补充讨论：
- 不同用户在处理DNS和流量加密时采取的不同策略，包括本地DNS设置、VPN全覆盖和使用自托管服务。
- 对Tailscale条款变更带来的隐私担忧，以及对不同网络设备和软件（如nginx）安全性的关注。
- 争议焦点在于如何有效管理和保护DNS请求及流量安全，特别是在面对现代复杂网络环境和应用的情况下。

44512470.article_content:
I've long had some form of VPN for my devices to use when I'm out and about.
Although I used to
run OpenVPN
, I moved to
Tailscale
a little while back. Tailscale builds a mesh network using
Wireguard
protocol and so is able to connect and run quite a bit faster than OpenVPN.
Side note: for those wondering, Tailscale is
Canadian
and can't see the content of connections (although if you're worried about this it's also possible to self-host using
Headscale
).
Although the tailnet has been up for some time, I hadn't got around to setting up split horizon DNS for clients on the tailnet. I was in a bit of a hurry when first setting up and so configured my reverse proxy box to advertise a route to it's own LAN IP.
This post talks about configuring my
Pi-hole
to implement a split horizon: returning the tailnet IP to tailnet clients and the LAN IP to LAN clients.
Splitting my Split Horizon
Many of the DNS names that I wanted to do this for
already
had a split horizon:
Clients on both the LAN and the wider internet connect to the same reverse proxy in my DMZ, but LAN clients connect using the proxy's local IP.
The reverse proxy fronts multiple services, most of which have authentication built in. However, it also requires that outside connections pass a separate (and valid) set of authentication credentials before it'll pass their connection on.
Having to authenticate twice is a little annoying though, and the split horizon makes it easy to disable the additional authentication when LAN clients connect:
satisfy any;
allow 192.168.3.0/24;
deny all;
auth_basic "Authenticate you must";
auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/wanaccess.htpasswd;
This extra authentication means that I'm not exposing any element of the backing service's authentication stack to the outside world. The underlying idea is that it
shouldn't matter
that there's an auth bypass zero day in (say) Grafana, because the wider world needs to get past my auth prompt before they can try to detect or exploit it.
You've Got Access: Why Make The Tailnet Special?
Given that there's an ability to access services via the WAN, you might be wondering why it is that I felt that I needed to do something specifically for the tailnet.
Unfortunately, the proxy
can't
enforce additional authentication for some services because those services clients don't support it.
Nextcloud
is a great example of this: the Nextcloud Desktop sync client authenticates with Nextcloud, but
It uses the
Authorization
header to present it's bearer token, so the reverse proxy will see an unexpected (and, to it, invalid) set of credentials
The client doesn't expose a way to add custom headers to the requests that it makes, so I can't simply send a shared secret and have the proxy check a different header
Having the reverse proxy require additional auth breaks off-net Nextcloud clients (and Nextcloud isn't the only service with this issue).
Geoblocking
Originally, I left the affected services accessible to the world.
Unfortunately, I
sometimes
seem to upset people enough to trigger prolonged attempts at compromising my services.
After
one such attempt
, I decided to reduce attack surface by
adding geo-blocking to my reverse proxy
, essentially restricting access to areas that I thought we'd be likely to connect from (or
at least
appear to).
This, of course, comes at a cost in flexibility, with access failing if any of the following are true:
We connected from an IP that doesn't have a location in the GeoDB (or is mislocated)
The ISP that we're connecting from does funky routing stuff and/or uses CGNAT
We've travelled somewhere that we wouldn't normally
Adding split horizon DNS to the tailnet allows me to avoid these scenarios, because the tailnet subnet can be special cased in
exactly
the same way that the LAN is.
It also increases the likelihood that I can close WAN access off and require that a client be on either the LAN or tailnet.
The Plan
The idea was that a tailnet client would also speak to the Pi-hole, but that names would resolve to a tailnet IP:
This is possible because Pi-hole is underpinned by a fork of
dnsmasq
called
pihole-FTL
which has inherited the setting
localise-queries
(in Pi-hole, this is enabled by default).
The
man page for dnsmasq
describes the setting as follows (line breaks mine):
Return answers to DNS queries from /etc/hosts and
--interface-name
and
--dynamic-host
which depend on the interface over which the query was received.
If a name has more than one address associated with it, and at least one of those addresses is on the same subnet as the interface to which the query was sent, then return only the address(es) on that subnet and return all the available addresses otherwise.
This allows for a server to have multiple addresses in /etc/hosts corresponding to each of its interfaces, and hosts will get the correct address based on which network they are attached to.
Currently this facility is limited to IPv4.
This means that we can create the following record set in
/etc/

data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 美国正致力于解决核废料问题。法国Orano公司在拉黑格的设施展示了通过先进技术回收和处理用过的核燃料，特别是将持久性强的放射性污泥转化为更稳定、危害较小的物质。这种方法不仅减少了核废料的体积，还降低了其长期放射性风险。研究人员利用创新化学工艺处理这些废物，目标是提高核能的可持续性和安全性，为应对气候变化提供更环保的能源选择。这一进展对全球核废料管理具有重要意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：核燃料循环与废料处理技术，包括钚回收、钍反应堆、以及各种核技术经济性和可行性

不同观点：
• **支持钚回收与MOX燃料**：mikewarot提到美国芝加哥附近的Dresden设施用于储存和处理废燃料，并提到历史上对钚回收的尝试。philipkglass则指出，钚回收制成MOX燃料在经济上并不吸引人，且美国曾因成本和进度问题取消了MOX工厂项目。

• **支持钍液态氟反应堆（LFTRs）**：greenavocado认为结合钍（Th-232）和钚（Pu）的燃料循环可以有效解决核废料问题，特别是LFTRs设计，可以燃烧钚废料并通过在线后处理系统维持核反应，且副产品U-233可以继续用于发电。

• **质疑与批评核废料处理的复杂性**：wffurr引用了一篇关于核燃料后处理风险的文章，带有些许讽刺意味。epistasis则对当前核能技术的经济性和过度乐观的态度提出质疑，认为核能技术成熟但缺乏突破，与太阳能和储能技术相比显得不具优势。

• **对不同技术的混淆与疑问**：yk对文章中提到的嬗变和再处理技术之间的区别感到困惑，不清楚具体的目标是减少废料的半衰期还是重新利用燃料。Synaesthesia则询问钍反应堆是否能解决核废料问题。

• **支持可再生能源的替代方案**：lucidguppy认为应更多关注太阳能和电池储能技术，认为这些技术才能真正解决问题。

• **对未来技术的乐观期待**：eagerpace认为可以将核废料储存直到未来技术成熟，甚至提出在月球轨道上处理废料的可能性。

补充讨论：
• **对特定同位素应用的讨论**：vavooom提到从核废料中分离出的锶-90同位素在医疗和工程领域的应用潜力，并引用了维基百科的相关内容。

• **对技术实现的质疑**：mathgradthrow对中子束技术如何实现表示困惑，暗示对某些技术方案可行性的怀疑。

总体来看，讨论围绕核废料处理的不同技术路线展开，包括钚回收、钍反应堆、以及可再生能源替代方案等，并涉及技术经济性、可行性和未来潜力等多个方面。争议焦点在于现有核技术的实际效益与未来技术突破的可能性。

data.title: Desktop Publishing Tools That Didn't Make It (2022)
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
本文回顾了20世纪80年代桌面出版软件的早期创新，重点介绍了10款可能被遗忘的软件。桌面出版曾在印刷行业引发革命，尽管随着印刷媒介的衰落，它显得有些过时，但每天仍有大量内容被排版。许多早期工具未能存活至今，包括一些具有开创性但未成功的平台和软件。

1. **Xerox Alto**：虽然严格来说不是专门的桌面出版平台，但其图形用户界面和排版功能启发了后来的Macintosh和桌面出版概念。
2. **The Book Machine**：基于Sirius微型计算机，专为排版设计，但价格昂贵，目标客户是专业技术作者，最终未广泛普及。
3. **MacPublisher**：在PageMaker之前推出，是Mac上早期的桌面出版工具，但不如后者成熟和知名。

这些早期工具展示了桌面出版的演变，尽管许多未能成功，但它们为现代出版技术奠定了基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：桌面出版（DTP）软件的历史和不同软件工具的回忆

不同观点：
• **taeric**：对文章中提到的Print Shop感到怀念，尤其是其标志性的横幅打印功能，引发了对过去使用类似软件的回忆。
• **WillAdams**：补充了一些未被文章提到的DTP软件，如Calamus、Ready-Set-Go、Microsoft Publisher等，并指出列举PageMaker有些不妥，因为其继任者InDesign已经取代了它。
• **Brajeshwar**：认为PageMaker并非失败，而是与QuarkXPress竞争激烈，并表示PageMaker曾为其教育和收入来源做出贡献。
• **jamesgill**：认同PageMaker在80年代和90年代的流行，并提到自己曾使用GeoPublish在Commodore电脑上进行DTP工作。
• **kstrauser**：分享了其在高中时使用PageSetter的经历，尽管软件有崩溃问题，但仍能制作出相当专业的文档，认为DTP在当时是革命性的。
• **wduquette**：纠正文章中对"Sirius microcomputer"的误称，实际应为Victor 9000，并详细介绍了该机器的规格和历史背景。
• **egypturnash**：指出文章中对"The Newsroom"软件平台描述的错误，并分享了自己使用Print Shop的经历。
• **leakycap**：提到UniQorn这个基于Apple QuickDraw GX的DTP应用，并指出其部分功能在Softpress Freeway中得以延续。
• **xp84**：希望看到对ReadySetGo的提及，这是一个由Letraset发布的DTP程序，并分享了自己家庭使用该软件的经历。
• **cormullion**：提到Interleaf的兴衰，特别指出其使用Common Lisp编写用户界面的独特之处。
• **paradox460**：对文章未提及lighthouse designs software和STONEworks感到遗憾，认为这些工具对NeXT和早期Mac OS X用户非常重要。
• **ornel**：分享了其父亲在80年代使用Ventura Publisher设立出版公司的经历，并提到使用Corel Paint和GEM的回忆。
• **pstuart**：回忆使用QuarkXPress、Ventura Publisher和PageMaker的经历，并提到Mac上的Word 4.0也能满足基本出版需求。
• **asplake**：惊讶于FrameMaker仍然存在，并询问现在谁在使用它。
• **insane_dreamer**：认为PageMaker很棒，并最终演变为InDesign，这是一种卓越的进步。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：PageMaker是否为失败产品。Brajeshwar认为其与QuarkXPress竞争激烈且有实际贡献，而WillAdams则认为列举PageMaker不妥，因其已被InDesign取代。
• 提到的其他DTP软件：Calamus、Ready-Set-Go、Microsoft Publisher、UniQorn、Interleaf、lighthouse designs software、STONEworks等，展示了DTP领域的多样性和不同工具的用户基础。
• 对历史细节的纠正：wduquette对"Sirius microcomputer"名称的纠正，以及egypturnash对"The Newsroom"软件平台描述的修正，显示了对历史准确性的关注。

Today in Tedium:
It’s easy to forget now, but desktop publishing was an immensely innovative thing when it emerged within the computing industry in the early ’80s. While at its heart a mishmash of hardware and software cleverly combined for a single goal, it was an empire builder, one that helped create new businesses and improve the status and positioning of existing ones. And with the decline of print as a medium, it can feel kind of old hat, but lots of stuff still gets typeset every single day. And while we’ve landed on a few standards, a lot of desktop publishing tools failed to make to it the present day. So in a continuation of our list of
things that didn’t make it
, Today’s Tedium takes a look at 10 early examples of desktop publishing software that you probably don’t remember desktop publishing was a killer app nearly 40 years ago and you were in diapers back then … if you existed at all. (Oh yeah,
quick reminder
of what makes things obscure, from our point of view.)
— Ernie @ Tedium
Find your next favorite newsletter with The Sample
Each morning,
The Sample
sends you one article from a random blog or newsletter that matches up with your interests. When you get one you like, you can subscribe to the writer with one click.
Sign up over this way
.
Today’s Tedium is sponsored by The Sample. (
See yourself here?
)
1. Xerox Alto
Platform:
Groundbreaking-but-failed computer platform that inspired the GUI-based world in which we live
Era:
Mid-’70s
Target audience:
Theoretical
This one is likely going to be controversial with someone, which I fully admit is true. It
is
controversial. But that doesn’t mean it’s necessarily wrong.
Looking at the Xerox Alto, the computer that inspired Apple to create the Macintosh, as a machine that could be used to lay out and publish things might to some degree fudge the “desktop publishing” definition for some, but the case for it is pretty strong. First, one only has to point to Xerox’s legacy in copiers and printers as being compatible with the needs of a publisher.
Additionally, computer historians who have researched this stuff in-depth, such as Ken Shirriff, have convincingly made the argument that the Alto represented a desktop publishing platform before desktop publishing was given that name, citing the fact that the handbook for the computer was actually laid out using the computer, the Alto’s typography capabilities, and that the publishing tools were commercialized, albeit poorly.
“The Macintosh owes everything from the WYSIWYG editor and spline-based fonts to the bitmapped display and laser printer to the Xerox Alto,”
Shirriff wrote on his blog in 2017
. “Of course, Steve Jobs deserves great credit for making desktop publishing common and affordable with the Macintosh and the LaserWriter, something Xerox failed to do with the Xerox Star, an expensive ($75,000) system that commercialized the Alto’s technology.”
If it’s good enough an argument for Ken Shirriff, it’s good enough for me.
An example of The Book Machine, as shown in
a 1983 issue of Practical Computing
.
2. The Book Machine
Platform:
Dedicated machine based on Sirius microcomputer
Era:
Mid-’80s
Target audience:
Professional
One of the earliest examples of a computer built around typesetting, this machine, produced by Prefis, could capably set type on a page at sizes between 6 points and 48 points, in a variety of forms—including paragraph and headline sizes. It produced disks capable of managing phototypesetting tools without needing any additional steps, meaning its use case was working with existing phototypesetting technology rather than its own separate thing like many DTP tools of the era were.
It was ambitious, but you very much paid for that ambition. At the time, it went for £5,980, roughly $8,000 based on exchange rates of the time—and £17,363 today ($19,129). Not cheap, especially for a machine dedicated to typesetting.
In a 1984 piece in the
FID News Bulletin
, the outlet tried to make sense of who the audience might be for such a tool, and came up with this:
So who will use the Book Machine? It is after all a do-it-yourself composition system and most authors restrict their role to writing and leave composition to printers. The answer Prefis believes is that there are many authors of technical and educational material who would prefer to format and arrange their own material.
This turned out to be correct! But they didn’t use the Book Machine, a non-WYSIWYG desktop publishing tool, to do it.
3. MacPublisher
Platform:
MacOS
Era:
1984-1986
Target audience:
Professional
Released just before the far-better-known PageMaker,
this early tool
was one of the first software-based desktop publishing tools for the Mac, being released a year before PageMaker and anticipating the interest in such a technology on the market. While nowhere near as polished as many later tool

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了发生在雷暴上方的神秘大气放电现象，包括红色精灵（red sprites）、绿色幽灵（green ghosts）和蓝色喷流（blue jets）。这些现象属于瞬态发光事件（TLEs），由雷暴产生的强大电场引发，通常发生在距地50至90公里的高空。红色精灵是最常见的TLEs，由正极闪电触发，呈现为短暂的红光，形状如同根系或水母。2022年，摄影师在青藏高原捕捉到105个红色精灵，并记录到罕见的喷流和幽灵现象。科学家正通过结合业余观测和专业研究，努力理解这些现象的成因及其与地球天气系统的关联。这些研究不仅满足了科学好奇心，还有助于更好地理解地面上的风暴系统。

44480363.article_content:
SCIENCE
The most otherworldly, mysterious forms of lightning on Earth
Scientists are working to understand the curious phenomena of red sprites, green ghosts and blue jets high above thunderstorms.
Red spites, a type of transient luminous event or TLE, appear in the upper atmosphere above a thunderstorm in Oklahoma in April 2025.
By
Isabel Swafford
Photographs by
Paul M Smith
June 26, 2025
Our atmosphere is like one big electrical circuit: Thunderstorms are the batteries that charge it up, and lightning is the current flowing through it. On the ground we see evidence of this circuit when lightning cracks and strikes the ground, or when it lights up deep inside a thundercloud, but high above the clouds lies a secret electrical zoo full of sprites, elves, and jets.
These fantastical terms refer to light displays called transient luminous events or TLEs that occur in Earth’s upper atmosphere during thunderstorms. “TLEs are mysterious, beautiful, and uniquely different from conventional lightning, yet they connect weather, space, and electricity in one dramatic moment. They occur high above the clouds, almost silently, and are invisible to most people—but they reflect powerful processes unfolding deep within thunderstorms,” says Hailiang Huang, a Ph.D. student at the University of Science and Technology of China who studies TLEs.
The very first photographic observations of these events in 1989 captured red flashes streaking across the sky in the blink of an eye. The displays were dubbed red sprites, inspired by characters in Shakespeare’s
A Midsummer Night’s Dream
, and a medley of other fairytale names followed, as researchers discovered new types of TLEs. Today, scientists are still working to understand these curious phenomena—what causes them, how often they happen, and what they can tell us about Earth’s atmosphere.
Red sprites, like these captured in December 2024 in Mississippi, are by far the most common TLE observed by both researchers and photographers.
A photographer snapped this image of red sprite lightning in June 2023 in Kansas. Some have described the flashes as looking like carrots or jellyfish.
What exactly are red sprites?
Just like storm chasing, some photographers have taken to sprite chasing, searching for elusive red sprites and other TLEs above nighttime thunderstorms.
(
See rare colorful lightning sprites dance above a hurricane
.)
Red sprites have been observed off the coast of Europe and over the U.S. Great Plains, but in 2022, astrophotographers Angel An and Shuchang Dong captured 105 red sprites, the largest number ever seen in a single thunderstorm in South Asia,
researchers recently
reported in the journal
Advances in Atmospheric Science
.
4th of July Sale - 25% OFF!
Magazine for all ages starting at $25/year
SEE SUBSCRIPTION OPTIONS
“Red sprites are the most iconic [of TLEs],” says Huang, the lead author of the paper.
They flash into existence for just a fraction of a second in a spindly root-like system of red streaks. The phenomenon is caused by positive lightning that strikes the ground, creating an electric field that reaches up into the atmosphere, about 50 to 90 kilometers above Earth.
On the Tibetan Plateau, north of the Himalayas, thunderstorms are very common. The dramatic changes in elevation produce intense convection in the atmosphere and the churning of wet air creates clouds—a rich laboratory for studying TLEs. Yet none had been recorded there until An and Dong’s storm imagery in 2022.
Huang and his collaborator
Gaopeng Lu
, an atmospheric physicist at the University of Science and Technology of China, developed a method to synchronize the videos and photos that An and Dong took on the Tibetan Plateau. Using satellite data and maps of the stars in the night sky to determine the timestamps of each video frame, the team linked around 70 percent of verified sprites to the parent lightning that triggered them.
To Huang, the results demonstrate the scientific value of amateur observations. “It’s exciting that this field brings together professional scientists and passionate amateurs, working side by side to understand something so ephemeral, yet so profound.”
Not only did the photographers capture a significant number of red sprites, the Himalayan storm also featured even rarer TLEs called jets and ghosts. The team found 16 secondary jets, powerful columns of often blue or purple light darting upwards into the sky, and at least four
ghosts
, green hazy glows that can sometimes hover above red sprites.
“While sprites [and other TLEs] may appear delicate and silent in the upper atmosphere, they are often linked to powerful, sometimes devastating weather systems,” says Huang. “Understanding them not only satisfies our curiosity about the upper atmosphere, but also helps us learn more about the storms we face here on Earth.”

data.title: Let Kids Be Loud
data.author: trevin
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了关于儿童户外玩耍噪音的争议，特别是在阿姆斯特丹的一个社区足球笼案例中，一些居民抱怨孩子玩耍太吵，要求缩小场地，但法院最终支持保留足球笼。阿姆斯特丹体育委员会随后发布报告，指出儿童玩耍的声音是“自然、欢迎且不可避免的”，建议修改地方法规，防止因噪音投诉而关闭游乐场。文章还提到全球其他城市类似的噪音投诉案例，如多伦多、温哥华、卡尔加里、德州和伦敦等地，反映出对儿童玩耍噪音的容忍度下降。专家认为，这种 intolerance 与人口老龄化有关，因为较少接触孩子噪音的人更易感到被打扰。文章强调，玩耍对孩子至关重要且必然伴随噪音，不应将这种声音视为污染，而应视为健康社区的一部分。同时，过度依赖安静的屏幕娱乐对孩子的发展有害。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社区中儿童噪音问题及其社会文化背景

不同观点：
• **对儿童噪音的包容性**：
  - [petercooper] 认为社区文化中的日常噪音（如教堂钟声、儿童玩耍、冰淇淋车音乐）是正常现象，禁止这些噪音是一种危险趋势。
  - [ysavir] 也表达了类似观点，认为儿童的玩耍噪音是健康和有趣的，相比之下，机械工具的噪音更令人讨厌。
  - [dpifke] 分享了一个正面例子，表示喜欢听到邻居孩子练习乐器，即使起初不太好听。

• **对噪音的限制与边界**：
  - [BrenBarn] 认为父母应为孩子的活动设置界限，不应让孩子的噪音在任何场合都不受限制，特别是在公共场合如商店等。
  - [pizzafeelsright] 强调在特定场合如电影院或餐馆，儿童应保持安静，以不影响他人为前提。
  - [airstrike] 进一步指出，公共场合和私人场合的噪音标准应有所不同，儿童在公共场合应保持适当音量。

• **文化差异与社会变迁**：
  - [rock_artist] 指出不同国家和文化对儿童噪音的接受程度不同，移民和文化差异使得这个问题更加复杂。
  - [voxleone] 提出社会对儿童噪音的容忍度增加可能与出生率下降和儿童在社会中的象征价值增加有关。

• **个人体验与特殊情况**：
  - [bartread] 分享了个别儿童持续尖叫导致困扰的例子，认为虽然大多数儿童噪音可以容忍，但极端情况仍需处理。
  - [Aurornis] 质疑是否真有“趋势”存在，认为互联网上收集的个别故事不能代表整体社会现象。
  - [Apreche] 自述可能有噪音敏感症，希望儿童噪音不要在自己附近发生。

补充讨论：
- **对儿童噪音的健康影响**：
  - [didibus] 提出是否存在科学证据证明儿童噪音对成人健康的影响，这可能是一个值得研究的领域。
  
- **对儿童户外活动的期望**：
  - [GuinansEyebrows] 回顾过去儿童在户外活动的普遍性，希望社会能重新认识到让儿童参与社会互动的重要性。

争议焦点：
- **儿童噪音的合理界限**：不同评论者在儿童噪音的可接受程度和场合上存在分歧，部分人强调需要设置界限，而另一些人则认为应更加包容。
- **文化差异的影响**：在不同文化背景下，对儿童噪音的接受程度和处理方式存在显著差异，这也引发了对全球趋势讨论的质疑。

总体而言，讨论的核心在于如何平衡儿童的正常活动噪音与社区中其他成员的需求和期望。

In Defense of Outdoor Play
Katherine Johnson Martinko
Jul 09, 2025

Source: Shutterstock
There was a heated debate in Amsterdam recently over whether children should be allowed to continue playing inside a neighborhood soccer cage. Some residents complained that it was too noisy and demanded the cage be reduced in size. Others argued that the noise of children playing was normal and healthy, and the case should stay as is. The case went to court, and the supporters won out. The cage stayed.
Following the decision, Amsterdam’s sports advisory council, the Sportraad,
published a report
stating that the sound of children playing should not be considered a nuisance. It called the noise a “natural, welcome, and unavoidable part of life,” and recommended that bylaws be changed so that “the sound of playing children was no longer a valid reason for complaint by vexed neighbours.” Doing so would help prevent playground closures due to complaints (
via The Guardian
).
This is welcome news to any parent. Raising kids is hard enough, but it’s even harder when you’re a parent who is trying to reduce a child’s screen time, increase their hours of outdoor play, and somehow
keep them quiet
at the same time. That can feel like a near impossibility, particularly in urban settings where homes are clustered near parks, and where small outdoor spaces are shared by kids of all ages.
Subscribe
This Is Not Just Amsterdam
Noise complaints about kids playing outdoors are becoming all too frequent. A Toronto mother
received an anonymous letter
telling her to “correct” her four sons for screaming and to keep them constantly supervised or take them to the park. In Vancouver, a popular playground slide was removed after neighbors
complained
it was too loud. In Calgary, a man installed a chirping alarm that went off every time the kids next door whooped or shouted in their own backyard. The kids’ mother
told a news reporter
, “I thought it was an annoying bird, and it wasn’t until we were out in the back that I realized it was when the kids were just playing.”
In Texas, a family was
sued by neighbors
who said the noise from their four kids playing in a backyard playhouse violated their “tranquil quality of life.” In Long Island, parents were
cited
for violating a noise ordinance because their daughters squealed while swimming in a pool. That summons was later dismissed, but the message was clear: your children’s joy is a problem.
Cities across North America and the UK have
restricted
street
sports
, citing noise, “
probable harm
,” and safety concerns. In Mississauga, Canada, officials
upheld a ban
on all street play. In the UK, London has more than 7,000 signs
forbidding ball games
across
housing estates, limiting the movement and activity of an estimated half a million children, despite nearly 53% of British kids failing to meet the recommended 60 minutes of daily exercise. The list goes on.
Understanding the Trend
Several years ago, the
New York Times
reported
on rising hostility toward child play noise in Japan. There’s even a crowdsourced website where people log complaints about “neighborhoods inhabited by stupid parents who let their children play on roads and parking lots.” Experts believe this growing intolerance reflects the country’s aging population. As one demographer put it, “fewer children makes people less accustomed to hearing the noise they naturally make,” which
leads
to more complaints, discourages families from having children, and reinforces a vicious cycle of demographic decline.
It’s easy to become annoyed by noise if you don’t spend time around children. When most kids are indoors, in cars, or in structured activities, and when fewer adults live near families, even ordinary sounds of outdoor play can feel disruptive.
But play is
essential
, and play is loud. Kids yelp, squeal, cheer, chant, and crash into things. That’s how they express joy, test boundaries, and connect with one another. Trying to suppress that energy by demanding silence or defaulting to screens is
damaging
.
Of course, there’s a difference between regular noisy play and gratuitous screaming, which parents should minimize. Reasonable rules are fair: no shouting early in the morning or late at night. But adults also need to recalibrate. The sound of children playing should not be treated as pollution. It is the sound of a healthy, functioning community.
Whether we want to admit it or not, many adults still cling to the old idea that “children should be seen, not heard.” That’s part of why screen-based entertainment has taken over. It’s quiet. It’s controlled. It keeps kids docile. But quiet does not mean well. A child staring at a tablet may seem calm, but it often comes at the
cost
of physical, emotional, and social development.
We don’t treat adult nois
44513801.article_summary: 文章讨论了关于儿童户外玩耍噪音的争议，特别是在阿姆斯特丹的一个社区足球笼案例中，一些居民抱怨孩子玩耍太吵，要求缩小场地，但法院最终支持保留足球笼。阿姆斯特丹体育委员会随后发布报告，指出儿童玩耍的声音是“自然、欢迎且不可避免的”，建议修改地方法规，防止因噪音投诉而关闭游乐场。文章还提到全球其他城市类似的噪音投诉案例，如多伦多、温哥华、卡尔加里、德州和伦敦等地，反映出对儿童玩耍噪音的容忍度下降。专家认为，这种 intolerance 与人口老龄化有关，因为较少接触孩子噪音的人更易感到被打扰。文章强调，玩耍对孩子至关重要且必然伴随噪音，不应将这种声音视为污染，而应视为健康社区的一部分。同时，过度依赖安静的屏幕娱乐对孩子的发展有害。

不同观点：

• [tezza] 分享了个人在使用Lovable/Bolt进行开发时的负面体验，指出其在修复过程中出现的循环故障问题（"doom loop"），每次修复都会引发之前的故障，质疑其稳定性和实用性。

• [transformi] 认为原文像广告，并推荐了一个开源的替代方案Daytona，提供了一个GitHub链接以供参考，显示了对原文内容的不信任以及对开源替代方案的偏好。

• [wyxuan] 提出Bolt/StackBlitz的初衷是通过WebAssembly在客户端运行Node.js以实现轻量化，但质疑其是否已经转向更依赖服务器端的模型，显示了对技术演进方向的关注。

• [bnchrch] 表达了对"sandboxing"解决方案的寻求，指出自行设置的难度，并提到Beam作为一个接近理想的产品但仍不完美，显示了对实用工具的迫切需求。

• 讨论中涉及多个技术工具和框架，包括FastMCP、Lovable/Bolt、Daytona和Beam，用户对这些工具的实际效果和应用场景存在不同看法。

data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在实现大规模正则表达式匹配时遇到的性能问题，特别是使用非确定性有限自动机（NFA）处理ε-转换的复杂性。作者解释了NFA中的ε-闭包概念，即在某些状态下无需输入符号即可进行的转换，这对于处理如"?"、"*"等正则表达式符号是必要的。文章详细描述了如何通过ε-闭包遍历NFA以匹配输入字符串，并指出了在处理复杂正则表达式（如包含循环的表达式）时可能遇到的无限循环和重复状态问题。作者建议通过记录遍历路径或使用哈希表来避免这些问题。文章还提到了Thompson’s construction方法，并推荐了Russ Cox的相关文章作为进一步阅读。

44514559.article_content:
QRS: Epsilon Wrangling
Search
I haven’t shipped any new features for
Quamina
in many months, partly due to a flow of real-life distractions, but
also I’m up against tough performance problems in implementing
Regular Expressions at massive scale
.
I’m still looking for a breakthrough, but have learned things about building and executing finite automata
that I think are worth sharing. This piece has to do with
epsilons
; anyone who has studied
finite automata will know about them already, but I’ll offer background for those people to skip.
I’ve written about this before in
Epsilon Love
. A commenter pointed out that the definition of “epsilon”
in that piece is not quite right per standard finite-automata theory, but it’s still a useful in that it describes how
epsilons support constructs like the shell-style “
*
”.
Background
·
Finite automata come in two flavors: Deterministic (DFA) and Nondeterministic (NFA).  DFAs move from state to state one input
symbol at a time: it’s simple and easy to understand and to implement.
NFAs have two distinguishing characteristics: First, when you’re in a
state and an input symbol arrives, you can transfer to more than one other state. Second, a state can have “epsilon transitions”
(let’s say “ε” for epsilon), which can happen any time at all while you’re in that state, input or no input.
NFAs are more complicated to traverse (will discuss below) but you need them if you want to
implement regular expressions with
.
and
?
and
*
and so on. You can turn any NFA into a
DFA, and I’ll come back to that subject in a future piece.
For implementing NFAs, I’ve been using
Thompson's construction
, where
“Thompson” is
Ken Thompson
, co-parent of Unix. This technique is also nicely
described by Russ Cox in
Regular Expression Matching Can Be Simple And Fast
. You don’t need to
learn it to understand this piece, but I’ll justify design
choices by saying “per Thompson”.
I’m going to discuss two specific issues today, ε-closures and a simpler NFA definition.
ε-closures
·
To set the stage, consider this regexp:
A?B?C?X
It should match “X” and “BX” and “ACX” and so on, but not “CAX” or “XX”.
Thompson says that you implement
A?
with a
transition to the next state on “A” and another ε-transition to that next state; because if you see an “A” you should transition,
but then you can transition anyhow even if you don’t.
The resulting NFA looks like this:
In finite-automaton
math, states are usually represented by the letter “q” followed by a number (usually italicized and subscripted, like
q
0
, but not here, sorry). Note
q4
’s double circle which means it’s
a goal state, i.e. if we get here we’ve matched the regexp.
I should add that this was produced with
draw.io
, which seems to make this sort of thing easy.
Back to that NFA
·
So, here’s a challenge: Sketch out the traversal code in your head. Think about the input strings “AX” and “BCX” and just “X”
and how you’d get through the NFA to the Q4 goal state.
The trick is what’s called the ε-closure. When you get to a state, before you look at the next input symbol, you have to set
up to process it. In this case, you need to be able to transition on an A or B or C. So what you do is pull together the
start state
q0
and also any other states you can reach from there through ε-transitions. In this case, the ε-closure
for the start state is
{q0, q1, q2, q3}
.
Suppose, then, that you see a “B” input symbol. You apply it to all the states in the ε-closure. Only
q1
matches,
transitioning you to
q2
. Before you look at the next input symbol, you compute the ε-closure for
q2
, which turns
out to be
{q2, q3}
. With this ε-closure, you can match “C” or “X”. If you get a “C”, you”ll step to
q3
, whose ε-closure is just itself, because “X” is the only path forward.
So your NFA-traversal algorithm for one step becomes something like:
Start with a list of states.
Compute the ε-closure of that that list.
Read an input symbol.
For each state in the ε-closure, see if you can traverse to another state.
If so, add it to your output list of states.
When you’re done, your output list of states is the input to this algorithm for the next step.
Computation issues
·
Suppose your regular expression is
(A+BC?)+
. I’m not going to sketch out the NFA, but just looking at it tells
you that it has to have loopbacks; once you’ve matched the parenthetized chunk you need to go back to a state where you can
recognize another occurrence.
For this regexp’s NFA, computing the ε-closures can lead you into an infinite loop. (Should be obvious, but I didn’t realize it until
after the first time it happened.)
You can have loops and you can also have dupes. In practice, it’s not that uncommon for a state to have more than one
ε-transition, and for the targets of these transitions to overlap.
So you need to watch for loops and to dedupe your output. I think the only way to avoid this is with a cookie-crumbs
“where I’ve been” trail, either as a list or a hash table.

data.title: TaIrTe₄ photodetectors show promise for sensitive room-temperature THz sensing
data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了基于拓扑半金属TaIrTe₄的新型太赫兹（THz）光电探测器，该探测器在室温下具有高灵敏度、快速响应和宽频带等优势。传统的THz探测器存在速度慢、灵敏度低或频率范围有限等问题，而TaIrTe₄材料展现出强大的非线性霍尔效应，使其在THz探测中表现优异。研究团队通过飞秒激光产生的THz脉冲测量了该探测器的内在响应速度，并利用二次谐波生成（SHG）光谱技术研究了材料的晶体对称性和低温下的电子相变，进一步提升了其THz响应能力。实验显示，该探测器在室温下具有高响应度（~0.3 A/W）、超低噪声等效功率（~ pW/Hz^(1/2)）、宽频带响应（0.1至10 THz）和快速响应（~皮秒级）。当材料进入关联电荷有序态时，零偏置响应度可提升约50倍（~18 A/W）。这一研究为THz传感技术的进步提供了新途径。

Terahertz radiation (THz), electromagnetic radiation with frequencies ranging between 0.1 and 10 THz, could be leveraged to develop various new technologies, including imaging and communication systems. So far, however, a lack of fast and sensitive detectors that can detect radiation across a wide range of frequencies has limited the development of these THz-sensing technologies.
In a recent paper
published
in
Nature Electronics
, researchers at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the University of Tennessee and other institutes have introduced new photodetectors made of tantalum iridium telluride (TaIrTe₄), a 2D-correlated topological semimetal that exhibits advantageous properties. Most notably, this material exhibits a strong nonlinear Hall effect, a physical effect that entails a transverse voltage in the absence of an external magnetic field, which is nonlinearly proportional to an applied electric field or current.
"THz technology is critical in
quantum information technology
and biomedical sensing because its frequency resonates with low-energy collective excitations in quantum materials and molecular vibrations in biological matters," Jun Xiao, senior author of the paper, told Phys.org.
"Moreover, the ultra-high bandwidth of the THz band could enable desired high-speed wireless communication. However, the widespread application of THz technologies has been hindered due to the lack of simultaneous sensitive, broadband, and fast THz detection in state-of-the-art detectors such as thermal bolometers and electronic Schottky diodes."
Existing photodetectors capable of detecting THz radiation are either too slow, not sensitive enough, or only capable of detecting signals at some frequencies. Xiao and his colleagues thus set out to develop new photodetectors based on alternative materials, which could overcome the limitations of previously developed devices, exhibiting good sensitivity, fast speeds and broadband.
"We fabricated Har bar geometry sensing devices using atomically thin TaIrTe₄, a 2D-correlated topological semimetal, and exposed them to terahertz (THz) radiation," explained Xiao. "We characterized this effect by measuring THz-induced photocurrent and evaluating device performance metrics such as responsivity and sensitivity. To assess the response speed, we conducted ultrafast autocorrelation measurements using femtosecond laser-generated THz pulses, revealing intrinsic picosecond-scale dynamics."
As part of their study, Xiao and his colleagues also probed the crystal symmetry of TaIrTe₄ using a technique known as second-harmonic generation (SHG) spectroscopy. Using this technique, they observed the emergence of a correlated electronic phase at low temperatures that further enhanced their photodetectors' THz response, or in other words, improved their ability to quickly and precisely detect THz radiation.
"Additionally, we demonstrated that the sensing performance and electronic state could be tuned via electrostatic gating," said Xiao. "These combined methods revealed TaIrTe₄'s promise for fast, broadband, and highly sensitive room-temperature THz sensing."
In initial tests, the photodetectors developed by this team of researchers were found to perform remarkably well. At room temperature, they attained a large zero-bias responsivity (~ 0.3 A/W), ultralow NEP (~ pW/Hz
1/2
), broadband THz response (0.1 to 10 THz) and ultrafast intrinsic speed (~ ps).

data.title: Fun with flags: How Compilers Break and Fix Constant-Time Code
data.author: belter
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了编译器优化如何破坏常量时间代码（constant-time code），从而导致计时侧信道攻击的风险。尽管开发人员使用常量时间编程来防止此类攻击，但编译器的优化可能无意中重新引入泄漏。作者通过分析GCC和LLVM编译器，识别出导致泄漏的具体优化过程，发现少数优化过程是泄漏的主要原因。基于此，作者提出通过禁用特定编译器标志来减轻泄漏，而无需修改源代码或定制编译器。该方法显著减少了泄漏，且性能开销极小，为开发人员提供了一种实用的防御手段。

Title:
Fun with flags: How Compilers Break and Fix Constant-Time Code
Authors:
Antoine Geimer
,
Clementine Maurice
View a PDF of the paper titled Fun with flags: How Compilers Break and Fix Constant-Time Code, by Antoine Geimer and Clementine Maurice
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Developers rely on constant-time programming to prevent timing side-channel attacks. But these efforts can be undone by compilers, whose optimizations may silently reintroduce leaks. While recent works have measured the extent of such leakage, they leave developers without actionable insights: which optimization passes are responsible, and how to disable them without modifying the compiler remains unclear.
In this paper, we conduct a qualitative analysis of how compiler optimizations break constant-time code. We construct a dataset of compiler-introduced constant-time violations and analyze the internals of two widely used compilers, GCC and LLVM, to identify the specific optimization passes responsible. Our key insight is that a small set of passes are at the root of most leaks. To the best of our knowledge, we are also the first to characterize how the interactions between these passes contribute to leakage. Based on this analysis, we propose an original and practical mitigation that requires no source code modification or custom compiler: disabling selected optimization passes via compiler flags. We show that this approach significantly reduces leakage with minimal performance overhead, offering an immediately deployable defense for developers.

We believe curiosity is a superpower. It’s the spark that propels humanity forward. Yet, the web—our greatest source of information—was never designed to nurture curiosity; instead we’ve been asked to “browse” it through a one-way lens. That’s why we made Comet.

Comet learns how you think, collaborates in your research, and keeps your digital life organized—so you’re never lost in tabs or forget what inspired you. Start a project, follow a new idea, or revisit an old one—and Comet adapts in real time, surfacing what you need before you even know you need it. With privacy as a foundation and usability as a promise, Comet is built to make every interaction smoother, smarter, and custom-fit to how you think and work. data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 加州在截至2024年9月30日的12个月内，地下蓄水层增加了约220万英亩-英尺的地下水，这一增长显著，但低于2023年极为湿润水年期间的870万英亩-英尺。尽管实施了节水计划和法规，中央谷地的农业抽水仍持续消耗大量地下水。州政府通过LandFlex计划提供2330万美元资助，帮助减少抽水并引导洪水补给地下水，已节省超过10万英亩-英尺的水。此外，州长纽森支持建设201亿美元的三角洲输水项目以现代化水基础设施，但该项目引发激烈争论。支持者认为项目能确保供水可靠性，反对者则担心生态影响和成本增加。
