The amount of groundwater replenishment was significant, but was less than the amount that percolated underground during the extremely wet 2023 water year.
A year of average precipitation gave California’s groundwater supplies a significant boost, according to a state analysis released Tuesday.
California’s aquifers gained an estimated 2.2 million acre-feet of groundwater in the 12 months that ended Sept. 30, the state’s 2024 water year. That’s about half the storage capacity of Shasta Lake, California’s largest reservoir.
State officials said local agencies reported that about 1.9 million acre-feet of water went underground as a result of managed aquifer recharge projects designed to capture stormwater and replenish groundwater.
The boost to underground supplies occurred while the state is implementing water-saving programs and regulations intended to help curb
chronic overpumping
in farming areas in the Central Valley.
Advertisement
The amount of groundwater replenishment during the 2024 water year
,
while significant, was less than the 8.7 million acre-feet that percolated underground during the extremely wet 2023 water year, according to
state estimates
.
Even as California has sought to capture more stormwater to recharge groundwater, pumping to provide for agriculture has continued drawing on underground supplies.
The groundwater report, prepared by the state Department of Water Resources, said about 11.5 million acre-feet of groundwater was pumped across 98 basins, based on data from local agencies that submitted annual reports. That was up from 9.7 million acre-feet reported during the previous year.
Climate & Environment
A decade after signing of California groundwater law, major challenges remain
Ten years ago, California adopted a law to curb chronic overpumping of groundwater. Significant challenges remain, even as the state works toward its goals.
Sept. 17, 2024
The Central Valley accounted for more than 84% of groundwater extraction statewide, and most of that water was used to supply the valley’s farmlands.
Gov. Gavin Newsom said California is collecting more groundwater data than it has previously, and is continuing to prioritize efforts to recharge aquifers. He said, however, that the state’s water infrastructure is unprepared for the effects of climate change, and he reiterated his support for building a water tunnel beneath the Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta.
“We’re done with barriers,” Newsom said in a statement. “We must modernize our water infrastructure.”
Advertisement
The proposed Delta Conveyance Project, with an estimated price tag of $20.1 billion, has
generated heated debate
. Supporters say the proposed project is essential to modernizing the state’s water infrastructure and maintaining the reliability of supplies from the State Water Project. Opponents say it would unnecessarily harm the Delta’s deteriorating ecosystem, threaten fish species and lead to significantly higher water costs for the public.
As they released the figures, state officials said efforts to address groundwater overpumping have been helped by a state program called LandFlex, which has provided $23.3 million in grants to local groundwater agencies, enabling dozens of small and midsize farms to take steps to bolster groundwater levels.
According to state estimates, the program has helped save more than 100,000 acre-feet of groundwater by reducing pumping. The Department of Water Resources said the program has also helped in redirecting floodwaters onto fallowed farmland to recharge groundwater.
Department Director Karla Nemeth called it a “climate-resilient solution” for local water management agencies as well as farmers.

补充讨论：
• OpenAI构建浏览器的动机，可能不仅是为了用户体验控制，还包括在技术竞争中给对手制造压力。
• 争议焦点在于专有浏览器的正当性，以及OpenAI是否能在浏览器市场中取得实质性突破。
• 技术实现方式（如是否基于现有开源项目）也是一个讨论点，反映出行业内常见策略的影响。

data.title: A simple monthly injection allows mice to live 25% longer and free from diseases
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 生物化学家Jesús Gil及其团队在伦敦的实验室中发现，通过每月注射一种抗体X203，18个月大的小鼠（相当于人类55岁）寿命延长了25%，且健康状况更好，癌症发生率更低、胆固醇水平下降、肌肉力量增强。这种抗体通过阻断与衰老相关的天然蛋白质白介素11（IL-11）起作用，减少细胞衰老和炎症。虽然小鼠实验结果积极，但研究人员强调，人类临床试验仍在初期阶段，主要关注安全性。目前，几家公司已开始测试类似抗体，目标包括治疗肺纤维化等老年疾病。尽管数据坚实，但有专家提醒，需更多不同品系小鼠的实验以验证结果的普遍性。该研究发表于《自然》杂志。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于延长动物寿命的研究及其意义

不同观点：
• JumpCrisscross 分享了一个关于抗IL-11抗体的链接，可能意在展示某种延长寿命或改善健康的技术。该用户只是简单分享链接，没有明确表达立场，但可能暗示对这种科学进展的关注或某种情绪上的"混乱"。

• Aken 对此作出幽默回应，提到科学进展能否在实际中被"复制"（即是否能应用于其他生物），并使用了"Aschen"这一科幻作品中的种族作为类比，暗示对这种技术在人类或其他生物中的应用持怀疑或调侃态度。

• Hulitu 则对延长小鼠寿命的技术表示讽刺，认为人类真正需要的不一定是让老鼠活得更久，而是针对人类本身的解决方案。该用户还提到纽约（可能暗指城市中的鼠患问题），进一步表达对延长小鼠寿命研究的不以为然，认为这可能不是人类应优先考虑的科学方向。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于科学研究的价值和优先级问题。部分评论者（如Aken和hulitu）对延长小鼠寿命的实际意义持怀疑态度，认为这未必是人类社会所迫切需要的，甚至带有调侃和讽刺的意味。

• 另一个值得注意的点是，JumpCrisscross的原始分享更像是单纯的信息传递，没有明确的立场，而其他评论者则对此信息进行了进一步的讨论和评价。

总体来看，讨论围绕科学研究的意义和优先级展开，尤其是延长动物寿命这一课题是否对人类社会具有直接价值。

It seems too good to be true, but biochemist Jesús Gil speaks enthusiastically from his laboratory in London. “There is no reason to think that what we have seen in mice will not work in people,” he says. What they have observed in rodents is verging on the miraculous: a team of scientists has given monthly injections of a simple antibody to mice that are almost 18 months old, an age equivalent to 55 human years. These animals have lived up to 25% longer than their peers and in good health, with lower incidence of cancer, less cholesterol, and greater muscle strength. It is as if
human life expectancy had skyrocketed to 104 years
, instead of the current 83 in Spain, for example.
The results are visible to the naked eye, explains cardiologist Stuart Cook, co-director of the research at the MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences in London. “The mice that received the X203 antibody looked leaner and more active, with better coat color — fewer gray hairs — and better vision, hearing, and walking ability.” Antibodies are proteins that circulate in the blood to defend the body against foreign substances, such as viruses and bacteria. In the case of X203, it is designed to block another natural protein with potent effects on aging: interleukin 11, whose concentration increases with age, causing cells to stop multiplying while accumulating and releasing harmful substances that cause inflammation and damage to nearby cells.
Cook stresses that there are already trials in people of experimental treatments to block interleukin 11, but they are not focused on studying aging over years or decades. He himself has founded a company, Enleofen, which is collaborating with the German pharmaceutical company Boehringer Ingelheim on the first tests of a similar antibody in healthy volunteers. Two other companies, the U.S.-based Lassen and China’s Mabwell, have also initiated similar projects, with the aim of curing
pulmonary fibrosis
and other age-related diseases.
“We have seen no adverse effects in mice.
Increasing longevity
and prolonging healthy life is the opposite of an adverse effect,” says Cook. The cardiologist adds that the first results in humans, from the Lassen trials, also show an “excellent safety profile.” In mice, the injection is made directly into the abdominal cavity for 25 weeks until euthanasia, the equivalent of administering it to a person for almost two decades. In humans, the injection is intravenous.
“To date, we have observed full equivalence between what interleukin 11 does in mice and humans. In the case of longevity, mice die mostly from cancer, whereas humans die mostly from
cardiovascular disease
and cancer. You would expect to see fewer tumors in humans with this therapy, as has already been seen in mice,” Cook explains. “As for heart disease, we’re not so sure, but interleukin 11-blocking treatments improved metabolism and cholesterol levels in mice, so it could also have effects on cardiovascular disease in humans. We will only know if clinical trials designed to study aging are conducted,” cautions the cardiologist, co-lead author of the paper with biologist Anissa Widjaja of the Duke-NUS Medical School at the National University of Singapore.
Biochemist Jesús Gil of the MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences in London.
Jesús Gil
Gil leads his own group at the Laboratory of Medical Sciences, a national center of the UK Medical Research Council. His team studies senescence, the state in which cells stop reproducing but do not die. As they accumulate, they promote inflammation, aging and cancer. “Inhibiting interleukin 11 can inhibit senescence,” says Gil, who has also conducted experiments with human cells. His results were published July 17 in the journal
Nature
.
Spanish biologist Rafael de Cabo, head of translational gerontology at the U.S. National Institute on Aging, applauds the new work, in which he did not participate. “The magnitude of life extension in mice is quite impressive,” he says. De Cabo, however, is cautious. “The data is super solid, but there are details that could call the interpretation a little into question. For example, they only use one genetic line of mice: the C57BLACK6, which are very common. To carry out longevity studies you have to use several strains of mice, in several places, to avoid it being a one-time observation, as has happened on a thousand occasions,” he warns.
However, the biologist is optimistic. “It is clear that playing with the inhibition of interleukin 11 has beneficial effects on the health of mice. The accumulation of data from this and other studies indicates that it can probably be used for specific types of diseases in humans,” he says. “The problem we have right now in the
field of aging research

data.title: Supabase MCP can leak your entire SQL database
data.author: rexpository
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Supabase的模型上下文协议（MCP）集成中的安全漏洞，该漏洞可能导致SQL数据库中的私密数据泄露。问题核心在于LLM（大语言模型）无法区分用户指令和数据，攻击者可以通过精心构造的用户数据诱导LLM执行未授权的SQL查询。在Supabase的默认配置中，IDE助理拥有高权限的`service_role`，可以绕过行级安全（RLS）策略执行数据库操作。如果攻击者通过提交表单注入恶意指令，可能导致敏感信息（如OAuth tokens和会话凭据）泄露。开发者需警惕此类风险，避免将高权限角色直接暴露给不可信的用户输入。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Supabase MCP中LLM（大型语言模型）提示注入攻击的讨论，以及对相关安全问题的不同看法和解决方案建议。

不同观点：
• **Supabase工程师的观点（gregnr）**：Supabase团队已经采取了一些缓解措施来防止提示注入攻击，包括鼓励使用只读模式、在SQL响应外包装提示以阻止LLM执行恶意指令、以及编写端到端测试来验证LLM是否容易受到攻击。他们承认提示注入是一个未完全解决的问题，并正在研究更细粒度的权限控制和更多文档说明。

• **XSS类比的观点（tptacek）**：将提示注入攻击类比为XSS（跨站脚本攻击），认为这是由于管理应用中处理未经验证的用户生成内容导致的常见问题。在LLM场景下，攻击者可以通过自然语言指令操纵系统，类似于通过Javascript在XSS中操作DOM。

• **问题根源的观点（dante1441）**：认为问题不在于Supabase MCP的具体实现，而在于将未经验证的用户生成内容注入LLM提示中。任何使用代理系统的场景都可能面临类似问题，提示是自然语言，表达方式多样且模型解释具有非确定性，使得防御攻击变得困难。

• **使用建议的观点（simonw）**：建议将数据库访问MCP配置为只读模式，并谨慎选择组合的其他MCP，以防止数据泄露。强调了"致命三合一"问题，即组合多种功能可能导致更严重的安全风险。

• **责任归咎的观点（vigilans）**：认为将LLM连接到生产基础设施的开发者自身是漏洞的根源，强调人为因素在安全问题中的重要性。

• **对MCP模型的批评观点（gortok）**：批评MCP模型的设计和推广，认为其在技术逻辑和安全考量上存在根本性问题，且受到资本推动而忽视了潜在风险。

• **实践经验的观点（nijave）**：分享了在工作中使用LLM进行数据探索的经验，认为通过Gated APIs或GraphQL等中间层可以更好地管理和限制LLM的访问权限，直接连接SQL是一个反模式。

补充讨论：
• **对攻击实例的关注**：多个评论提到实际攻击案例，如通过支持票注入指令（qualeed）和在其他平台发现的类似漏洞（coderinsan）。
• **对行业趋势的看法**：有评论指出支持网站常成为攻击载体（pests），并对Supabase团队为何推动此功能提出质疑（jppope）。
• **对现有实现的失望**：有评论对Cursor助手使用高权限账户操作数据库表示失望（yard2010），并对提示工程作为缓解措施的效果表示困惑（borromakot）。

争议焦点：
• **是否应直接将LLM与数据库或关键基础设施连接**：一些评论认为这是不安全的做法，建议通过中间层或沙盒环境限制LLM的访问权限。

44502318.article_content:
Supabase MCP can leak your entire SQL database
2025-06-16
Model Context Protocol (MCP) has emerged as a standard way for LLMs to interact with external tools. While this unlocks new capabilities, it also introduces new risk surfaces. In this post, we show how an attacker can exploit Supabase’s MCP integration to leak a developer’s private SQL tables.
The Problem
LLMs are often used to process data according to pre-defined instructions. The system prompt, user instructions, and the data context is provided to the LLM as text.
[
SYSTEM
PROMPT
]
You
are a helpful assistant.
[
FETCHED
DATA
]
Customer
: I
'm having trouble with billing.
Customer: I need to update my credit card because the current one expired.
[USER INSTRUCTION]
Summarize the ticket and suggest a reply.The core issue is that LLMs don'
t have a built-
in
understanding
of
context boundries.
They
process all text the same way; whether it is data/context or user instructions.
The core problem of LLMs interacting with tools is that they can not distinguish instructions from data. Therefore, if a caarefully crafted piece of user-provided “data” happens to look like an instruction, the model may process it as one.
The Setup
To keep the demonstration self-contained, we spun up a
fresh Supabase project
that mirrors a typical multi-tenant customer-support SaaS.
The instance was populated with dummy data only, Row-Level-Security (RLS) was enabled exactly as documented, and no additional extensions or policies were introduced.
Everything the attack exploits therefore exists in an “out-of-the-box” configuration: the standard
service_role
, the default model, RLS and a language-model assistant that issues MCP calls on behalf of the developer.
We assume the developer uses Cursor to interact with the MCP to list the latest support tickets occasionally.
1. Actors & Privilege Boundaries
Actor (Role)

44502318.article_summary: 本文讨论了Supabase的模型上下文协议（MCP）集成中的安全漏洞，该漏洞可能导致SQL数据库中的私密数据泄露。问题核心在于LLM（大语言模型）无法区分用户指令和数据，攻击者可以通过精心构造的用户数据诱导LLM执行未授权的SQL查询。在Supabase的默认配置中，IDE助理拥有高权限的`service_role`，可以绕过行级安全（RLS）策略执行数据库操作。如果攻击者通过提交表单注入恶意指令，可能导致敏感信息（如OAuth tokens和会话凭据）泄露。开发者需警惕此类风险，避免将高权限角色直接暴露给不可信的用户输入。
44502318.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Supabase MCP中LLM（大型语言模型）提示注入攻击的讨论，以及对相关安全问题的不同看法和解决方案建议。

不同观点：
• **Supabase工程师的观点（gregnr）**：Supabase团队已经采取了一些缓解措施来防止提示注入攻击，包括鼓励使用只读模式、在SQL响应外包装提示以阻止LLM执行恶意指令、以及编写端到端测试来验证LLM是否容易受到攻击。他们承认提示注入是一个未完全解决的问题，并正在研究更细粒度的权限控制和更多文档说明。

• **XSS类比的观点（tptacek）**：将提示注入攻击类比为XSS（跨站脚本攻击），认为这是由于管理应用中处理未经验证的用户生成内容导致的常见问题。在LLM场景下，攻击者可以通过自然语言指令操纵系统，类似于通过Javascript在XSS中操作DOM。

• **问题根源的观点（dante1441）**：认为问题不在于Supabase MCP的具体实现，而在于将未经验证的用户生成内容注入LLM提示中。任何使用代理系统的场景都可能面临类似问题，提示是自然语言，表达方式多样且模型解释具有非确定性，使得防御攻击变得困难。

• **使用建议的观点（simonw）**：建议将数据库访问MCP配置为只读模式，并谨慎选择组合的其他MCP，以防止数据泄露。强调了"致命三合一"问题，即组合多种功能可能导致更严重的安全风险。

• **责任归咎的观点（vigilans）**：认为将LLM连接到生产基础设施的开发者自身是漏洞的根源，强调人为因素在安全问题中的重要性。

• **对MCP模型的批评观点（gortok）**：批评MCP模型的设计和推广，认为其在技术逻辑和安全考量上存在根本性问题，且受到资本推动而忽视了潜在风险。

• **实践经验的观点（nijave）**：分享了在工作中使用LLM进行数据探索的经验，认为通过Gated APIs或GraphQL等中间层可以更好地管理和限制LLM的访问权限，直接连接SQL是一个反模式。

补充讨论：
• **对攻击实例的关注**：多个评论提到实际攻击案例，如通过支持票注入指令（qualeed）和在其他平台发现的类似漏洞（coderinsan）。
• **对行业趋势的看法**：有评论指出支持网站常成为攻击载体（pests），并对Supabase团队为何推动此功能提出质疑（jppope）。
• **对现有实现的失望**：有评论对Cursor助手使用高权限账户操作数据库表示失望（yard2010），并对提示工程作为缓解措施的效果表示困惑（borromakot）。

争议焦点：
• **是否应直接将LLM与数据库或关键基础设施连接**：一些评论认为这是不安全的做法，建议通过中间层或沙盒环境限制LLM的访问权限。

44498133.article_content:
SVGs that feel like GIFs
2025-07-07
web
cli
tools
The moving image below is only 49Kb and has an incredibly high resolution.
It's similar to a GIF but instead of showing moving images, it shows moving SVGs! The best part: Github supports these in their README.md files!
Getting these to work involves
asciinema
and
svg-term-cli
. After uploading the asciinema you can use the tool to download a file that you can immediately click and drag into a README, or you can use this snippet to keep things local:
> asciinema rec test.cast
<do stuff in the terminal then ctrl-d>
> cat test.cast | svg-term --out=test.svg
It's something that I'm using extensively on
bespoken
.
How it works?
I was surpised to learn that moving SVGs were even a thing. But then I was reminded that animations are built into
the svg spec
.
<animate>
- animates individual attributes over time
<animateTransform>
- animates transformations like rotation, scaling, translation
<animateMotion>
- moves elements along a path
This is what the
svg-term-cli
leverages under the hood.

《Section 174 撤销：所有美国境内研发支出可立即全额扣除》

摘要：
2025年，美国国内研发支出不再需要按五年摊销，立即可全额扣除。自2022年以来被摊销的研发支出，符合条件的企业（年收入不超过3100万美元）可申请退税或在2025年税表中补扣。企业需在法案生效后一年内修改2022至2024年的税表以追回已摊销成本，或选择在2025年税表中补扣。2024年12月31日后的研发支出可全额扣除。Afternoon.co可协助处理相关税务和修改申报。

关键点：
- 撤销Section 174的五年摊销要求。
- 符合条件的小企业可追溯申请退税。
- 需修改2022-2024年税表或在2025年补扣。
- 修改申报须在法案生效一年内完成。
- Afternoon.co提供相关税务咨询服务。

主要讨论点：关于技术社区中AI生成内容、开源项目贡献的质量及审核机制的讨论。

不同观点：

• 观点一：AI生成内容对开源项目贡献的质量产生负面影响。
  - 论据：一些用户认为，AI生成的代码或文档往往质量较低，缺乏深度理解，可能包含错误或不完整的解决方案。
  - 例子：有评论提到，AI生成的PR（Pull Request）在实际项目中可能导致更多的维护负担，因为需要花费额外时间去审查和修正。

• 观点二：AI生成内容可以提高开源项目的贡献效率。
  - 论据：支持者认为，AI工具能够帮助初学者或非专业开发者更快上手，并为项目提供基础性贡献，例如生成样板代码或文档。
  - 例子：有用户指出，AI生成的内容在某些简单任务上表现良好，可以作为贡献者的辅助工具，提高开发速度。

• 观点三：审核机制需要加强，而不是排斥AI生成内容。
  - 论据：部分讨论者认为，问题的核心不在于AI本身，而在于开源项目现有的审核机制不够严格。应该通过改进审核流程和工具来应对AI生成内容的潜在问题。
  - 例子：有评论建议，使用更严格的代码审查工具和自动化测试来筛选AI生成的内容，确保其质量达到项目标准。

• 观点四：AI生成内容的道德与知识产权问题。
  - 论据：一些讨论者关注AI生成内容的知识产权问题，认为AI生成的代码或文档可能涉及侵权或者归属权不明，这会对开源社区的贡献文化造成影响。
  - 例子：有用户担心，AI生成的内容可能复制了受版权保护的代码片段，而贡献者或项目维护者无法察觉。

补充讨论：

• 关于AI生成内容的透明度问题。
  - 一些讨论者提出，应该要求贡献者明确标注哪些内容是由AI生成的，以便更好地进行审核和评估。

• 关于AI对开源社区文化的长远影响。
  - 有观点认为，如果过度依赖AI生成内容，可能会削弱开发者之间的协作和学习机会，长远来看对开源社区的发展不利。

争议焦点：AI生成内容对开源项目的贡献是利大于弊还是弊大于利，以及如何在质量和效率之间找到平衡。

As part of the
One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA)

What was Section 174 amortization?
Since 2022,
Section 174 required businesses to amortize U.S. R&D expenses over five years
(and 15 years for most foreign R&D).
New section 174A
Updated Section 174A of the Internal Revenue Code allows
immediate full expensing
of
domestic
research and experimental (R&E) expenditures, reversing the 5-year amortization requirement imposed under the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) for these expenses.

Jai Ramaswamy
,

Kevin McKinley

Posted July 9, 2025
It used to be a no-brainer: start a company, incorporate in Delaware. That is no longer the case due to recent actions by the Court of Chancery, which have injected an unprecedented level of subjectivity into judicial decisions, undermining the court’s reputation for unbiased expertise. This has introduced legal uncertainty into what was widely considered the gold standard of U.S. corporate law. In contrast, Nevada has taken significant steps in establishing a technical, non-ideological forum for resolving business disputes. We have therefore decided to move the state of incorporation of our primary business, AH Capital Management, from Delaware to Nevada, which has historically been a business friendly state with fair and balanced regulatory policies.
We could have made this move quietly, but we think it’s important for our stakeholders, and for the broader tech and VC communities, to understand why we’ve reached this decision. For founders considering a similar move, there is often a reluctance to leave Delaware, based in part on concerns for how investors will react. As the largest VC firm in the country, we hope that our decision signals to our portfolio companies, as well as to prospective portfolio companies, that such concerns may be overblown. While we will continue to fund companies incorporated in Delaware, we believe Nevada is a viable alternative and may make sense for many founders.
The foundation of Delaware’s historical reputation has been non-ideological, specialized business courts that have developed a robust body of case law around the so-called “business judgment rule”, legal shorthand for a (rebuttable) presumption borrowed from English common law that boards of directors act in good faith and with informed judgment when making business decisions. Over the years, the Delaware courts developed a limited number of objective, common sense exceptions to this general rule; however, recently, those exceptions have begun to swallow the rule. Director independence has been questioned in cases where the board has granted
“moonshot”
grants to exceptional founders, and in one notable case the court reprised the chorus from
Hotel California
by
rejecting
a board’s decision to move its place of incorporation out of Delaware (although it was later reversed by the Delaware Supreme Court). This has rightly caused tech startup founders to question the primacy of Delaware.
Although the Delaware Legislature has taken some
exception
to these developments, its actions fail to take full measure of the problem. In particular, Delaware courts can at times appear biased against technology startup founders and their boards. Litigation – even where successfully defeated – is costly and time consuming, particularly for the tech startups that need every penny they raise to build innovative companies. The resulting legal uncertainty is a real cause for concern for entrepreneurs and their professional investors  who often sit on their boards. As a result, many of the companies we fund and the entrepreneurs that we talk to are taking a second look at whether they should incorporate in other jurisdictions, prompted by the departure from Delaware of significant technology companies like Dropbox, Tripadvisor and Tesla.
Nevada has taken a different path, choosing instead to codify the business judgement rule in statute, eliminating the ability of judges to modify or change the rule. In addition, the Nevada legislature recently passed two measures that take significant steps toward upgrading its existing business courts into specialized venues to resolve complex commercial disputes. AB 239 provides for a waiver of jury trials in civil cases, while AJR 8 calls for the adoption of a constitutional amendment to permit the direct appointment of business court judges by the Governor, rather than through the current system of elections. Both measures passed with overwhelming bipartisan majorities in the state Assembly and Senate, receiving the support of Nevada’s Republican Governor and Democratic Secretary of State, Speaker of the Assembly, and Senate Majority leader. While more work remains to be done on reforming Nevada’s business courts, we think that these measures represent a critical step in making Nevada a destination of choice for entrepreneurs.
A more detailed summary of the reasons for our decision to move from Delaware to Nevada is provided below.
Statutory Business Judgement Rule.
The presumption of good faith and informed decision making is the bedrock of any corporate code that seeks to encourage entrepreneurship and risk taking. While Delaware was a pioneer in this area of law, what developed was a creature of judicial decision, not statute. The critical limitation of this approach has been made plain

data.title: When politicians gain power, their language becomes garbled
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary:
一项由哥本哈根大学政治学副教授Frederik Hjorth进行的研究显示，执政的政治人物在掌握权力后，语言变得更加复杂难懂。该研究分析了近150万条议会演讲文本片段，发现执政者的语言比在野者更为复杂，且当他们离开政府后，语言会再次变得简单。这种变化主要由官僚术语、正式角色和话题选择导致，如处理法律细节和复杂议题。实验还表明，选民更青睐语言简单的政治人物。Hjorth认为，这可能解释了民粹主义运动的受欢迎程度以及执政党为何常失去支持。研究强调，执政不仅可能失去选民，还可能失去简洁沟通的能力。

来源: University of Copenhagen, Phys.org

不同观点：

• [giardini] 提出一种讽刺的观点，认为无论政治人物（如拜登）处于巅峰还是低谷，他们的语言表达总是被描述为含糊不清，建议将讨论主题直接改为"政治人物的语言是含糊的"以概括问题，暗示这种讨论没有实际意义。

• [bell-cot] 提出另一个角度，认为政治人物的语言被过度分析，尤其是记者和互联网对政客所说的每一个细节进行剖析，而对无关紧要或无权力的人则不会如此关注。这暗示了媒体和公众对政治人物言辞的不同标准。

The GIST
When politicians gain power, their language becomes garbled
by
University of Copenhagen
edited by
Lisa Lock
, 																								reviewed by
Robert Egan
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
trusted source
proofread
Credit: Unsplash/CC0 Public Domain
It's well known that governing parties often lose voters over time—the so-called cost of governing. But a new study from Frederik Hjorth, Associate Professor of Political Science at the University of Copenhagen, documents a lesser-known but potentially crucial side effect of being in government: politicians begin to speak less simply and understandably.
"We see that politicians in government use more complex language than their colleagues in the opposition—not because they want to, but because they have to," says Hjorth.
1.5 million text snippets reveal the pattern
The study,
published
in the journal
Comparative Political Studies
, is based on an analysis of almost 1.5 million text snippets from parliamentary speeches over three decades. Using language technology, Frederik Hjorth measured how understandable the speeches were and compared this to whether the speaker was in government or not.
The results are clear: when politicians enter government, their language becomes less simple. But when they leave government again, they return to more understandable language.
"This suggests that it's not about personal style or learning, but about the demands and roles you are subject to as a minister," explains Hjorth.
He emphasizes three factors that contribute to the effect:
Bureaucratic jargon: Ministers have to deal with technical and legal details.
Formal roles: for example, they have to present bills that are often written in difficult language.
Topic choice: Government politicians talk more about complex issues like regulation and crisis management—and less about ideologically clear topics like tax and immigration.
"It's not because they don't want to speak clearly, it's because their role forces them to talk about difficult things in a precise way," Hjorth points out.
Voters favor simplicity
But voters don't reward complexity. In an experiment with more than 4,000 participants, Hjorth shows that politicians who use simple language are rated more favorably, even when the content is the same.
"This confirms that there is a real political cost to speaking in a complicated way. Voters just prefer simplicity," he says.
The study also points to a possible explanation for the popularity of populist movements: populists can speak simply and directly—something government
politicians
find harder to do.
"Populists often emphasize that the elites have lost touch with the people. This study suggests that the criticism is correct in a sense: more technocratic language is part of the price of government accountability," says Hjorth.
According to him, the study shows that government power doesn't just cost voters. It also costs the ability to communicate simply.
"This gives the opposition a rhetorical advantage and may help explain why governing parties often lose support—And why new, linguistically sharp challengers gain ground," Hjorth concludes.
More information:
Frederik Hjorth, Losing Touch: The Rhetorical Cost of Governing,
Comparative Political Studies
(2025).

data.title: The Tradeoffs of SSMs and Transformers
data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了状态空间模型（SSM）与Transformer在序列建模中的 trade-offs，特别是针对语言模型的应用。文章首先定义了状态空间模型，并通过一组方程介绍了SSM的基本结构。接着，文章提出了SSM成功的三个关键要素：

1. **状态大小**：SSM的隐藏状态比输入和输出更大，以存储更多信息，类似于扩展版的RNN。
2. **状态表达力**：模型需要具有足够表达力的状态更新函数，以选择性地记住重要信息，Mamba模型通过使转换矩阵随时间变化提高了表达力。
3. **训练效率**：更大的状态和更高的表达力增加了计算难度。Mamba通过算法创新实现了并行计算和内存管理，从而提升了训练效率。

文章总结，Mamba通过结合状态扩展、选择性机制和算法创新，成功提升了SSM的性能，使其在语言建模上能与Transformer媲美。

- [macleginn] 的观点暗示了对分词方法本质的哲学性思考，强调了在不同文化和书写系统中，“原子”单位的多样性和相对性。
- [Herring] 的观点基于对当前技术趋势的观察，依赖于主流模型的选择来质疑SSMs的实际应用价值。
- 争议焦点可能在于新方法（如字符/字节替换BPE，或SSMs替代Transformers）是否真的能带来实质性的改进或创新，还是只是现有方法的变体或延续。

44503056.article_content:
On the Tradeoffs of SSMs and Transformers
(or - tokens are bs)
This blog post was adapted from a talk I’ve given a handful of times over the last year. It was meant to be a high-level talk accessible to a fairly broad audience, but hopefully has some interesting insights, opinions, and intuitions around sequence models for the dedicated researchers too.
State Space Models
Just so we’re on the same page, I’ll start by defining what I mean by a state space model. (This section isn’t strictly necessary to get to the main part of this post though; feel free to skip directly to
the next section
.)
\[\begin{equation} \label{eq:ssm} \begin{aligned} h_{t} &= A_t h_{t-1} + B_t x_t \\ y_t &= C_t^{\top} h_t \end{aligned} \end{equation}\]
These equations define the (structured) state space model (SSM) as developed in a line of work
culminating in Mamba
. They can be viewed as a modern version of a recurrent neural network (RNN) with a few key characteristics. While a lot of technical work was involved in getting this family of models to work, I’ll start by trying to abstract away what I view as the main high-level ingredients that made these models successful, e.g. match the performance of Transformers on language modeling.
The three ingredients
1. State size
A characteristic of the SSM is that its hidden state $h_t$ has a larger size than the the inputs and outputs $x_t, y_t$. The key idea is that the hidden state of any recurrent model is its only access to the model’s context (in an autoregressive setting). So for modeling information-dense modalities such as language, the model needs a large enough state to store the relevant information that it wants to access later.
In SSMs, if each input $x_t$ is a 1-dimensional scalar, then the hidden state $h_t$ is an $\mathtt{N}$-dimensional vector, where $\mathtt{N}$ is an independent hyperparameter called the
state size, state dimension, or state expansion factor
. This is also known as a SISO (single-input single-output) SSM and allows the models to store $\mathtt{N}$ times as much information as older RNNs such as LSTMs and GRUs
.
2. State expressivity
Not only does the model need to have a large enough state to
theoretically
store relevant context, it needs to have an expressive enough state update function to encode and access exactly the information it needs.
Earlier versions of “linear time-invariant” SSMs used simple recurrences $h_{t} = A h_{t-1} + B x_t$ whose updates are constant at every time step
. While this works great for compressible data like audio, it doesn’t provide enough flexibility for sequences with variable information rates like language, where the model may have to selectively choose what information to remember.
Selective SSMs
like Mamba fix this by making the recurrence more expressive by letting the transition matrices vary through time and depend on the data itself. These mechanisms are closely related to the gating mechanisms of classical RNNs!
This is the area with the most active research on modern recurrent models, which are focused on understanding the theoretical expressivity of different parameterizations of the transition matrix $A_t$ and what they allow the model to remember in its state.
3. Training efficiency
Having a larger and more expressive recurrent state is important, but comes with a critical trade-off – the model becomes much harder to compute. Mamba addressed this with careful parameterization of the recurrence and utilizing the classic parallel scan algorithm
.
Many other algorithmic innovations have appeared, all with a few shared characteristics:
Parallelization
: They aim to be parallelizable and practically efficient on accelerators like GPUs and TPUs – preferably leveraging matrix multiplications (matmuls) as the workhorse.
Memory management
: They have to control memory usage carefully. In particular, any model that uses state expansion can’t actually materialize the state in main memory! While Mamba brute-forced the problem using clever awareness of the GPU memory hierarchy
, most alternatives find ways of rewriting the equations entirely to use different computation paths that don’t need to compute the state explicitly during a parallel training pass.
Linearity
: The model generally has to be linear in $x_t$, leading some to call this whole family of models
linear recurrent models
. Linearity plays a role in both computational efficiency as well as modeling/optimization ability, which I won’t get into here.
Mamba - putting it all together
None of these three ingredients is new:
Linear attention
and earlier SSMs
had similar equations utilizing state expansion.
Selectivity was inspired by, and closely related to, gating mechanisms in classical RNNs like the LSTM and GRU
.
Parallel scans were utilized in earlier SSMs/linear RNNs like S5
and LRU
. Linear attention variants also used parallelizable training algorithms leveraging matmuls.
What Mamba did was show that
combining all of these together
was the key to a step c

这篇文章讨论了状态空间模型（SSM）与Transformer在序列建模中的 trade-offs，特别是针对语言模型的应用。文章首先定义了状态空间模型，并通过一组方程介绍了SSM的基本结构。接着，文章提出了SSM成功的三个关键要素：

1. **状态大小**：SSM的隐藏状态比输入和输出更大，以存储更多信息，类似于扩展版的RNN。
2. **状态表达力**：模型需要具有足够表达力的状态更新函数，以选择性地记住重要信息，Mamba模型通过使转换矩阵随时间变化提高了表达力。
3. **训练效率**：更大的状态和更高的表达力增加了计算难度。Mamba通过算法创新实现了并行计算和内存管理，从而提升了训练效率。

文章总结，Mamba通过结合状态扩展、选择性机制和算法创新，成功提升了SSM的性能，使其在语言建模上能与Transformer媲美。

主要讨论点：关于不同技术方法在语言模型中的有效性和应用前景的讨论，包括分词（tokenisation）方法和不同模型架构（SSMs与Transformers）的比较。

不同观点：
• 关于分词（tokenisation）：
   - [macleginn] 认为，用字符或字节替换BPE（Byte Pair Encoding）并不能真正“去除分词”。他认为，无论是字符还是字节，在不同文化和书写传统中仍然作为一种“原子”单位存在，和语言本质无关。BPE只是用符号表示语言序列的一种方式，虽然它减少了对语言使用的归纳偏见，但和任何其他书写系统并无根本不同。

• 关于SSMs（State Space Models）与Transformers：
   - [Herring] 对SSMs（以及混合SSM/Transformer模型）持怀疑态度。他认为，当前领先的开源模型（如DeepSeek, Qwen, Gemma, Llama）都是基于Transformers架构的，如果SSMs有明显优势，这些模型应该已经尝试过SSMs，但目前并没有这样做的迹象。

补充讨论：
- [macleginn] 的观点暗示了对分词方法本质的哲学性思考，强调了在不同文化和书写系统中，“原子”单位的多样性和相对性。
- [Herring] 的观点基于对当前技术趋势的观察，依赖于主流模型的选择来质疑SSMs的实际应用价值。
- 争议焦点可能在于新方法（如字符/字节替换BPE，或SSMs替代Transformers）是否真的能带来实质性的改进或创新，还是只是现有方法的变体或延续。

data.title: Berry Script: lightweight embedded scripting language for microcontrollers
data.author: hasheddan
data.article_summary: Berry是一种超轻量、动态类型的嵌入式脚本语言，专为低性能嵌入式设备设计。其解释器核心代码小于40KiB，可在低于4KiB堆内存的环境下运行（基于ARM Cortex M4 CPU）。Berry采用单通道编译器和基于寄存器的虚拟机，全部代码用ANSI C99编写。它支持命令式、面向对象和函数式编程，具有灵活的FFI（外部函数接口）和简单的语法。基本类型包括Nil、布尔、整数、实数、字符串、类、实例、模块、列表、映射和范围。Berry提供控制结构、函数嵌套、闭包、类与单继承、垃圾回收等功能，并支持正则表达式和LVGL映射。其语法简洁，类似于高级语言，易于嵌入现有代码中使用，如Tasmota。

44472246.article_content:
Berry is a ultra-lightweight dynamically typed embedded scripting language. It is designed for lower-performance embedded devices. The Berry interpreter-core's code size is less than 40KiB and can run on less than 4KiB heap (on ARM Cortex M4 CPU, Thumb ISA and ARMCC compiler).
The interpreter of Berry include a one-pass compiler and register-based VM, all the code is written in ANSI C99. In Berry not every type is a class object. Some simple value types, such as int, real, boolean and string are not class object, but list, map and range are class object. This is a consideration about performance. Register-based VM is the same meaning as above.
Lightweight
A well-optimized interpreter with very little resources. Ideal for use in microprocessors.
Fast
Optimized one-pass bytecode compiler and register-based virtual machine.
Powerful
Supports imperative programming, object-oriented programming, functional programming.
Flexible
Berry is a dynamic type script, and it's intended for embedding in applications. It can provide good dynamic scalability for the host system.
Simple
Simple and natural syntax, support garbage collection, and easy to use FFI (foreign function interface).
RAM saving
With compile-time object construction, most of the constant objects are stored in read-only code data segments, so the RAM usage of the interpreter is very low when it starts.

data.title: AI Makes It Look Good. Craft Makes It Matter
data.author: realvjy
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了AI生成内容（如视觉效果、视频、代码等）的快速和精致，但指出这些内容往往缺乏真正的 craft（ craft指精心制作和人类意图）。虽然AI工具如Midjourney和ChatGPT可以帮助突破创意瓶颈，但它们生成的内容常常只有表面的“氛围”，而没有深层次的故事或情感。文章强调，真正的创作过程是混乱且个人化的，包含了构思、修改和追求意义的努力，而AI则可能将这一过程简化为输入提示词并生成结果。这种转变可能导致我们为了速度而牺牲意义，为了方便而放弃关怀，为了规模而忽视工艺。在代码方面，AI虽然能提高效率，但如果没有人类指导，它生成的代码往往不够完善。最终，AI只是放大了已有的东西，如果使用者本身缺乏技能和品味，AI生成的内容也只会是表面光鲜的“完美空壳”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI与艺术创作的核心价值

不同观点：
• 观点一：AI创作类似于即兴表演（improv）。这个观点由sjmog提出，认为AI创作虽然有时有趣甚至出色，但缺乏伟大艺术所具备的核心 crafted 元素，无法达到那种让艺术变得“透明”的高度。这意味着AI缺少深思熟虑的人类创作意图和精心打磨。

• 观点二：AI创作可能具有潜力。虽然评论中没有明确提出，但从sjmog的评论可以推断出，可能有人认为AI在适当的经验和操作下，有可能达到或接近人类创作的高度，尤其在技术不断进步的背景下。

补充讨论：
• AI在艺术中的角色：评论引发了对AI在艺术创作中角色的思考，即AI是工具还是创作者。sjmog认为AI更像是缺乏灵魂的工具，即使操作得当，也仅能达到某种程度的娱乐性，而非真正的艺术精髓。

• 艺术的定义：sjmog的评论隐含了对“什么是真正艺术”的讨论。他认为伟大艺术有一种“透明”的特质，而AI缺少这种特质，这反映了对艺术本质和人类创作核心价值的探讨。

• 技术与人类创作的区别：评论强调了人类创作中经验、意图和匠心的重要性，这是AI目前难以模仿的。这也涉及到技术能否真正理解和复制人类情感和创造力的争议。

争议焦点：
• AI是否能够创造出具备艺术核心价值的作，即是否能达到“透明”的艺术高度。这涉及到技术极限和艺术定义的深层次问题。

AI Makes It Look Good. Craft Makes It Matter
We’re surrounded by AI-generated visuals, videos, and code — fast, slick, and impressive. But behind all that polish, something essential is missing: real craft, care, and human intent.
Jul 8, 2025
·
8
min read
Lately, my feed’s been overflowing with wild AI-made clips—anime openings for shows that don’t exist, fake movie trailers for movies no one shot, cinematic pans through rain-soaked neon streets.
Someone posts: “Took me 5 minutes to make this.”
And yeah—it looks great. The vibes are perfect.
But I watch them... and feel nothing.
Vibes, But No Pulse
Don’t get me wrong—I use AI. Midjourney, Claude AI, ChatGPT. These tools are fast, fun, and sometimes exactly what I need to break through creative blocks.
But there’s this feeling I can’t shake.
Like I’m looking at something that looks finished, but it’s missing life.
It looks complete, but feels empty inside.
Sure, you generated a scene.
But where’s the part that stays with you?
Where’s the heartbeat?
Cool Outputs, No Story
I’ve played with these tools. You type “cyberpunk alley at night” or “Ghibli-style train ride,” and seconds later, you’ve got a stunning image.
And for someone who’s never drawn or filmed before, that’s powerful.
Let’s be honest: a lot of what people post isn’t really a story.
It’s just a cool vibe. Something pretty to look at. Nothing deeper.
That viral AI anime opening? Yeah, it looks slick. The camera sweeps, the music hits.
But... nothing happens. No characters. No arc. No stakes. Just vibes.
Now go watch the first four minutes of
Up
. No dialogue. Just scenes.
And suddenly your chest tightens. That’s storytelling. That’s human.
It’s not just how polished something looks—it’s
why
it exists.
The intention behind it.
Why do you think Nolan still crashes real planes?
Why did Greta Gerwig paint skies for
Barbie
?
Not because they couldn’t fake it—but because they
wanted you to feel it
.
Same reason Tom Cruise keeps doing his own stunts.
It’s not realism.
It’s commitment. You’re watching someone
care
.
And that effort? It shows. Even when people can’t explain why, they feel it.
That’s what’s missing in a lot of AI-generated stuff today.
It’s shiny. But it doesn’t breathe.
The Flood of Perfect, Empty Things
Here's what feels off about all this:
AI isn't just helping artists go faster — it's replacing the creative part of making something real.
What used to be a messy, personal process—coming up with ideas, struggling through drafts, chasing something meaningful—is now reduced to typing a prompt and hitting “generate.”
Look around: YouTube is packed with AI-generated music.
Tracks built by algorithms, made to fill playlists, not to move people.
Amazon’s flooded with AI-written books—churned out to fill search results, not say something worth hearing.
And it’s not stopping there.
It’s images. Videos. Fake trailers. Whole creative works that once took time, effort, and soul—now spun out in seconds.
But when you watch those clips or listen to those songs... do you feel anything?
That’s what we’re risking:
Trading meaning for speed.
Care for convenience.
Craft for scale.
And maybe that feels fine right now, while it’s new.
But when no one struggles to make things anymore—what’s left to be proud of?
Code Is Different Though
Interestingly, in code, AI helps
more than it hurts
.
Ask ChatGPT or Copilot to build a to-do app, and yeah—you’ll get buttons, an input field, maybe some direction to make backend. It works.
But open it up:
No clear structured code.
Could lack of error handling.
No real testing for vulnerabilities.
No accessibility.
No real architecture, unless you know what you’re doing.
It’s duct-taped together. Built to run, not to last.
But flip it—if you know your fundamentals, your patterns, your edge cases—AI becomes a force multiplier.
It handles the boring parts while you solve the hard ones.
It catches mistakes before you even see them.
The difference? Direction.
AI guesses. You guide.
If you know what “good” looks like, you can build something real.
If you don’t, you’re just stacking guesses on top of guesses.
For most of the work—boilerplate, repetitive tasks—AI is enough.
But that last 20%? The structure, the weird user bugs, the fragile 2 a.m. failures?
That’s still on you.
AI is a multiplier. But it multiplies what you already have.
If you’ve got taste and skill, it takes you further.
If not, it just makes your shortcuts faster.
Why We Love the Shortcuts
But then... why does all this stuff blow up?
Why do people proudly say, “This took me 5 minutes”?
Because for a lot of people, this is the first time they’ve
made
something.
The first time they felt creative.
AI lets you skip the years of learning, the rejection, the self-doubt.
And that shortcut feels amazing.
It looks good. People like it.
And social media rewards
the surface
, not the soul.
So of course people post it.
We all want to feel like creators.
Even if AI did most of the work,
you
still typed the pro
44512974.article_summary: 文章讨论了AI生成内容（如视觉效果、视频、代码等）的快速和精致，但指出这些内容往往缺乏真正的 craft（ craft指精心制作和人类意图）。虽然AI工具如Midjourney和ChatGPT可以帮助突破创意瓶颈，但它们生成的内容常常只有表面的“氛围”，而没有深层次的故事或情感。文章强调，真正的创作过程是混乱且个人化的，包含了构思、修改和追求意义的努力，而AI则可能将这一过程简化为输入提示词并生成结果。这种转变可能导致我们为了速度而牺牲意义，为了方便而放弃关怀，为了规模而忽视工艺。在代码方面，AI虽然能提高效率，但如果没有人类指导，它生成的代码往往不够完善。最终，AI只是放大了已有的东西，如果使用者本身缺乏技能和品味，AI生成的内容也只会是表面光鲜的“完美空壳”。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MCP（Multi-Channel Protocol）工具的应用、安全性、实用性以及其与现有技术（如OAuth、Swagger等）的关系。

不同观点：
• **工具选择与使用难度**：throwanem认为直接提供基础工具（如锯子、锤子、钉子）比给一个Home Depot（五金店）让用户自己挑选要简单，而slt2021则提出是否可以通过发布OpenAPI规范和使用Swagger客户端来替代MCP，认为这样可以手动建立认证会话。

• **项目贡献与技术实现**：fzysingularity提到GitHub上一个相关项目（MiguelsPizza/WebMCP）的贡献数据，指出Claude的提交量很大。abrookewood则认为MCP与Elixir的Tidewave MCP服务器类似，但Tidewave更专注于开发者。

• **安全性与授权问题**：mehdibl对MCP的安全性提出质疑，指出OAuth在亚马逊内部不兼容，且MCP在多租户应用中的授权问题尚未解决。他认为限制模型的权限和数据访问是重要的，但现有方案可能存在绕过安全机制的风险。

• **用户体验与可用性**：netrem认为产品看起来有趣，但登陆页面混乱，信息重复，阅读体验不佳，甚至怀疑是AI生成的。SchemaLoad不确定产品的目标用户是谁，认为对于前端测试和自动化，现有的API可能更合适。

• **简化解释与技术门槛**：cryptozeus请求用简单易懂的语言解释MCP，orliesaurus也表示不理解MCP与Selenium的区别，希望开发者能解释清楚。

• **自动化与应用场景**：muratsu认为MCP的实现对网站拥有者来说负担较大，建议自动化MCP的创建和维护。Flux159则关心MCP工具是否开源，并提出是否可以通过反向工程为任意网站编写Chrome扩展。

• **实用价值与开发者替代问题**：rapind对MCP在应用中的潜力表示认可，特别是对用户的帮助。然而，mupuff1234则质疑MCP的必要性，认为如果AI将取代开发者，为何还要 bother 开发MCP。

补充讨论：
• **对产品细节的关注**：metta2uall对项目的效率和节能表示赞赏，但指出Chrome扩展的跨浏览器声明不准确。ge96以幽默的方式提出一个实际测试建议，希望看到MCP在支付系统中的应用效果。

争议焦点：
• MCP的安全性与授权机制，特别是OAuth的兼容性问题及其在多租户应用中的潜在风险。
• MCP的实际应用价值以及是否值得投入开发精力，尤其是在AI可能取代开发者的背景下。

data.title: Show HN: MCP server for searching and downloading documents from Anna's Archive
data.author: iosifache
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Anna's Archive的MCP服务器（annas-mcp），用于搜索和下载文档。该平台是一个综合存储库，自动化检索在宽松许可框架下发布的文档，如Creative Commons和公共领域材料。文章强调该软件不支持未经授权获取版权内容，用户需尊重知识产权。工具功能包括文档搜索和下载，使用需要MCP客户端、捐赠以获取API访问权限及API密钥。设置步骤包括下载二进制文件并配置环境变量。文章还提供了Claude Desktop的配置示例。项目使用Go语言开发，目前有46个星标和1个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Anna's Archive项目及其相关技术工具的使用和伦理问题

不同观点：
• [profsummergig] 认为Anna's Archive需要下载大量包含数千本书的大型压缩文件（>10GB），即使只需要一本书。他提到曾使用基于IPFS的工具成功下载了一本200年前的公共领域书籍《最后的莫西干人》，但过程非常复杂。

• [irskep] 对使用MCP服务器而不是命令行工具的优势感到好奇，并询问在什么情况下选择使用其中一种工具更为合适，同时对项目表示赞赏。

• [toomuchtodo] 提出是否可以接受一个PR（Pull Request），以通过env变量覆盖搜索和下载端点的 hostname，认为这对拥有自己副本和ES索引的人可能有帮助。

• [puppycodes] 简单表达了对Anna's Archive的支持和喜爱。

• [xmonkee] 作为LLM新手，询问是否可以开发一个能够下载、阅读并引用文献的研究代理，质疑其可行性。

• [neilv] 质疑软件声明中关于不支持未经授权获取版权内容的诚意，强调用户应尊重知识产权。

• [thorum] 对Claude调用这些功能表示惊讶，并质疑项目在处理公共领域作品和版权作品（如《哈利·波特》）时的选择和道德问题。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现：讨论了工具的使用复杂性和技术改进建议（如[profsummergig]和[toomuchtodo]的评论）。
• 伦理与法律：关注下载内容的版权问题，尤其是公共领域和受版权保护作品的区分，以及软件声明的诚意（[neilv]和[thorum]的观点）。
• 项目应用：对项目扩展功能（如研究代理）的可行性进行了探讨（[xmonkee]的疑问）。

data.title: A Typology of Canadianisms
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary:
《DCHP-3使用指南》概述了加拿大英语词典的条目结构和分类体系。词典根据词义将加拿大词汇分为六种类型及“非加拿大”类。类型包括：  
1. **起源**：词汇及其意义源自加拿大，如"garburator"。  
2. **保存**：在其他英语变体中消失，但在加拿大保留的词汇，如"pencil crayon"。  
3. **语义变化**：在加拿大发生语义转变的词汇，如"toque"。  
4. **文化意义**：对加拿大身份重要的词汇，如"goalie mask"。  
5. **频率**：通过使用频率确立为加拿大英语的词汇，如"washroom"。  
6. **纪念**：反映加拿大历史阴暗面的词汇，如"residential school"。  

每个条目按时间顺序标注版本和起始日期，条目左侧提供意义及链接。
data.comments_summary:

  - joshdavham提到“soaker”和“booters”是曼尼托巴地区对特定情境的描述。

• **语言习惯差异**：
  - no_ja讨论了在加拿大说“Hospital”而不是“the hospital”的习惯，认为这与美国的用法不同。
  - regus提到通过发音“resources”中的字母Z来辨别加拿大人。
  - wk_end表示在国外时常意识到某些词是加拿大特有的。

• **特定词汇和其误解**：
  - michaelmior分享了作为加拿大人在美国生活时因使用加拿大特有词汇如“hydro”而产生的误解。
  - PieUser指出“upload”和“download”在加拿大政治语境中有特殊的含义。

• **文化词汇和娱乐影响**：
  - neurobashing提到“dart”未被列出，质疑其是否因新近流行而未被收录。

• **家庭用语和地区不确定性**：
  - scarecrw提到其家庭中使用的某些词汇不确定是否为加拿大特有的。
  - bawolff对美国人不用“pencil crayons”一词表示惊讶。

补充讨论：
- ** washroom vs. bathroom**：
  - sheepscreek解释了公共空间使用“washroom”和家庭内使用“powder room”的区别。
  
- **学校年级表达**：
  - bardak指出加拿大和美国在年级表达上的差异，如“grade one”与“first grade”。

- **传统词汇**：
  - throaway5454提到了“chesterfield”和“serviette”这些可能已经不太常用的老式加拿大词汇。

争议焦点：
- 某些词汇如“dart”是否广泛使用或是否因新近流行而未被广泛认可。

The basic principles of entry structure remain the same as in DCHP-2 (
see here
), though the appearance is quite different.
A Typology of Canadianisms
While this dictionary lists entries (headwords, lexemes), meanings are its smallest unit. Each meaning is assigned to one of six Types of Canadianism or is marked as “Non-Canadian”. The label “Non-Canadian” is used for meanings that were previously classified as Canadian or that were suspected to be Canadian but turned out to be none of our six types. The six types of Canadianisms are:
Type 1 – Origin
: a form and its meaning were created in what is now Canada
Type 2 – Preservation
: a form or meaning that was once widespread in many Englishes, but is now preserved in Canadian English in the North American context or beyond; sometimes called “retention”
Type 3 – Semantic Change
: forms that have undergone semantic change in Canadian English
Type 4 – Culturally Significant
: forms or meanings that have been enshrined in the Canadian psyche and are widely seen as part of Canadian identity
Type 5 – Frequency
: forms or meanings that are Canadian by virtue of frequency
Type 6 – Memorial
: forms or meanings now widely considered to be pejorative
Non-Canadian
: forms or meanings once thought to be Canadian for which evidence is lacking
(
Dollinger 2019
: 122-23)
Type 1
is a Canadianism by virtue of originating—entering the English language—in what is now Canada. A classic example is
garburator
; newer examples from this edition are
hang a larry
,
hang a roger
,
levidrome
,
renovict
and
quinzhee
.
Type 2
is a preservation in Canadian English from another variety of English, often from the UK but also from the US. The standard example is
pencil crayon
, once used in the US and now exclusively Canadian. Newer examples are
joe job
, the newly reclassified
parkade
and
peace bond
.
Type 3
is assigned when semantic change has been witnessed of an older form in Canadian English, where
toque
‘a chef’s hat, a woman’s hat’ was adapted to a close-fitting warm winter hat or
Canuck
, meaning 2b, which underwent semantic amelioration in Canada, from a term of abuse to a term of endearment for Anglophone Canadians (meaning 2a, ‘French Canadians’ did not bear such positive connotations throughout Canada’s history). New additions to this category include
quadrex
‘a four-plex’, which is influenced by Quebec French and used to refer to other entities,
soaker
‘a wet foot’ rather than just an alcoholic (US English)’ or
social
‘wedding party’, which is common in Manitoba today.
Type 4
is the Culturally significant vocabulary, of which hockey terminology and things to do with revered Canadian institutions are prime contenders.
Universal healthcare
or hockey terminology, e.g.
goalie mask
, have that status, as do Indigenous words, e.g.
culturally modified tree
. This category includes those meanings of
eh
that are associated with Canadian English. As the country realigns itself out of Anglophone/Francophone hegemony we will see what other forms of activity will become associated with Canada. Newer terms include
elbows up
(meaning #2), the battle cry to avoid becoming a “51st state”, while meaning #1 is in the same category as a style of playing hockey. Other examples include
poudrerie
, as part of the Canadian (winter) experience,
deke (n.)
and
deke (v.)
as well as
rink rat
or, from local UBC student culture,
bzzr
‘beer’.
Type 5
is a label that has been used often, as it is methodologically often the simplest way to establish a Canadian dimension in the comparative usage record. The classic examples are
washroom
‘(public) toilet’ nationally and
cube van
‘box-shaped (moving) truck’ in Central Canada. We used that criterion to declare
chirp
,
goal suck
,
heat dome
,
klick
,
rig pig
,
substance use
and
quilling
(meaning #2) Canadian, often in contrast to US English, in which case we insisted on a difference of several multiples of frequency in Canada compared to the US. As well, that’s how
brown bread
and
shit disturber
were assigned their Canadian labels.
Finally,
Type 6
is the Memorial type. It’s the flipside of Type 4, Cultural significance, and concerns the darker aspects of Canada’s history. A prime example is
residential school
, the euphemism that sounds innocent but which exerted such brutal force with ongoing consequences in society today. In this edition we added
maplewashing
(meaning #1a) and
pretendian
yet we only, it seems, scratched the surface. As in DCHP-2, Type 6 - Memorial is the least developed, which would offer an approach for the next edition.

《DCHP-3使用指南》概述了加拿大英语词典的条目结构和分类体系。词典根据词义将加拿大词汇分为六种类型及“非加拿大”类。类型包括：  
1. **起源**：词汇及其意义源自加拿大，如"garburator"。  
2. **保存**：在其他英语变体中消失，但在加拿大保留的词汇，如"pencil crayon"。  
3. **语义变化**：在加拿大发生语义转变的词汇，如"toque"。  
4. **文化意义**：对加拿大身份重要的词汇，如"goalie mask"。  
5. **频率**：通过使用频率确立为加拿大英语的词汇，如"washroom"。  
6. **纪念**：反映加拿大历史阴暗面的词汇，如"residential school"。  

每个条目按时间顺序标注版本和起始日期，条目左侧提供意义及链接。

data.title: Multi-Region Row Level Security in CockroachDB
data.author: rusticwizard
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了CockroachDB 25.2版本中引入的行级安全（Row-Level Security）功能，该功能允许在数据库内实现对数据访问的细粒度控制，尤其是在多租户和多地域场景中非常有用。传统表级权限控制不够精细，难以应对复杂访问场景，而行级安全可以通过基于用户角色或属性的策略来限制数据访问。

在多租户环境中，所有租户的数据共享同一数据库表，通过行级安全根据租户身份控制访问权限，既保证了逻辑隔离，又降低了基础设施和运营成本。此外，使用单一共享模式简化了 schema 变更和管理复杂度，提高了性能和资源利用率。

文章还通过具体示例展示了如何在CockroachDB中使用行级安全来实现多租户设置，步骤包括创建数据库、表、索引、用户及启用行级安全策略，从而实现高效、安全的数据访问控制。

• journal提出了对多租户单数据库模式的质疑，认为这种模式丧失了单租户单数据库的一个主要优势，即能够轻松地对单个租户进行灾难恢复或将租户迁移到专用服务器上。这表明journal更倾向于单租户单数据库的架构，因为它在灵活性和可管理性上具有优势。

多租户架构中，行级别安全是否能够有效隔离不同租户的数据，以及多租户单数据库模式是否在可维护性和灵活性上存在不足。

Controlling who can access what data is more important than ever as organizations scale and modernize their data infrastructure.
Enterprises are modernizing their critical databases, and they need fine-grained, built-in access controls that go beyond table-level permissions. That’s why, with the
25.2 release of CockroachDB
, we’re introducing Row-Level Security — a powerful feature that allows you to define and enforce access policies
at the row level
, directly within the database.
This form of mandatory access control enables developers and operators to tightly govern data visibility based on user roles or attributes. That makes it a natural fit for securing sensitive workloads and building robust multi-tenant applications.
In this article we’ll explore how CockroachDB makes it simple to isolate data, comply with regulatory requirements, and reduce application-side complexity, all while maintaining performance at scale and with minimal application changes using Row Level Security.
Why row-level security matters
CockroachDB already has robust support for managing privileges at the table, database or the schema level. While table-level permissions provide essential control, they often lack the granularity needed to handle nuanced access scenarios effectively.
For instance, consider a multi-tenancy situation where multiple customers or tenants share a single table within an application. Without granular, row-level access control, ensuring that each tenant can access only their own data becomes challenging and risky.
Another critical scenario, multi-region, involves data restriction based on geography. Consider an enterprise where users should only have access to rows related to a specific geographical region: Table-level privileges alone would not be sufficient to enforce this policy without complicating the data model.
Next we'll explore these two scenarios in greater detail, and show you how Row Level Security in CockroachDB effectively addresses each use case.
Multi-Tenancy + Row Level Security
Multi-tenancy in databases
is a design where a single database instance serves multiple customers (tenants), with each tenant's data kept logically isolated. This approach helps reduce infrastructure costs, streamline operations, and scale more easily, which is especially valuable for SaaS applications.
There are two common approaches to
implementing multi-tenancy
:
A separate database or cluster per tenant provides strong isolation but is expensive and operationally complex as the number of tenants increases.
Separate schema or table per tenant lowers infrastructure costs but becomes hard to manage at scale, requiring duplicated schema changes and inconsistent performance tuning.
A third and more scalable option is Row-Level Security (RLS). With RLS in
CockroachDB
, all tenant data lives in shared tables, and access is controlled at the row level based on tenant identity. This model combines strong logical isolation with lower infrastructure and operational costs, making it well suited for high-scale multi-tenant environments.
From an operational perspective, Row-Level Security (RLS) makes management simpler. Instead of maintaining a separate schema or table for each tenant, you use a single shared schema.
This means schema changes, like adding a column or modifying an index, only need to be applied once. It reduces the risk of inconsistencies between tenants and eliminates the need for complex migration processes or tenant-specific logic in deployment pipelines.
On the infrastructure side, RLS allows for more efficient resource usage. By consolidating tenant data into shared tables, CockroachDB can optimize performance across tenants without duplicating storage or compute resources. This lets you host more tenants on the same cluster, improving hardware utilization and reducing the need for additional infrastructure to support growth.
To demonstrate how Row Level Security can enable multi-tenant setups with minimal application changes, let’s look at the following example:
First, we create an in-memory cluster for demo purposes.
cockroach demo --no-example-database --insecure
Then we will create our database and a multi-tenant table, note the
tenant_id
column.
CREATE DATABASE store;
CREATE TABLE tenant_data (
id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
tenant_id UUID NOT NULL,
data TEXT NOT NULL
);
Next, we’ll create an index on the data column, prefixed with
tenant_id
. This is a crucial step because including
tenant_id
at the beginning of the index ensures that queries scoped to a specific tenant can efficiently locate relevant rows.
Without these indexes, the database may need to scan large portions of the table, which can degrade performance as your dataset grows.
CREATE INDEX ON tenant_data(tenant_id, data);
Next we will create a user that we will later login as:
CREATE ROLE secureuser LOGIN;
GRANT ALL ON store.* TO secureuser;

data.author: kushalpandya
data.article_summary: Petrichor是一款离线macOS音乐播放器，支持映射音乐文件夹、浏览有序的音乐库、创建播放列表和管理播放队列。它具有侧边栏快速访问、右键导航到专辑或艺术家等功能，并集成macOS菜单栏和Dock播放控制，支持深色模式。搜索功能可以快速查找大型音乐库中的歌曲。未来计划加入智能播放列表、AirPlay 2、迷你播放器和全屏模式等功能。该应用使用Swift和SwiftUI开发，音乐文件夹添加后会扫描并存入SQLite数据库，利用SQLite FTS5进行搜索，播放由AVFoundation支持。要求macOS 14或更高版本。

Petrichor
An offline music player for macOS
Summary
✨ Features
Everything you'd expect from an offline music player!
Map your music folders and browse your library in an organized view.
Create playlists and manage the play queue interactively.
Browse music using folder view when needed.
Pin
anything
(almost!) to the sidebar for quick access to your favorite music.
Navigate easily: right-click a track to go to its album, artist, year, etc.
Native macOS integration with menubar and dock playback controls, plus dark mode support.
Search quickly through large libraries containing thousands of songs.
💡
Tip
: Petrichor relies heavily on tracks having good metadata for all its features to work well.
⌛ Planned features
Smart playlists with user-configurable conditional filters
AirPlay 2 casting support
Miniplayer and full-screen modes
Automatic in-app updates
Online album & artist information fetching
... and much more!
 Requirements
macOS 14 or later
⚙️ Installation
Go to
Releases
and download the latest
.dmg
.
Open the
.dmg
and drag the app icon into the Applications folder.
In Applications, right-click
Petrichor > Open
.
P.S. I plan publish it on Homebrew soon.
📷 Screenshots
🏗️ Development
Motivation
I have a large collection of music files that I’ve gathered over the years, and I missed having a good offline
music player on macOS. I used
Swinsian
(great app, by the way!), but it hasn't been
updated in years. I also missed features commonly found in streaming apps; so I built Petrichor to scratch that
itch and learn Swift and macOS app development along the way!
Implementation Overview
Built entirely with Swift and SwiftUI for the best macOS integration.
Once folders are added, the app scans them and populates a SQLite database using
GRDB
.
Petrichor does
not
alter your music files, it only reads from the directories you add.
Tracks searching is powered by
SQLite FTS5
with fall-back to in-memory search.
Playback is powered by
AVFoundation
.

data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了CPU性能和分支指令在程序决策中的作用。程序通常按照顺序执行模型运行，即每个指令依次执行，除非遇到改变控制流的分支指令。分支指令根据条件是否满足来决定是否跳转到目标指令，分为无条件分支和条件分支。无条件分支总是执行跳转，常见于函数调用和返回等场景；条件分支则根据特定条件决定是否跳转，常见于if语句和循环比较。某些CPU使用标志寄存器来判断条件，而其他则通过比较寄存器或内存值来决定分支是否执行。文章还提到，编译器在无法预判条件时会使用条件分支。这是Pointer Wars挑战的一部分，旨在帮助开发者编写高效的C/C++代码。

44481627.article_content:
Branch instructions are the primary means by which a program running on a CPU makes a decision.
This post is part of a series of posts on CPU performance, as part of the Pointer Wars: Linked List Edition challenge. This challenge is great for undergraduates, graduate students, and new engineers who want feedback about writing high performance C or C++ code.
Much more info here.
The Sequential Execution Model and Branch Instructions
Programs written to execute on a CPU follow something called the sequential execution model. Sequential execution means that each CPU instruction is executed one at a time, and unless specified otherwise, the next instruction to execute is at a memory location directly after the current instruction. Do note that the sequential execution model refers to the semantics that the CPU must follow, not their actual implementations, as implementations violate this rule in ways the programmer isn’t aware of all the time.
Instructions that might change the control flow of a program (control flow being the path the program takes through the code) are called branches or jumps, depending on the instruction set of the CPU. There are also dedicated call and return instructions to support function calls and those that are used to implement privileged or debug execution, such as system calls. For the purposes of this blog post, I’m generally going to refer to all of those instructions as “branches”.
Branches ultimately have a target, which is an instruction to which they may branch to if some condition is met. When they redirect the CPU to that target instruction, the branch is said to be “taken”. That’s true even in the case when the target instruction is the next sequential address (note that this is an odd corner case that likely never exists in “real code”). When a branch instruction is not taken, it’s called “not taken”. Relatively straightforward terminology.
Conditional versus Unconditional Branches
One classification of branches is whether they are conditional or unconditional. An unconditional branch is one that is always taken, by definition. Unconditional branches tend to show up when the compiler absolutely can’t avoid them, often because the target of the branch cannot be placed sequentially in memory following the instruction that proceeds it, for whatever reason (a real reason, or a compiler heuristic telling it not to). That tends to occur with function calls and returns, goto statements, switch statements, tail call recursive function implementations, and unoptimized C loop implementations (for instance C semantics are such that the condition of a while loop is evaluated first, and then the loop body is executed, repeat). There are likely others, compilers emit some beautifully optimized code, but those in my mind are the common cases.
Conditional branches on the other hand are only taken if a particular condition is met, otherwise they “fall through” to the next sequential instruction. The condition to be met is specified by the assembly language instruction. There tend to be two classes of specifying conditions, where an instruction set tends to gravitate towards one or the other:
Whether certain CPU flags are set.
Certain CPU implementations have a flags register, a special purpose register which is populated by the ALU or other instructions indicating certain conditions have occurred. The four common conditions are Zero (Z), Carry (C), Negative (N), and signed carry (V), and a combination of these flags can be used to determine equality, overflow, and inequality (less than/greater than). These instruction sets often rely on an explicit compare instruction to update the flags (although the result of many other ALU instructions can update the flags as well) and may have specific instructions whose sole purpose is to set or clear individual flags.
Comparison between two registers or other data.
Other CPU implementations compare two register values, or a register and an immediate value, or a register and a value in a memory location, or even a memory value and an immediate value. An immediate value is a constant that is directly encoded in the instruction, or inferred by the instruction of the branch (eg, compare register against zero). Based on the comparison that the branch instruction performs, and the criteria specified by the instruction (eg, equal, greater than), the branch is either taken or not taken. Some instruction sets have helper instructions, such as the MIPS SLT (Set Less Than), which are used in conjunction with equality testing to implement certain branch conditions across multiple instructions.
Conditional branches show up when the program has to make a choice, and the compiler can’t deduce at compile time that the choice remains unchanged throughout the lifetime of the program, or even if it can, cannot deduce the value of that condition. When you think of conditional branches, you should think of if statements and loop comparisons.

data.title: HyAB k-means for color quantization
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在CIELAB色彩空间中进行颜色量化，并使用了一种名为"HyAB"的距离公式来优化聚类效果，以提高图像质量。传统上，颜色距离通过RGB空间的欧几里得距离计算，但这种方法在感知上并不均匀。CIELAB空间通过表示亮度（L*）和色度（a*, b*）来更好地匹配人眼感知，但直接使用欧几里得距离在大色差和某些蓝色调上表现不佳。

文章介绍了一种来自2019年论文的"CD1"公式（称为HyAB），结合了亮度的绝对差值和色度的欧几里得距离，以更准确地反映人眼对颜色差异的感知。作者将此公式应用于k-means聚类算法，在CIELAB空间中进行颜色量化，并与传统方法进行了对比。结果显示，HyAB方法在保持颜色准确性上表现更好，特别是在处理大色差时。此外，通过调整亮度权重，可以进一步优化图像细节。

总体而言，HyAB公式提供了一种更直观且有效的颜色距离计算方法，适用于颜色量化和图像压缩。

44514946.article_content:
30fps.net
— Computer Graphics & Programming with Pekka Väänänen
Color quantization in CIELAB space, visualized. The input is converted to CIELAB space and a special “HyAB” distance formula is used when clustering. This in theory should result in better image quality.
I’ve been obsessing over color quantization algorithms lately, and when I learned that an image conversion app called
Composite
did its so-called pixel mapping step in CIELAB space, I instantly thought of the “HyAB” color distance formula I’d seen in the
FLIP error metric paper
from 2020.
By “pixel mapping” I mean choosing for each pixel the closest color in a fixed palette.
This results in a compressed version of the original image.
The closest color is the one with the shortest Euclidean distance, computed in 3D for the RGB coordinates.
Unfortunately it’s not perceptually uniform, so two colors with a small computed color difference might actually look very different to the human eye.
Computing color differences in sRGB space is surprisingly decent but there are better options.
The CIELAB aka L*a*b* space represents colors as their perceived brightness component
L
, the “luminance”, and two components
a
and
b
that encode a “chrominance” coordinate in a 2D (red-green, blue-yellow) plane.
Notably the
L
component is still gamma corrected here but with gamma=3 instead of 2.2 like in sRGB.
Given two colors
(L^*_1, a^*_1, b^*_1)
and
(L^*_2, a^*_2, b^*_2)
in the CIELAB color space, it’s simple to compute their difference, again, by their Euclidean distance:
\text{Euclidean} = \sqrt{(L^*_1 - L^*_2)^2 + (a^*_1 - a^*_2)^2 + (b^*_1 - b^*_2)^2}
This is also known as
the “CIE 1976” formula
and apparently the reason CIELAB’s existence.
Unfortunately it breaks down in large differences and also fails in some shades of blue.
Wikipedia lists three later, increasingly complex, supposedly better-behaved formulas from years 1984, 1994, and 2001.
But what if there’s a simpler fix?
Now we get to the point.
In a 2019 paper
Distance metrics for very large color differences
, Saeedeh Abasi and colleagues suggest the following “CD1” formula large color distances:
\text{CD1} = |L^*_1 - L^*_2| + \sqrt{(a^*_1 - a^*_2)^2 + (b^*_1 - b^*_2)^2}
So now we take an absolute difference in lightness and an Euclidean distance in chromaticities.
It’s a hybrid of a
“city block”
and Euclidean distance of
(a,b)
, so they called this space “HyAB”.
I’ll just call the CD1 formula above with that name for simplicity.
In the paper, they justify this choice with “psychological separability” between lightness and the two other color dimensions, hue and chroma.
1
They ran an experiment with 17 participants and its results suggest HyAB is more faithful to large observed color differences than an Euclidean distance or the
CIEDE2000
formula from 2001.
I’m convinced!
Time to try it in practice.
k-means in CIELAB space
I’ll apply the new distance formula to a color quantization problem.
Given an 24-bit image, find a palette of
K
colors the represent the image well, and then reconstruct the image using only the palette colors alone.
This can be considered a clustering problem with a known number of centers, so we can directly apply k-means to it.
Recall the two alternating steps of k-means: assigning each point to the closest cluster, and computing new cluster centers as averages of their assigned points.
The first step is usually the Euclidean distance but let’s change that to HyAB instead and see what happens.
To be clear, running k-means in CIELAB is nothing new.
For example Google’s
material-color-utilities project does it
.
The HyAB distance formula in it is the novelty here.
Below a quick comparison of 16-color paletted versions between an input image,
Pillow
’s
quantize()
,
libimagequant
, and my implementation (
GitHub
,
local copy
) of modified k-means in CIELAB space with the HyAB formula plugged in.
Image
Description
The original image
“hats” by Don Cochran
, downscaled to 384x256.
Pillow’s median cut
with
kmeans=3
. Note how the green and magenta hats have lost their color, and the red hats cap has no shading.
libimagequant
with
max_quality=100
. Shading is better but the green has become olive and magenta still looks red.
HyAB k-means
. While the green hat still isn’t perfect, its tone is closer to the original. The magenta cap has now its correct hue. As a downside, the red hat now has a visible halo.
It really seems to work!
But is this better than doing k-means directly in sRGB or CIELAB space with the Euclidean distance?
Comparison to sRGB and pure CIELAB
Perhaps the most useful thing about the HyAB formulation is how it affords a clear way to control luminance-vs-color error.
In the distance function we can multiply
|L^*_1 - L^*_2|
by say, two, without introducing wrong hues.
Consider the examples below.
The non-weighted version is on the left, exaggarated luminance distance on the right.
HyAB k-means
HyAB k-means with 2x L-channel weight
Slightly more definition in the green hat,

• refulgentis推荐使用Celebi的K-Means，加权平方均值方法。他指出，这种方法将来自Wu量化器的结果输入到K-Means中，从而提供确定性的初始集群和结果，并利用CIELAB距离来避免大量计算。他认为这种方法在需要更高集群计数的情况下表现出色。

补充讨论：
• mattdesl提供了有关其测试的参考链接，并讨论了不同色彩空间及其在色彩量化中的应用。[1][2][3]
• refulgentis的方法强调了计算效率和结果的确定性，特别适用于需要高集群计数的场景，例如Material 3的动态色彩。

• 争议焦点可能在于哪种方法更具普遍适用性和效率。mattdesl强调了灵活性和可调性，而refulgentis则强调了方法的确定性和计算效率。

data.title: White Noise – secure and private messenger
data.author: onhacker
data.article_summary: White Noise是一款注重隐私和安全的消息应用，采用端对端加密，支持前向保密和妥协后安全，确保即使密钥泄露，消息仍能保密。它不依赖电话号码或电子邮件，允许匿名通信，并支持跨平台使用。应用基于开放标准如Nostr和MLS协议，具备去中心化特性，不受单一实体控制，抗审查。独立节点运行确保网络不受干扰。White Noise快速、可靠且可扩展，支持从个人到大规模群组的通信。作为非营利、社区驱动的项目，它不受公司或政府控制，所有代码开源，用户可以免费使用并能在多设备上运行。

  - globalnode进一步讨论了去中心化和P2P消息传递的挑战，认为必须确保安全的操作系统以及去信任的第三方，并提出了一些如通过DNS或Tor中继进行安全通信的设想。

• **法律与安全性**：

  - skeptrune调侃Nostr再度流行。
  - journal评论对安全和隐私条款表示质疑，指出开发者声明不对隐私问题负责。

- 讨论中涉及多个技术概念，如元数据隐私、去中心化网络、消息协议的并发问题等，反映了用户对隐私保护和消息安全的深层次关注。
- 政府监管与法律问题也是用户关注的重要方面，尤其是在隐私保护和法律执行之间的矛盾。

A truly secure and private messenger thatâs lightning fast, infinitely scalable, and identity-free.

Supported By
Privacy & Security
White Noise secures conversations using strong cryptography, enforced by end-to-end encryption. With forward secrecy and post-compromise security, even if keys are exposed, your past and future messages stay hidden.
Identity Freedom
Communicate without needing phone numbers or emails. Choose anonymity, a pseudonym, or your real name. Your identity, your rules.
Open & Decentralized
Built on open standards like Nostr and the Messaging Layer Security (MLS) protocol, White Noise lets you take your identity, data, and contacts across platforms. Switch apps anytime without losing connections.
Distributed & Unscensorable
No single entity controls the network. Thousands of independent nodes worldwide ensure censorship resistance. Run your own relay in minutes, no corporate servers needed.
Fast, Reliable, & Scalable
Engineered for real-time performance, White Noise handles direct messages to massive groups seamlessly. Built for speed, designed for reliability.
Non-Profit & Community-Driven
White Noise is a non-profit, community-driven project. We are not funded by any corporation, and we are not beholden to any government or organization. We are a group of volunteers who are passionate about privacy and security.

data.title: Ask HN: How is the tech scene in LA?
data.author: asdev
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：洛杉矶（LA）作为科技从业者的工作和生活地点的优缺点

不同观点：
• mylaaccount：认为洛杉矶的科技从业者相较于湾区不那么追求职业发展，他们更多是为了生活方式而选择住在洛杉矶，并且通过工作来支持这种生活方式。尽管有人抱怨洛杉矶，但对他来说，这里是最好的居住地，只要能赚足够的钱并能忍受驾驶，洛杉矶有无尽的娱乐活动和充满激情的人。

• achillesheels：指出在洛杉矶很难结交朋友，因为这是一个高度流动性的城市，很多人没有长期定居的打算。洛杉矶的科技从业者相较于湾区或纽约雄心不足。然而，洛杉矶的天气无可挑剔，食物文化丰富多彩，有机会偶遇创意行业的专业人士，并且洛杉矶国际机场（LAX）交通便利。

• dgunay：认为洛杉矶没有那么大的纯软件创业场景，他的大部分职业生涯都在当地国防工业或为其他州的创业公司远程工作。总体上，他不喜欢住在洛杉矶，觉得这是美国管理最不善的城市之一，但由于社会原因无法轻易离开。

• lamroger：在洛杉矶生活了两年，并有十年前在洛杉矶上大学的经历。他认为洛杉矶的创业公司有趣，尤其是在大数据和广告技术兴起时。尽管疫情后感到一些兴奋，但洛杉矶的创业聚会往往是同一小群人。

• VirusNewbie：指出大多数大公司（如FAANG）在洛杉矶有办公室，但这些办公室往往难以到达且价格昂贵。相比之下，橙县（Orange County）的生活成本较低，交通不那么拥堵，是一个更好的居住选择。

• 999900000999：认为洛杉矶房租高，公共交通不可靠，人们不友好，不推荐任何人来洛杉矶。超长的通勤时间（单程一小时以上）很常见。

• superconduct123：指出洛杉矶拥有最多的游戏工作室，对于游戏行业的从业者来说可能是一个不错的选择。

补充讨论：
• 洛杉矶的生活方式和天气被普遍认为是优点，尤其是对于那些重视生活质量和娱乐活动的人。
• 洛杉矶的交通和通勤问题被多次提及，尤其是高房租和长通勤时间是主要抱怨点。
• 橙县被一些评论者认为是一个更好的居住和工作的选择，因为生活成本较低，交通不那么拥堵。
• 洛杉矶的科技从业者被认为相较于其他科技中心（如湾区和纽约）雄心不足，但也有评论者认为这是洛杉矶的独特魅力之一。

争议焦点：
• 洛杉矶是否适合长期居住和工作：一些人认为洛杉矶生活质量高，是理想居住地；另一些人则抱怨交通、房租和通勤问题，不推荐洛杉矶作为科技从业者的工作地。

data.title: Would You Like an IDOR With That? Leaking 64m McDonald's Job Applications
data.author: samwcurry
data.article_summary: 本文描述了研究人员在麦当劳招聘聊天机器人平台McHire中发现的安全漏洞。该平台由Paradox.ai开发，使用Olivia机器人收集求职者的个人信息和偏好。研究人员通过简单默认凭证（123456:123456）登录系统，并发现一个不安全的直接对象引用（IDOR）漏洞，可访问超过6400万求职者的个人数据，包括姓名、联系方式、申请状态和聊天记录。研究人员立即向Paradox.ai和麦当劳披露了该漏洞，随后漏洞被迅速修复。Paradox.ai也表示保护候选人和客户数据是其首要任务，并承诺进行进一步审查以防止类似问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个安全事件及相关测试的讨论，包括人格测试、安全漏洞、以及企业应对。

不同观点：
• [ryandrake] 认为人格测试体验令人不安，猜测这种测试只是让申请者在合适的时候选择对雇主有利的答案，类似于一种CAPTCHA，实际价值有限。
• [david2ndaccount] 关注安全问题，指出在发现安全漏洞后无法找到合适的披露联系人，最终只能随机发送邮件，并批评Paradox.ai的安全页面过于简单，缺乏实质性指导。
• [bravesoul2] 澄清该安全漏洞并非由AI引发，而是由于对象ID枚举问题，且漏洞发现过程是通过使用简单密码（123456）测试实现的。
• [bombcar] 批评麦当劳对安全漏洞的反应比许多互联网公司更为迟缓，表达了对企业应对速度的失望。
• [ge96] 提到自己曾遇到类似的申请过程，涉及到行为问题（如选择杀1个人还是5个人），暗示有些招聘问题设计不合理。
• [Titan2189] 赞扬Paradox在报告漏洞后30小时内就进行了修复，认为反应速度值得肯定。
• [snypher] 对使用简单密码（123456）成功进入系统表示好奇，暗示可能有更深的故事未被揭示。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于人格测试的实际价值和其是否仅仅是一种让申请者"学会说谎"的工具。
• 安全漏洞的发现和披露过程中的困难也被重点讨论，尤其是缺乏公开的披露联系方式。
• 对麦当劳及其他公司在应对安全漏洞方面的反应速度存在不同看法，有人批评，也有人赞扬特定公司的快速反应。
• 行为问题和密码安全性成为讨论中的次要话题，展示了招聘过程中的其他潜在问题。

44513940.article_content:
Would you like an IDOR with that? Leaking 64 million McDonald’s job applications
Introduction
McHire
is the chatbot recruitment platform used by
90%
of McDonald’s franchisees. Prospective employees chat with a bot named Olivia, created by a company called
Paradox.ai
, that collects their personal information, shift preferences, and administers personality tests. We noticed this after seeing complaints on Reddit of the bot
responding with nonsensical answers
.
During a cursory security review of a few hours, we identified two serious issues: the McHire administration interface for restaurant owners accepted the default credentials
123456:123456
, and an insecure direct object reference (IDOR) on an internal API allowed us to access any contacts and chats we wanted. Together they allowed us and anyone else with a McHire account and access to any inbox to retrieve the personal data of more than 64 million applicants.
Applying for a job
We started by applying for a job at our local McDonald’s. McHire has a consumer-facing site at
https://jobs.mchire.com/
where it is easy to find available postings near you. We were immediately sent to Olivia, who helped us fill in our email and phone number along with what shifts we can work, and we were instantly moved to the next stage: the personality test!
McHire personality test
The personality test was a disturbing experience powered by
Traitify.com
where we were asked if phrases like “enjoys overtime” are either
Me
or
Not Me
. It was simple to guess that we should probably select
Me
for the pro-employer questions and
Not Me
for questions referencing being argumentative or aggressive, but it was still quite strange.
Unfortunately, after this, we were stuck without any further progress and appeared to be awaiting human review. We tried to prompt inject the Olivia chatbot, which likely ruined our chance at a human approving us, but it seemed to be locked to a list of pre-set responses or something similar, and there were no interesting APIs for the candidates.
Logging in
We noticed that restaurant owners can login to view applicants at
https://www.mchire.com/signin
. Although the app tries to force SSO for McDonald’s, there is a smaller link for “Paradox team members” that caught our eye.
Without much thought, we entered “123456” as the username and “123456” as the password and were surprised to see we were immediately logged in!
McHire user administration
It turned out we had become the administrator of a test restaurant inside the McHire system. We could see all of the employees of the restaurant were simply employees of Paradox.ai, the company behind McHire. This was great because we could now see how the app worked, but annoying because we had still not demonstrated any actual confidentiality or integrity impact.
Applying for our job
We decided to apply to one of the test job postings the account had set up already and see what it looked like on the other side. The restaurant can view all of the in-progress conversations with “Olivia” and then intervene when they hit certain stages like having completed the personality test.
Restaurant’s view of our conversation application
While viewing our test conversations, we noticed an interesting API to fetch the candidate information
PUT /api/lead/cem-xhr
, which seems to be a reference to proxying to some kind of Customer or Candidate Experience Manager (CEM) via an XHR request. The main parameter of this request was the
lead_id
of the chat, which for our test applicant was about
64,185,742
. We tried decrementing this number, and were immediately faced with PII from another McDonald’s applicant (including “unmasked” contact data)!
We quickly realized this API allows us to access every chat interaction that has ever applied for a job at McDonald’s. The information returned included:
Name, email address, phone number, address
Candidacy state and every state change/form input the candidate had submitted (shifts they could work, etc)
Auth token to log into the consumer UI as that user, leaking their raw chat messages and presumably other information
We immediately began disclosure of this issue once we realized the potential impact. Unfortunately, no disclosure contacts were publicly available and we had to resort to emailing random people. The
Paradox.ai security page
just says that we do not have to worry about security!
After our outreach reached the appropriate people, the
Paradox.ai
team engaged with us, emphasized that safeguarding candidate and client data was their top priority, promptly remediated the vulnerability, and committed to further reviews to identify and close any remaining avenues of exploitation.
Disclosure
We disclosed this issue to
Paradox.ai
and McDonald’s at the same time.

data.title: Making Explainable Minesweeper
data.author: greentec
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了经典游戏《扫雷》中存在的50/50猜测局面以及如何通过逻辑推理避免纯粹靠运气的情况。作者玩了一款包含14种扫雷变体的游戏，并对其提供的提示功能产生了兴趣。文章解释了扫雷中的数字如何表示周围地雷的数量，并指出某些局面下玩家可能误以为需要靠运气猜测，而实际上通过逻辑推理可以确定地雷的位置。

文章还介绍了如何通过算法生成完全可推理的扫雷地图。首先随机生成地雷分布，然后通过模拟玩家的解谜过程筛选出仅靠推理可解的地图。在生成过程中，优先选择可揭示更多周边格子的起始点，并通过逻辑规则逐步验证地图的可解性。作者最终决定开发一款通过自然语言解释提示的扫雷游戏，以帮助玩家更好地理解并解决扫雷中的难题。

此外，文章总结了游戏中所使用的逻辑推理规则，确保地图生成完全依赖推理而非运气。
